title.zh: 卷九 志第一 禮上
title.raw: 卷九 志第一 禮上 Volume 9 Treatises 1: Rituals 1

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷九‧志第一

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, volume nine, treatise one
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, volume 9, treatise 1

sentences.zh: 禮儀繁博，與天地而爲量，紀國立君，人倫攸始。

translations.literal: Rites and ceremonies are vast and manifold, measured against Heaven and Earth; they record founding a state and installing a lord—the beginning of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is broad and deep, commensurate with Heaven and Earth; it grounds the state and the ruler and marks where human order begins.

sentences.zh: 三代遺文，略在經誥，蓋秦餘所亡逸也。

translations.literal: Surviving writings of the Three Dynasties lie chiefly in the classics and royal pronouncements; what was lost was mostly in the wreckage left by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: What the Three Dynasties left survives mainly in the classics and edicts; most of what vanished did so in the Qin destruction.

sentences.zh: 漢初叔孫通制漢禮，而班固之志不載。

translations.literal: Early in Han, Shusun Tong devised Han ritual, but Ban Gu's treatise does not record it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Han, Shusun Tong framed Han court ritual, yet Ban Gu's monograph omits it.

sentences.zh: 及至東京，太尉胡廣撰《舊儀》，左中郎蔡邕造《獨斷》，應劭、蔡質咸綴識時事，而司馬彪之書不取。

translations.literal: When it reached the Eastern Capital, Grand Marshal Hu Guang compiled Old Rites; Left Palace Attendant Cai Yong wrote Exclusive Decisions; Ying Shao and Cai Zhi both added notes on current affairs—yet Sima Biao's book does not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Han, Hu Guang as grand marshal compiled Old Rites and Cai Yong as left palace attendant wrote Exclusive Decisions; Ying Shao and Cai Zhi annotated recent practice too, but Sima Biao's history leaves them out.

sentences.zh: 魏氏籍漢末大亂，舊章殄滅，侍中王粲、尚書衞覬集創朝儀，而魚豢、王沈、陳壽、孫盛竝未詳也。

translations.literal: Wei, drawing on the great disorder at Han's end, saw old statutes perish; Palace Attendant Wang Can and Minister of the Masters Wei Ji gathered and created court ritual—yet Yu Huan, Wang Shen, Chen Shou, and Sun Sheng together give no detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wei arose amid Han's final chaos, when old regulations were wiped out; Wang Can and Wei Ji compiled new court rites, but Yu Huan, Wang Shen, Chen Shou, and Sun Sheng say little about them.

sentences.zh: 吳則太史令丁孚拾遺漢事，蜀則孟光、許慈草建衆典。

translations.literal: Wu had Grand Clerk Ding Fu recover lost Han matters; Shu had Meng Guang and Xu Ci draft the mass of statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, grand clerk Ding Fu salvaged Han precedents; in Shu, Meng Guang and Xu Ci drafted the major codes.

sentences.zh: 晉初司空荀覬因魏代前事，撰爲《晉禮》，參考今古，更其節文，羊祜、任愷、庾峻、應貞竝共刪集，成百六十五篇。

translations.literal: Early Jin: Minister of Works Xun Yi, following Wei's prior affairs, compiled them as Jin Rites, consulting past and present and revising the rubrics; Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, and Ying Zhen together edited and collected them into one hundred sixty-five chapters.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin, minister of works Xun Yi drew on Wei precedents to produce Jin Rites, comparing old and new usage and revising the rubrics; Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, and Ying Zhen jointly edited the work into 165 chapters.

sentences.zh: 後摯虞、傅咸纘續此製，未及成功，中原覆沒，今虞之《決疑注》，是遺事也。

translations.literal: Later Zhi Yu and Fu Xian continued this project but did not finish; the central plains fell, and today Yu's Doubt-Resolving Commentary is what remains of the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Fu Xian later carried the project on but never finished; the heartland was lost, and Zhi Yu's Doubt-Resolving Commentary is all that survives.

sentences.zh: 江左僕射刁協、太常荀崧，補緝舊文，光祿大夫蔡謨又踵修輯朝故。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze: Vice Director Diao Xie and Chamberlain for Ceremonials Xun Song patched old texts; Grand Master of Splendor Cai Mo again followed in compiling court precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the south, vice director Diao Xie and chamberlain for ceremonials Xun Song restored old texts, and grand master of splendor Cai Mo in turn compiled court precedent.

sentences.zh: 宋初因循改革，事係羣儒，其前史所詳，竝不重述。

translations.literal: Early Song followed and reformed; the matter involved many scholars—what earlier histories already treat in detail is not repeated here.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song carried on with reform under a circle of scholars; what earlier histories already cover is not retold.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表定禮樂。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2, crown prince's infantry commandant Fu Manrong memorialized to fix ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2, crown prince's infantry commandant Fu Manrong petitioned to settle ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 於是詔尚書令王儉制定新禮，立治禮樂學士及職局，置舊學四人，新學六人，正書令史各一人，幹一人，祕書省差能書弟子二人。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Minister of the Masters Wang Jian to fix new ritual, establish officers and a bureau for governing ritual and music, appoint four scholars of the old learning and six of the new, one chief clerk and one recorder each, one clerk, and two skilled calligraphers from the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered minister of the masters Wang Jian to draft new ritual, set up a ritual-and-music office with staff, four scholars in the old learning and six in the new, one chief clerk and one recorder apiece, one clerk, and two skilled copyists from the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 因集前代，撰治五禮，吉、凶、賔、軍、嘉也。

translations.literal: Gathering former ages, they compiled the five rites—auspicious, inauspicious, guest, military, and celebratory.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on earlier dynasties, they compiled the five rites: auspicious, inauspicious, guest, military, and celebratory.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is mostly not recorded in the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Most of that material is not recorded in the annals and is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 若郊廟庠序之儀，冠婚喪紀之節，事有變革，宜錄時事者，備今志。

translations.literal: As for suburban, temple, and school rites, and the norms of capping, marriage, and mourning—where practice changed and current affairs should be recorded—they are set out in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban, temple, and school rites and the rules for capping, marriage, and mourning—where usage changed and the times ought to be noted—are covered in this treatise.

sentences.zh: 其輿輅旗常，與往代同異者，更立別篇。

translations.literal: Carriages, regalia, banners, and constants that differ from past ages are given a separate section.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages, regalia, banners, and court insignia that differ from earlier ages appear in a separate chapter.

sentences.zh: 案《禮記王制》，天子先祫後時祭，諸侯先時祭後祫。

translations.literal: According to Royal Regulations in the Book of Rites, the Son of Heaven performs cha before seasonal sacrifices; feudal lords perform seasonal sacrifices before cha.
translations.idiomatic: Royal Regulations in the Book of Rites has the Son of Heaven perform cha before seasonal sacrifices, and feudal lords the reverse.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》魯僖二年祫，明年春禘，自此以後，五年再殷。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records a cha in Lu in Duke Xi's second year and a di the next spring; thereafter twice every five years came the great service.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records a cha for Lu in Duke Xi year 2 and a di the following spring; after that the great service came twice in five years.

sentences.zh: 《禮緯稽命徵》曰「三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites Wei, Investigating Mandates, says 「Every three years a cha, every five years a di.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites apocrypha Investigating Mandates says 「A cha every three years, a di every five years.

sentences.zh: 」經、記所論禘祫與時祭，其言詳矣，初不以先殷後郊爲嫌。

translations.literal: 」The classics and commentaries discuss di, cha, and seasonal sacrifices in detail; they never fault performing the great service before the suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: 」Classics and commentaries treat di, cha, and seasonal sacrifices at length and never treat holding the great service before the suburban rite as improper.

sentences.zh: 至於郊配之重，事由王迹，是故杜林議云「漢業特起，不因緣堯，宜以高帝配天」。

translations.literal: As for the weight of suburban accompaniment, it follows the trace of royal achievement; therefore Du Lin's proposal said 「Han rose on its own, not inheriting from Yao; the High Emperor should accompany Heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: The weight of who accompanies Heaven at the suburban altar follows a dynasty's founding story; Du Lin argued that 「Han rose by itself, not from Yao's line, so the High Emperor should accompany Heaven.」

sentences.zh: 魏高堂隆議以舜配天。

translations.literal: Under Wei, Gao Tanglong's proposal used Shun to accompany Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Gao Tanglong proposed Shun as Heaven's companion at the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟云「漢時奏議，謂堯已禪舜，不得爲漢祖，舜亦已禪禹，不得爲魏之祖。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji said 「Han memorial debates held that Yao had already ceded to Shun and could not be Han's ancestor, and Shun had already ceded to Yu and could not be Wei's ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji said 「Han court debate held that Yao had already yielded to Shun and could not be Han's forebear, and Shun had yielded to Yu and could not be Wei's forebear.

sentences.zh: 今宜以武皇帝配天」。

translations.literal: Now the Martial Emperor should accompany Heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor should now accompany Heaven.」

sentences.zh: 晉、宋因循，卽爲前式。

translations.literal: Jin and Song followed precedent, and it became the former model.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Song followed that precedent, and it became the established pattern.

sentences.zh: 又案禮及《孝經援神契》竝云「明堂有五室，天子每月於其室聽朔布教，祭五帝之神，配以有功德之君」。

translations.literal: Examining ritual texts and the Classic of Filial Piety, Divine Correspondence, both say 「The Bright Hall has five chambers; the Son of Heaven each month in its chamber hears the new moon and spreads instruction, sacrifices to the gods of the Five Emperors, with meritorious lords as companions.」
translations.idiomatic: Ritual texts and the Classic of Filial Piety apocrypha Divine Correspondence both say 「The Bright Hall has five chambers; each month the Son of Heaven in one chamber hears the new moon, proclaims policy, sacrifices to the Five Emperors' spirits, and pairs them with meritorious rulers.」

sentences.zh: 《大戴禮記》曰「明堂者，所以明諸侯尊卑也」。

translations.literal: The Records of the Elder Dai say 「The Bright Hall is for clarifying the precedence of feudal lords.」
translations.idiomatic: The Elder Dai's ritual compilation says 「The Bright Hall makes clear the rank of the feudal lords.」

sentences.zh: 許慎《五經異義》曰「布政之宮，故稱明堂。

translations.literal: Xu Shen's Discordant Meaning of the Five Classics says 「The palace for spreading governance, hence called Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen's Discordant Meaning of the Five Classics says 「It is the hall where policy is proclaimed, hence Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 明堂，盛貌也」。

translations.literal: Bright Hall means splendid appearance.」
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall means a splendid aspect.」

sentences.zh: 《周官匠人職》稱明堂有五室。

translations.literal: The Craftsman's Office in the Offices of Zhou states that the Bright Hall has five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou, Craftsman's section, says the Bright Hall has five chambers.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云「周人明堂五室，帝一室也」。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said 「The Zhou Bright Hall had five chambers; the Sovereign had one chamber.」
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said 「The Zhou Bright Hall had five chambers—the Sovereign's was one of them.」

sentences.zh: 初不聞有文王之寢。

translations.literal: One never hears of a dormitory for King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Nowhere is a sleeping chamber for King Wen mentioned.

sentences.zh: 《鄭志》趙商問云「說者謂天子廟制如明堂，是爲明堂卽文廟邪」？

translations.literal: In Zheng's Notes, Zhao Shang asked, 「Expositors say the Son of Heaven's temple system is like the Bright Hall—is the Bright Hall then the temple of King Wen?」
translations.idiomatic: In Zheng's Notes, Zhao Shang asked, 「Some say the Son of Heaven's ancestral temple follows the Bright Hall model—is the Bright Hall King Wen's temple?」

sentences.zh: 鄭荅曰「明堂主祭上帝，以文王配耳，猶如郊天以后稷配也」。

translations.literal: Zheng answered, 「The Bright Hall chiefly sacrifices to the Supreme God, with King Wen as companion only, just as at suburban Heaven sacrifice Hou Ji is companion.」
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, 「The Bright Hall chiefly worships the Supreme God, with King Wen paired only as companion—as at the suburban Heaven rite Hou Ji is paired with Heaven.」

sentences.zh: 袁孝尼云「明堂法天之宮，本祭天帝，而以文王配，配其父於天位則可，牽天帝而就人鬼，則非義也」。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiaoni said 「The Bright Hall is the palace patterned on Heaven; it originally sacrifices to the Heavenly Sovereign, yet uses King Wen as companion—matching one's father to Heaven's seat is permissible; dragging the Heavenly Sovereign down to human ghosts is not right.」
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiaoni said 「The Bright Hall mirrors Heaven's palace and was meant to worship the Heavenly Sovereign; pairing King Wen is fitting his father to Heaven's place, but pulling the Heavenly Sovereign down among human spirits is wrong.」

sentences.zh: 泰元十三年，孫耆之議，稱「郊以祀天，故配之以后稷；

translations.literal: Taiyuan year 13, Sun Qizhi's proposal stated 「The suburban rite sacrifices to Heaven, so Hou Ji accompanies it;
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 13, Sun Qizhi argued 「The suburban altar worships Heaven, so Hou Ji is paired there;

sentences.zh: 明堂以祀帝，故配之以文王。

translations.literal: the Bright Hall sacrifices to the Sovereign, so King Wen accompanies it.
translations.idiomatic: the Bright Hall worships the Sovereign, so King Wen is paired there.

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，郊爲皇天之位，明堂卽上帝之廟」。

translations.literal: From this wording, the suburban rite is the seat of August Heaven; the Bright Hall is the temple of the Supreme God.」
translations.idiomatic: On that logic the suburban altar is August Heaven's seat and the Bright Hall is the Supreme God's temple.」

sentences.zh: 徐邈謂「配之爲言，必有神主；

translations.literal: Xu Miao said 「Companion in speech necessarily implies a spirit tablet;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao said 「To pair is to imply a spirit tablet;

sentences.zh: 郊爲天壇，則堂非文廟」。

translations.literal: the suburban rite is Heaven's altar, so the Hall is not King Wen's temple.」
translations.idiomatic: the suburban altar is Heaven's mound, so the Hall is not King Wen's temple.」

sentences.zh: 《史記》云趙綰、王臧欲立明堂，于時亦未有郊配。

translations.literal: The Records of the Historian says Zhao Fen and Wang Zang wished to establish the Bright Hall; at the time there was also no suburban accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Historian says Zhao Fen and Wang Zang wanted to build the Bright Hall when suburban pairing had not yet been settled.

sentences.zh: 漢又祀汾陰五畤，卽是五帝之祭，亦未有郊配。

translations.literal: Han also sacrificed at Fenyin to the five altars—that was sacrifice to the Five Emperors, and again there was no suburban accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: Han also offered at Fenyin on the five mounds—a rite to the Five Emperors—with no suburban pairing either.

sentences.zh: 議者或謂南郊之日，已旅上帝，若又以無配而特祀明堂，則一日再祭，於義爲黷。

translations.literal: Some debaters said that on the day of the southern suburban rite, having already assembled the Supreme God, if one again specially sacrificed at the Bright Hall without accompaniment, it would be two sacrifices in one day—in ritual terms, excess.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that on the southern suburban day, once the Supreme God had been assembled, a separate Bright Hall service without its own pairing would mean two sacrifices in one day—ritually excessive.

sentences.zh: 案古者郊本不共日。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity, suburban rites were originally not on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, suburban rites were not held on the same day.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕《獨斷》曰「祠南郊，祀畢，次北郊，又次明堂、高廟、世祖廟，謂之五供」。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's Exclusive Decisions says 「Sacrifice at the southern suburb; when the sacrifice is complete, next the northern suburb, then next the Bright Hall, High Temple, and Founder Temple—called the five offerings.」
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's Exclusive Decisions says 「Offer at the southern suburb; when that is done, the northern suburb; then the Bright Hall, High Temple, and Founder Temple—in all, the five offerings.」

sentences.zh: 馬融云「郊天之祀，咸以夏正，五氣用事，有休有王，各以其時，兆於方郊，四時合歲，功作相成，亦以此月總旅明堂」。

translations.literal: Ma Rong said 「Sacrifice to Heaven at the suburb, all use the first month of summer; the five qi govern, with rest and with ascendancy, each in its season, divination at the directional suburb; the four seasons complete the year, achievements and labors completing one another—also in this month the Bright Hall is assembled in full.」
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong said 「Suburban Heaven sacrifice always falls in the first summer month, when the five phases hold sway in turn; each season has its directional suburban divination; the four seasons complete the year and its labors—and in that same month the Bright Hall rite is gathered in full.」

sentences.zh: 是則南郊、明堂各日之證也。

translations.literal: This is proof that the southern suburb and Bright Hall were on separate days.
translations.idiomatic: That shows the southern suburb and Bright Hall were on different days.

sentences.zh: 近代從省，故與郊同日，猶無煩黷之疑。

translations.literal: Recent ages have followed economy, so they are held on the same day as the suburb; still there is no worry of excess.
translations.idiomatic: Later practice economized and combined them with the suburban day, yet that need not count as excess.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 其爲祭雖同，所以致祭則異。

translations.literal: Though the sacrifice is the same, the means of performing it differ.
translations.idiomatic: The rite may look the same on the surface, but what is actually being offered is not.

sentences.zh: 孔晁云，言五帝佐天化育，故有從祀之禮，旅上帝是也。

translations.literal: Kong Chao said: The text means the Five Thearchs assist Heaven in nurturing creation, hence the rite of attendant sacrifice—presenting the congregation to the Supreme Lord is that.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chao explained that the Five Thearchs help Heaven nurture the world, which is why there is attendant sacrifice—"assembling the Supreme Lord" means exactly that.

sentences.zh: 至於四郊明堂，則是本祀之所，譬猶功臣從饗，豈復廢其私廟。

translations.literal: As for the suburban altars of the four directions and the Bright Hall, these are places of primary sacrifice—like meritorious ministers sharing at a feast; how could one abolish their private temples?
translations.idiomatic: The four suburban altars and the Bright Hall are where the main sacrifices belong—like meritorious ministers feasting at court. Would anyone abolish their own ancestral shrines?

sentences.zh: 且明堂有配之時，南郊亦旅上帝，此則不疑於共日，今何故致嫌於同辰。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Bright Hall had a collateral spirit, the southern suburb also assembled the Supreme Lord—then no one doubted holding them on the same day; why now scruple at the same time?
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall had a matched spirit, the southern suburb still assembled the Supreme Lord on the same day—and no one called that improper. Why object now to the same occasion?

sentences.zh: 又《禮記》「天子祭天地、四方、山川、五祀，歲徧」。

translations.literal: Further, the Record of Rites: "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the four directions, mountains and rivers, and the five sacrifices—each year in full."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites also says: "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the four quarters, mountains and rivers, and the five sacrifices—each year without omission."

sentences.zh: 《尚書堯典》「咸秩無文」。

translations.literal: The Canon of Yao in the Documents: "All ranks are complete; nothing is omitted."
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Yao in the Documents: "Every rank is in order; nothing is left out."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云「昭事上帝，聿懷多福」。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Brightly serve the Lord on High, and you will harbour many blessings."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Serve the Lord on High with clarity, and many blessings will gather to you."

sentences.zh: 據此諸義，則四方、山川，猶必享祀，五帝大神，義不可略。

translations.literal: According to these several meanings, the four directions and mountains and rivers must still receive sacrifice; the great lords among the Five Thearchs in right cannot be passed over.
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds, even the four quarters and mountains and rivers must be honoured—and the great spirits of the Five Thearchs cannot rightly be slighted.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年正月，郊天地明堂，明帝太和元年正月，以武皇帝配天，文皇帝配上帝，然則黃初中南郊明堂，皆無配也。

translations.literal: In the first month of Huangchu 2, Emperor Wen of Wei sacrificed at the suburban altars to Heaven and Earth and the Bright Hall; in the first month of Taihe 1, Emperor Ming matched Emperor Wu with Heaven and Emperor Wen with the Supreme Lord—thus in the Huangchu years both southern suburb and Bright Hall had no collateral spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2, first month, Emperor Wen of Wei sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs and the Bright Hall; in Taihe 1, first month, Emperor Ming matched Cao Cao with Heaven and Cao Pi with the Supreme Lord—so under Huangchu neither the southern suburb nor the Bright Hall had a matched spirit.

sentences.zh: 又郊日及牲色，異議紛然。

translations.literal: Further, on the day of suburb sacrifice and the colour of victims, disputing voices were many.
translations.idiomatic: On the suburban date and the colour of the victims, opinions were sharply divided.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》云「郊之用辛，周之始郊也」。

translations.literal: Records of Suburban Sacrifice says: "The suburb uses xin—Zhou's first suburb sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Records of Suburban Sacrifice says: "Suburban sacrifice uses a xin day—Zhou's first suburban rite did so."

sentences.zh: 盧植云「辛之爲言自新絜也」。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi said: "Xin in meaning is renewing purity."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said: "Xin means to renew oneself in purity."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云「用辛日者，爲人當齋戒自新絜也」。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Using a xin day is because people should fast and renew purity."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "A xin day is chosen so that people may fast and make themselves pure again."

sentences.zh: 漢魏以來，或丁或己，而用辛常多。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward, sometimes ding or ji days were used, but xin was most common.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, some used ding or ji days, but xin days were used most often.

sentences.zh: 考之典據，辛日爲允。

translations.literal: Examining canonical authority, a xin day is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against the classics, a xin day is the sound choice.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》又云，郊牲幣宜以正色。

translations.literal: Records of Suburban Sacrifice also says: suburban victims and silks should use the correct colours.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Suburban Sacrifice also says suburban victims and silks should use the orthodox colours.

sentences.zh: 繆襲據《祭法》，云天地騂犢，周家所尚，魏以建丑爲正，牲宜尚白。

translations.literal: Miao Xi, citing Regulations of Sacrifice, said Heaven and Earth take red bulls—Zhou honoured this; Wei took the yin month as year-start, so victims should favour white.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Xi, citing Regulations of Sacrifice, argued that Heaven and Earth receive red bulls, as Zhou preferred; Wei took the yin month as New Year, so victims should be white.

sentences.zh: 《白虎通》云，三王祭天，一用夏正，所以然者，夏正得天之數也。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall says: the three dynasties in sacrificing to Heaven all used the Xia calendar—because the Xia calendar obtains Heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall says the three dynasties all sacrificed to Heaven by the Xia calendar, for the Xia calendar holds Heaven's reckoning.

sentences.zh: 魏用異朔，故牲色不同。

translations.literal: Wei used a different new-year, hence victim colour differed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei kept a different New Year, and so the colour of victims differed too.

sentences.zh: 今大齊受命，建寅創曆，郊廟用牲，一依晉、宋。

translations.literal: Now Great Qi has received the mandate, established the yin month as year-start and created the calendar; suburb and temple victims follow Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Great Qi has received the mandate, set the yin month as New Year, and promulgated a calendar, suburban and temple victims should follow Jin and Song.

sentences.zh: 謂宜以今年十月殷祀宗廟。

translations.literal: It is fitting to hold the grand Yin temple sacrifice this year in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: The grand Yin-style ancestral rite should be held in the tenth month of this year.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，五年再殷。

translations.literal: From this onward, every five years hold the grand sacrifice again.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the grand rite should be held once every five years.

sentences.zh: 來年正月上辛，有事南郊。

translations.literal: Next year, first month, first xin day: perform the southern suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, on the first xin day of the first month, hold the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 宜以共日，還祭明堂。

translations.literal: On the same day one should return to sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On that same day, sacrifice at the Bright Hall as well.

sentences.zh: 又用次辛，饗祀北郊。

translations.literal: On the next xin day, feast-sacrifice at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the following xin day, hold the feast-sacrifice at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 而竝無配。

translations.literal: Yet with no collateral spirit in either case.
translations.idiomatic: In both cases, without a matched spirit.

sentences.zh: 犧牲之色，率由舊章。

translations.literal: The colour of victims should follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The colour of the victims should follow established precedent.

sentences.zh: 詔「可。

translations.literal: Edict: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 明堂可更詳」。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall may be reconsidered in detail."
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall may be examined further."

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「明堂尋禮無明文，唯以《孝經》爲正。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized again: "In searching the rites, the Bright Hall has no explicit text; only the Classic of Filial Piety is taken as authoritative.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized again: "The rites give no explicit rule for the Bright Hall; only the Classic of Filial Piety is taken as the standard.

sentences.zh: 竊尋設祀之意，蓋爲文主有配則祭，無配則止。

translations.literal: I humbly trace the intent of establishing sacrifice: broadly, when King Wen has a collateral spirit there is sacrifice; without a collateral spirit it stops.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the intent behind the rite, it seems sacrifice at the Bright Hall was meant for when King Wen had a matched spirit; without a match, it ceased.

sentences.zh: 愚謂旣配上帝，則以帝爲主。

translations.literal: I deem that once one has matched the Supreme Lord, the Lord on High is taken as chief.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once the Supreme Lord has a matched spirit, the Lord on High is treated as the principal.

sentences.zh: 今雖無配，不應闕祀。

translations.literal: Though now there is no collateral spirit, sacrifice should not be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Even without a matched spirit now, the sacrifice should not be dropped.

sentences.zh: 徐邈近代碩儒，每所折衷，其云『郊爲天壇，則堂非文廟』，此實明據。

translations.literal: Xu Miao, a great scholar of recent times, whenever he weighed matters, said: 'The suburb is the altar of Heaven—then the Hall is not King Wen's temple'—this is clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, a leading scholar of recent times, always ruled that "the suburb is Heaven's altar, so the Hall is not King Wen's temple"—and that is decisive evidence.

sentences.zh: 內外百司立議已定，如更詢訪，終無異說。

translations.literal: Within and without, the hundred offices have set their debate and it is settled; if one asks further, in the end there will be no differing view.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court the hundred offices have already settled the debate; further consultation would change nothing.

sentences.zh: 傍儒依史，竭其管見。

translations.literal: Secondary scholars follow the histories and exhaust their narrow sight.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser scholars mine the histories and offer only what little they can see.

sentences.zh: 旣聖旨惟疑，羣下所未敢詳，廢置之宜，仰由天鑒。

translations.literal: Since the sacred intent alone is uncertain—what the assembled ministers dare not elaborate—the propriety of abolishing or retaining rests on Heaven's discernment."
translations.idiomatic: Because Your Majesty alone remains in doubt—what your ministers dare not decide for themselves—whether to keep or abolish the rite must be left to Heaven's judgment."

sentences.zh: 」詔「依舊」。

translations.literal: " Edict: "As before."
translations.idiomatic: " Edict: "Let it stand as before."

sentences.zh: 建元四年，世祖卽位。

translations.literal: Jianyuan 4, Shizu took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 4: Shizu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 其秋，有司奏：「尋前代嗣位，或仍前郊年，或別更始，晉、宋以來，未有畫一。

translations.literal: That autumn, the relevant offices memorialized: "Reviewing how former dynasties on succeeding to the throne either kept the former suburb year or changed it anew—from Jin and Song onward there has been no single rule.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the relevant offices memorialized: "Former dynasties on accession either kept the old suburban year or began a new one—from Jin and Song onward there has been no fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 今年正月已郊，未審明年應南北二郊祀明堂與不？

translations.literal: This year the first-month suburb has already been performed; we do not know whether next year the southern and northern suburban sacrifices and Bright Hall should be performed or not?"
translations.idiomatic: This year's first-month suburban sacrifice is already done; should the southern and northern suburbs and the Bright Hall be held next year or not?"

sentences.zh: 」依舊通關八座丞郎博士議。

translations.literal: Follow former precedent and circulate for joint deliberation among the Eight Seats, aides, academicians, and erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Follow former practice and circulate the question for joint deliberation by the Eight Seats, aides, gentlemen, and erudites.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉議：「案秦爲諸侯，雜祀諸畤，始皇幷天下，未有定祠。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian argued: "Examination shows Qin as a feudal lord mixed sacrifices at various altars; when the First Emperor united the realm, fixed sacrifices were not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian argued: "Qin, while still a feudal state, offered mixed sacrifices at many altars; when the First Emperor united the realm, no fixed cult had yet been set.

sentences.zh: 漢高受命，因雍四畤而起北畤，始祠五帝，未定郊丘。

translations.literal: When Han Gao received the mandate, from Yong's four altars he raised the northern altar and first sacrificed to the Five Thearchs, but suburban mound altars were not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gao received the mandate, he built on Yong's four altars to raise the northern altar and first sacrificed to the Five Thearchs, but the suburban mound altars were not yet fixed.

sentences.zh: 文帝六年，新垣平議初起渭陽五帝廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Emperor Wen, Xinyuan Ping's proposal first raised the Five Thearchs temple at Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen's sixth year, Xinyuan Ping's proposal first established the Five Thearchs temple at Weinan.

sentences.zh: 武帝初至雍郊見五畤，後常三歲一郊祠雍。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Wu's reign he went to Yong for suburb sacrifice and saw the five altars; afterward he regularly every three years offered suburb sacrifice at Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wu's reign he went to Yong for suburban sacrifice and saw the five altars; thereafter he regularly sacrificed at Yong every three years.

sentences.zh: 元鼎四年，始立后土祠於汾陰，明年，立太一祠於甘泉，自是以後，二歲一郊，與雍更祠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanding the altar to Earth was first established at Fenyin; the next year the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan—from then on suburb every two years, alternating with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding 4: the altar to Earth was first established at Fenyin; the next year, the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan. From then on suburban sacrifice came every two years, alternating with Yong.

sentences.zh: 成帝初卽位，丞相匡衡於長安定南北郊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng first took the throne, Chancellor Kuang Heng established southern and northern suburbs at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng first took the throne, Chancellor Kuang Heng established the southern and northern suburbs at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 哀、平之際，又復甘泉、汾陰祠。

translations.literal: At the time of Ai and Ping, Ganquan and Fenyin altars were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ai and Ping, sacrifice at Ganquan and Fenyin was restored.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始五年，王莽奏依匡衡議，還復長安南北郊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping, Wang Mang memorialized following Kuang Heng's proposal and restored southern and northern suburbs at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi 5 of Emperor Ping: Wang Mang memorialized adopting Kuang Heng's plan and restored the southern and northern suburbs at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 光武建武二年，定郊祀兆於洛陽。

translations.literal: In Jianwu year 2 of Guangwu, the suburban sacrifice sites were fixed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangwu's Jianwu 2, the suburban cult sites were established at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉因循，率由漢典，雖時或參差，而類多閒歲。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin followed in succession, generally by Han precedent; though timing sometimes varied, for the most part many years were years of rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin largely followed Han precedent; dates sometimes slipped, but for the most part suburban sacrifice came only in off-years.

sentences.zh: 至於嗣位之君，參差不一。

translations.literal: As for succession emperors, the variation was not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: When a new emperor took the throne, practice was not uniform.

sentences.zh: 宜有定制。

translations.literal: There should be a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: A fixed rule was needed.

sentences.zh: 檢晉明帝太寧三年南郊，其年九月崩，成帝卽位，明年改元卽郊；

translations.literal: Examination shows Emperor Ming of Jin in Taining 3 performed southern suburb sacrifice; in the ninth month of that year he died, Emperor Cheng took the throne, and the next year, at the change of era, he performed suburb sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Check Jin Mingdi, Taining 3: southern suburb that year; he died in the ninth month; Chengdi succeeded and performed suburb sacrifice the next year at the era change;

sentences.zh: 簡文咸安二年南郊，其年七月崩，孝武卽位，明年改元亦郊；

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen in Xian'an 2 performed southern suburb sacrifice; in the seventh month of that year he died, Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, and the next year, at the change of era, he also performed suburb sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen, Xian'an 2: southern suburb; he died in the seventh month; Xiaowu succeeded and sacrificed at the suburbs the next year at the era change;

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉三十年正月南郊，其年二月崩，孝武嗣位，明年改元亦郊。

translations.literal: In the first month of Yuanjia 30 of Song, southern suburb sacrifice; in the second month of that year the emperor died, Xiaowu succeeded, and the next year, at the change of era, he also performed suburb sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Yuanjia 30, first month: southern suburb; the emperor died in the second month; Xiaowu succeeded and held suburb sacrifice the next year at the era change.

sentences.zh: 此則二代明例，差可依放。

translations.literal: These are clear precedents across two dynasties and may be followed in rough measure.
translations.idiomatic: These are clear two-dynasty precedents and may be followed in substance.

sentences.zh: 謂明年正月宜饗祀二郊，虔祭明堂，自茲厥後，依舊閒歲。

translations.literal: It is proposed that in the first month of next year both suburbs should be feasted and the Bright Hall reverently sacrificed to, and from then on, as before, off-years.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal: next year's first month should feast both suburbs and reverently sacrifice at the Bright Hall; thereafter, as before, off-years only.

sentences.zh: 」尚書領國子祭酒張緒等十七人竝同儉議。

translations.literal: 」Seventeen persons including Zhang Xu, director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent libationer of the Imperial University, all agreed with Jian's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: 」Seventeen officials, including Zhang Xu—director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent libationer of the Imperial University—all sided with Jian.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 永明元年當南郊，而立春在郊後，世祖欲遷郊。

translations.literal: Yongming year 1 was due for southern suburb sacrifice, but Establishment of Spring fell after the suburb; the Shizu emperor wished to move the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 1 called for southern suburb sacrifice, but Establishment of Spring fell after the rite; Emperor Shizu wanted to move the date.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉啓：「案《禮記郊特牲》云『郊之祭也，迎長日之至也，大報天而主日也』。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian memorialized: 「According to Record of Rites, Suburban Sacrifice: 『The suburb sacrifice welcomes the arrival of the lengthening day; it is the great report to Heaven and makes the sun paramount.』
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian wrote: 「The Record of Rites, Suburban Sacrifice, says: 『Suburban sacrifice welcomes the lengthening day; it is the great report to Heaven and enthrones the sun.』

sentences.zh: 《易說》『三王之郊，一用夏正』。

translations.literal: Explanation of the Changes says 『The three kings' suburb sacrifices all used the Xia calendar's New Year.』
translations.idiomatic: The Explanation of the Changes says: 『The three kings all held suburb sacrifice by the Xia New Year.』

sentences.zh: 盧植云『夏正在冬至後，傳曰啓蟄而郊，此之謂也』。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi said 『The Xia New Year falls after the winter solstice; the tradition says suburb sacrifice at Awakening of Insects—this is what is meant.』
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said: 『The Xia New Year comes after the winter solstice; tradition says suburb at Awakening of Insects—that is the point.』

sentences.zh: 然則圜丘與郊各自行，不相害也。

translations.literal: Thus the Round Mound and the suburb each proceed on their own and do not harm one another.
translations.idiomatic: So the Round Mound and the suburb rite proceed separately and do not conflict.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『建寅之月，晝夜分而日長矣』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said 『In the month of Establishing yin, day and night divide and the day grows long.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: 『In the month Establishing yin, day and night are equal and daylight lengthens.』

sentences.zh: 王肅曰『周以冬祭天於圜丘，以正月又祭天以祈穀』。

translations.literal: Wang Su said 『Zhou sacrificed to Heaven at the Round Mound in winter, and in the first month again sacrificed to Heaven to pray for grain.』
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: 『Zhou sacrificed to Heaven at the Round Mound in winter, and in the first month sacrificed again to Heaven to pray for grain.』

sentences.zh: 《祭法》稱『燔柴太壇』，則圜丘也。

translations.literal: Regulations of Sacrifice says 『Burning firewood on the Great Mound』—that is the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations of Sacrifice speaks of 『burning firewood on the Great Mound』—that is the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 春秋傳云『啓蟄而郊』，則祈穀也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals tradition says 『Suburb sacrifice at Awakening of Insects』—that is praying for grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn tradition says 『suburb at Awakening of Insects』—that is the grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 謹尋禮、傳二文，各有其義，盧、王兩說，有若合符。

translations.literal: Carefully examining the two texts of ritual and tradition, each has its meaning; the two explanations of Lu and Wang fit like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Read against ritual and tradition, each passage has its sense; Lu's and Wang's views align like tally and seal.

sentences.zh: 中朝省二丘以并二郊，卽今之郊禮，義在報天，事兼祈穀，旣不全以祈農，何必俟夫啓蟄。

translations.literal: The central dynasty reduced the two mounds and merged the two suburbs—that is today's suburban rite: its meaning lies in reporting to Heaven, and the affair also includes praying for grain; since it is not wholly for praying to the fields, why must one wait for Awakening of Insects?
translations.idiomatic: The central court folded two mounds into one suburban rite—today's suburb: it reports to Heaven and also prays for grain; since it is not solely a farm prayer, why wait for Awakening of Insects?

sentences.zh: 史官唯見傳義，未達禮旨。

translations.literal: Historians have seen only the tradition's wording and have not grasped the ritual's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Historians have read the tradition's letter without catching the rite's purpose.

sentences.zh: 又尋景平元年正月三日辛丑南郊，其月十一日立春，元嘉十六年正月六日辛未南郊，其月八日立春，此復是近世明例，不以先郊後春爲嫌。

translations.literal: Further, examination shows Jingping year 1, first month, third day xinchou southern suburb; on the eleventh day of that month Establishment of Spring; Yuanjia 16, first month, sixth day xinwei southern suburb, eighth day of that month Establishment of Spring—these again are clear recent precedents, and performing suburb before spring is not held improper.
translations.idiomatic: Again: Jingping 1, first month, day 3 xinchou—southern suburb; day 11—Establishment of Spring. Yuanjia 16, first month, day 6 xinwei—southern suburb; day 8—Establishment of Spring. These too are recent clear cases; suburb before spring drew no objection.

sentences.zh: 若或以元日合朔爲礙者，則晉成帝咸康元年正月一日加元服，二日親祠南郊，元服之重，百僚備列，雖在致齋，行之不疑。

translations.literal: If some take new-year's-day conjunction of new moon as an obstacle, then Jin Emperor Cheng in Xiankang year 1, first month, first day performed the capping ceremony, second day personally sacrificed at southern suburb—the weight of capping, the full array of officials: though within the purification fast, it was performed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone objects that New Year's Day coincides with new moon, Jin Chengdi, Xiankang 1, first month, day 1—capping; day 2—personal southern suburb. Capping outranks all offices; even amid the fast, the court did not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 今齋內合朔，此卽前准。

translations.literal: Today, conjunction within the fast—this is the former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A new moon inside the fast period is already precedent.

sentences.zh: 若聖心過恭，寧在嚴絜，合朔之日，散官備防，非預齋之限者，於止車門外別立幔省，若日色有異，則列於省前，望實爲允，謂無煩遷日。

translations.literal: If the sage heart is overly reverent and prefers strict purity, on the day of conjunction let scattered officials stand guard; those not within the fast limit should set up a separate curtained office outside the Halting Carriage Gate; if the sun's colour is unusual, line up before the office and observe the fact—that is acceptable, and there is no need to move the day.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty prefers utmost purity, on conjunction day let scattered officials keep watch; anyone outside the fast may pitch a separate curtained post beyond the Halting Carriage Gate. If the sun looks wrong, observe from before that post—that suffices; the date need not move.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，祠部郎中蔡履議：「郊與明堂，本宜異日。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2, Palace Attendant of the Sacrificial Bureau Cai Lü argued: 「Suburb and Bright Hall should originally be on different days.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 2: Cai Lü of the Sacrificial Bureau argued: 「Suburb and Bright Hall ought to fall on different days.

sentences.zh: 漢東京《禮儀志》『南郊禮畢，次北郊、明堂、高廟、世祖廟，謂之五供』。

translations.literal: Eastern Han Records of Rites says 『When southern suburb rite is complete, next northern suburb, Bright Hall, High Temple, and Founder's Temple—called the five offerings.』
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han Records of Rites: 『When the southern suburb ends, next the northern suburb, Bright Hall, High Temple, and Founder's Temple—the five offerings.』

sentences.zh: 蔡邕所據亦然。

translations.literal: What Cai Yong relied on is likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's authority says the same.

sentences.zh: 近世存省，故郊堂共日。

translations.literal: Recent times economized, hence suburb and hall on one day.
translations.idiomatic: Recent practice trimmed costs, so suburb and hall shared a day.

sentences.zh: 來年郊祭，宜有定准。」

translations.literal: Next year's suburban sacrifices should have a fixed rule.」
translations.idiomatic: Next year's suburbs need a fixed schedule.」

sentences.zh: 太學博士王祐議：「來年正月上辛，宜祭南郊，次辛，有事明堂，後辛，饗祀北郊。」

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial University Wang You argued: 「Next year, first month, upper xin day should sacrifice at southern suburb; next xin, perform Bright Hall; last xin, feast northern suburb.」
translations.idiomatic: University erudite Wang You: 「Next year, first month: upper xin—southern suburb; next xin—Bright Hall; last xin—northern suburb feast.」

sentences.zh: 兼博士劉蔓議：「漢元鼎五年，以辛巳行事，自後郊日，略無違異。

translations.literal: Concurrent erudite Liu Man argued: 「Han Yuanding 5 used xinsi to perform the rites; thereafter suburban dates show almost no deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent erudite Liu Man: 「Han, Yuanding 5, used xinsi for the rite; after that suburban dates scarcely varied.

sentences.zh: 元封元年四月癸卯，登封泰山，坐明堂。

translations.literal: Yuanshi year 1, fourth month, guimao, ascended Mount Tai in feng, seated in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi 1, fourth month, guimao: feng on Mount Tai, then seated in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年甲子，以高祖配。

translations.literal: Year 5, jiazi, with the High Ancestor as companion.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, jiazi: the High Ancestor as companion spirit.

sentences.zh: 漢家郊祀，非盡天子之縣，故祠祭之月，事有不同。

translations.literal: Han suburban sacrifice did not wholly follow the Son of Heaven's commanderies, hence the months of temple sacrifice differed in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Han suburbs did not always follow the capital calendar, so sacrifice months differed.

sentences.zh: 後漢永平以來，明堂兆於國南，而郊以上丁，故供修三祀，得幷在初月。

translations.literal: From Eastern Han Yongping onward, the Bright Hall site was south of the capital, while suburb used upper ding; thus supplying and repairing the three sacrifices could be joined in the first month.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Han Yongping on, the Bright Hall stood south of the capital while suburb used upper ding; all three rites could be prepared in the first month.

sentences.zh: 雖郊有常日，明堂猶無定辰。

translations.literal: Though suburb has a fixed day, the Bright Hall still has no fixed time.
translations.idiomatic: Suburb has a fixed day; the Bright Hall still has no fixed hour.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 郊丁社甲，有說則從，經禮無文，難以意造，是以必算良辰，而不祭寅丑。

translations.literal: Suburb on ding, soil god on jia—if there is doctrine, follow it; canonical ritual has no text, and one cannot invent by whim; therefore one must calculate the auspicious day and does not sacrifice on yin or chou days.
translations.idiomatic: Suburb on ding, soil god on jia—follow doctrine where it exists; the classics give no warrant for invention, so one must calculate the lucky day and does not sacrifice on yin or chou.

sentences.zh: 且禮之奠祭，無同共者，唯漢以朝日合於報天爾。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ritual there is no joint offering of the same kind; only Han combined the morning sun with reporting to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ritual does not double the same offering on one occasion; only Han merged the morning sun with Heaven's report.

sentences.zh: 若依《漢書》五供，便應先祭北郊，然後明堂。

translations.literal: If one follows the Book of Han's five offerings, one should first sacrifice at northern suburb, then the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the Book of Han's five offerings, northern suburb should come before the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 則是地先天食，所未可也。」

translations.literal: That would be Earth before Heaven in eating the sacrifice—what cannot be done.」
translations.idiomatic: That would feed Earth before Heaven—unthinkable.」

sentences.zh: 兼太常丞蔡仲熊議：「《鄭志》云『正月上辛，祀后稷於南郊，還於明堂，以文王配』。

translations.literal: Concurrent aide of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials Cai Zhongxiong argued: 「Zheng's Notes says 『First month, upper xin: sacrifice to Hou Ji at southern suburb, return and at the Bright Hall pair King Wen.』
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent aide Cai Zhongxiong: 「Zheng's Notes: 『First month, upper xin: Hou Ji at southern suburb; return to the Bright Hall with King Wen paired.』

sentences.zh: 故宋氏創立明堂，郊還卽祭，是用《鄭志》之說也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Song house, establishing the Bright Hall, sacrificed upon return from suburb—that follows Zheng's Notes.
translations.idiomatic: So Song, founding the Bright Hall, sacrificed right after suburb—that follows Zheng's Notes.

sentences.zh: 蓋爲《志》者失，非玄意也。

translations.literal: Likely the author of the Notes erred; it is not Zheng's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Likely the Notes' compiler slipped; that is not Zheng's meaning.

sentences.zh: 玄之言曰『未審周明堂以何月，於月令則以季秋』。

translations.literal: Zheng's words say 『It is not clear in which month Zhou's Bright Hall [was used]; in Monthly Ordinances it is the last autumn month.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng wrote: 『Which month Zhou used the Bright Hall is unclear; the Monthly Ordinances place it in late autumn.』

sentences.zh: 案玄注《月令》季秋大饗帝云『大饗，徧祭五帝』。

translations.literal: Examination shows Zheng's commentary on Monthly Ordinances, last autumn's great feast to the Thearch, says 『Great feast: offering to all Five Thearchs.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's gloss on Monthly Ordinances, late autumn's great feast to the Thearch: 『Great feast—sacrifice to all Five Thearchs.』

sentences.zh: 又云『大饗於明堂，以文武配』。

translations.literal: Again it says: "The great feast is at the Bright Hall, with Wen and Wu as matches."
translations.idiomatic: He also says: "The great feast is held at the Bright Hall, with King Wen and King Wu as matched spirits."

sentences.zh: 其時秋也，去啓蟄遠矣。

translations.literal: The season was autumn—far from Excited Insects.
translations.idiomatic: That season was autumn, long past Excited Insects.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮大司樂》『凡大祭祀，宿縣』。

translations.literal: Again, the Offices of Zhou, Grand Director of Music: "For all great sacrifices, suspend the bells overnight."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou, Grand Director of Music, also says: "For every great sacrifice, suspend the bells overnight."

sentences.zh: 尋宿縣之旨，以日出行事故也；

translations.literal: Tracing the point of suspending the bells overnight, it is because affairs are conducted by daylight;
translations.idiomatic: The point of suspending the bells overnight is that the rite is carried out by daylight;

sentences.zh: 若日闇而後行事，則無假預縣。

translations.literal: if one waits until dark to act, there is no need to suspend them beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: if the rite waited until nightfall, there would be no call to set them up in advance.

sentences.zh: 果日出行事，何得方俟郊還。

translations.literal: If affairs truly proceed by daylight, how could one wait only until the suburb sacrifice returns?
translations.idiomatic: If the rite truly runs by daylight, how could one still wait until the suburban sacrifice is finished?

sentences.zh: 東京《禮儀志》不記祭之時日，而《志》云『天郊夕牲之夜，夜漏未盡八刻進熟；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital Rites Protocols does not record the calendar date of the sacrifice, but the Protocols say: "On the night of preparing victims for the Heavenly suburb, before the night clepsydra has run eight units, the cooked offering is presented;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital Rites Protocols does not give the calendar date of the sacrifice, yet they say: "On the night victims are prepared for the Heavenly suburb, the cooked offering is presented before the night clepsydra has run eight units;

sentences.zh: 明堂夕牲之夜，夜漏未盡七刻進熟』。

translations.literal: on the Bright Hall night of preparing victims, before the night clepsydra has run seven units, the cooked offering is presented."
translations.idiomatic: on the Bright Hall night of preparing victims, it is presented before the night clepsydra has run seven units."

sentences.zh: 尋明堂之在郊前一刻，而進獻奏樂，方待郊還。

translations.literal: Tracing this, the Bright Hall rite was one unit before the suburb in presenting offerings and sounding music—yet still waiting for the suburb to return.
translations.idiomatic: Read closely, the Bright Hall was one clepsydra unit ahead of the suburb in presenting offerings and sounding music—yet still waiting on the suburb to finish.

sentences.zh: 魏高堂隆表「九日南郊，十日北郊，十一日明堂，十二日宗廟』。

translations.literal: Wei: Gao Tanglong's memorial: "On the ninth day the southern suburb, the tenth the northern suburb, the eleventh the Bright Hall, the twelfth the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Gao Tanglong memorialized: "The ninth day, southern suburb; the tenth, northern suburb; the eleventh, Bright Hall; the twelfth, ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 案隆此言，是審于時定制，是則《周禮》二漢及魏，皆不共日矣。

translations.literal: Examining Long's words, they reflect the fixed practice of the time; thus the Rites of Zhou, the two Han, and Wei did not share days.
translations.idiomatic: Long's schedule matches the settled practice of the age—under the Rites of Zhou, both Han, and Wei, the rites were not held on one day.

sentences.zh: 《禮》以辛郊，書以丁祀，辛丁皆合，宜臨時詳擇。」

translations.literal: The Rites use xin for suburb, the Documents use ding for sacrifice—both xin and ding are acceptable; the date should be chosen in detail at the time."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites take xin for suburb and the Documents take ding for sacrifice; either xin or ding will serve, and the court should choose the day with care when the time comes."

sentences.zh: 太尉從事中郎顧憲之議：「《春秋傳》以正月上辛郊祀，《禮記》亦云郊之用辛，尚書獨云丁巳用牲于郊。

translations.literal: Attendant to the Grand Commander Gu Xianzhi argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals takes the first xin of the first month for suburban sacrifice; the Record of Rites also says suburb uses xin; only the Documents say on dingsi victims were used at the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xianzhi, attendant to the grand commander, argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals fixes suburban sacrifice on the first xin of the first month; the Record of Rites likewise says the suburb uses xin; only the Documents record dingsi as the day victims were presented at the suburb.

sentences.zh: 先儒以爲先甲三日辛，後甲三日丁，可以接事天神之日。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars held that the three days before jia is xin and the three days after jia is ding can connect the days for serving Heaven and the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that the three days before jia are xin and the three days after jia are ding—days fit to receive Heaven and the spirits in succession.

sentences.zh: 後漢永平二年正月辛未，宗祀光武皇帝於明堂。

translations.literal: In Later Han Yongping 2, first month, xinwei day, they performed the ancestral rite to Emperor Guangwu at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 2 of Later Han, on xinwei day in the first month, Emperor Guangwu was honored in ancestral rite at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛旣是常郊之日，郊又在明堂之前，無容不郊而堂，則理應郊堂。」

translations.literal: Since xin was the usual suburban day and the suburb preceded the Bright Hall, one cannot sacrifice at the Hall without the suburb—thus suburb and Hall on the same principle are fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Xin was the usual suburban day, and the suburb came before the Bright Hall; there is no room for the Hall without the suburb—so suburb and Hall on the same day is the sound reading."

sentences.zh: 司徒西閤祭酒梁王議：「《孝經》鄭玄注云『上帝亦天別名』。

translations.literal: Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Minister of Works Liang Wang argued: "The Classic of Filial Piety, Zheng Xuan's commentary, says 'The Supreme Lord is also another name for Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wang, libationer of the Western Pavilion of the minister of works, argued: "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety says, 'The Supreme Lord is only another name for Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 如鄭旨，帝與天亦言不殊。

translations.literal: By Zheng's intent, "Lord" and "Heaven" are not distinguished in speech.
translations.idiomatic: On Zheng's reading, Lord and Heaven are not spoken of as different.

sentences.zh: 近代同辰，良亦有據。

translations.literal: Recent ages holding them on the same occasion also has solid grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Holding suburb and Hall on the same occasion in recent times also has solid grounds.

sentences.zh: 魏太和元年正月丁未，郊祀武皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝於明堂以配上帝，此則已行之前准。」

translations.literal: Wei Taihe 1, first month, dingwei day: suburb sacrifice to match Emperor Wu with Heaven, ancestral rite to Emperor Wen at the Bright Hall to match the Supreme Lord—this is established precedent already in practice."
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Taihe 1, first month, dingwei day: at the suburb Emperor Wu was matched with Heaven, and at the Bright Hall Emperor Wen was honored to match the Supreme Lord—precedent already in force."

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍江淹議：「郊旅上天，堂祀五帝，非爲一日再黷之謂，無俟釐革。」

translations.literal: Valiant Cavalry General Jiang Yan argued: "The suburb presents the journey to Heaven; the Hall sacrifices to the Five Thearchs—this is not called doubly impious in one day; there is no need for reform."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, valiant-cavalry general, argued: "The suburb presents the journey to Heaven; the Hall sacrifices to the Five Thearchs—this is not the sort of doubled impiety that must be reformed in a single day."

sentences.zh: 尚書陸澄議：「遺文餘事，存乎舊書，郊宗地近，勢可共日。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Cheng argued: "Surviving texts and ancillary matters are preserved in old books; the suburban altars and Earth-altar are near in place, and by circumstances can share a day.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng, director of the masters of writing, argued: "What survives of the rites is preserved in old books; the suburban altars and the Earth-altar lie close together, and by circumstance they may share a day.

sentences.zh: 不共者，義在必異也。

translations.literal: When they do not share a day, the principle requires them to differ.
translations.idiomatic: When they do not share a day, the principle itself demands that they differ.

sentences.zh: 元始五年正月六日辛未，郊高皇帝以配天，二十二日丁亥，宗祀孝文於明堂配上帝。

translations.literal: Yuanshi 5, first month, 6th day xinwei: suburb to match Gao with Heaven; 22nd day dinghai: ancestral rite to Xiaowen at Bright Hall with Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi 5, first month, sixth day xinwei: suburb sacrifice matching Emperor Gao with Heaven; twenty-second day dinghai: ancestral rite to Emperor Xiaowen at the Bright Hall with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 永平二年正月辛未，宗祀五帝於明堂，光武皇帝配。

translations.literal: Yongping 2, first month xinwei: ancestral rite to Five Thearchs at Bright Hall, Emperor Guangwu matched.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping 2, first month, xinwei: ancestral rite to the Five Thearchs at the Bright Hall, with Emperor Guangwu as match.

sentences.zh: 章帝元和二年，巡狩岱宗，柴祭，翌日，祠五帝於明堂。

translations.literal: Zhangdi Yuanhe 2: tour to Mount Tai, faggot sacrifice; next day, sacrifice to Five Thearchs at Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 2 of Emperor Zhang: a tour to Mount Tai and a faggot sacrifice; the next day, sacrifice to the Five Thearchs at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 柴山祠地，尚不共日，郊堂宜異，於例益明。

translations.literal: Faggot sacrifice on the mountain to Earth still did not share a day—suburb and Hall should differ; the precedents are clearer still.
translations.idiomatic: Even the faggot sacrifice on the mountain to Earth was not held the same day—suburb and Hall should differ all the more; the precedents could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 陳忠《奏事》云『延光三年正月十三日南郊，十四日北郊，十五日明堂，十六日宗廟，十七日世祖廟』。

translations.literal: Chen Zhong's Memorial Matters says: "Yanguang 3, first month, 13th southern suburb, 14th northern suburb, 15th Bright Hall, 16th ancestral temple, 17th Founder temple."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhong's Memorial Matters records: "Yanguang 3, first month: thirteenth day, southern suburb; fourteenth, northern suburb; fifteenth, Bright Hall; sixteenth, ancestral temple; seventeenth, Founder's temple."

sentences.zh: 仲遠五祀，紹統五供，與忠此奏，皆爲相符。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's five sacrifices and Shaotong's five offerings likewise match this memorial of Chen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's five sacrifices and Shaotong's five offerings all accord with this memorial of Chen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆表，二郊及明堂宗廟各一日，摯虞《新禮》議明堂南郊閒三兆，禋天饗帝共日之證也。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong's memorial: southern and northern suburbs and Bright Hall and ancestral temple each on separate days; Zhi Yu's New Rites on the three altars between Bright Hall and southern suburb is evidence that honoring Heaven and feasting the Lord were not held on one day.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong set the two suburbs, Bright Hall, and ancestral temple each on its own day; Zhi Yu's New Rites, in placing three altars between the Bright Hall and the southern suburb, shows that the journey to Heaven and the feast to the Lord were not combined on one day.

sentences.zh: 又上帝非天，昔人言之已詳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Supreme Lord is not Heaven; former writers have explained this at length.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Supreme Lord is not Heaven—earlier writers have already explained that at length.

sentences.zh: 今明堂用日，宜依古在北郊後。

translations.literal: For the Bright Hall date now, one should follow antiquity and place it after the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: For the Bright Hall date now, antiquity should be followed: it belongs after the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 漢唯南郊備大駕，自北郊以下，車駕十省其二，今祠明堂，不應大駕。」

translations.literal: Han only equipped the full progress for the southern suburb; from the northern suburb down, the carriage escort was reduced by two tenths; for the Bright Hall now, the full progress should not be used."
translations.idiomatic: In Han only the southern suburb received the full imperial progress; from the northern suburb onward the escort was cut by two tenths; the Bright Hall today should not receive the full progress."

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉議：「前漢各日，後漢亦不共辰，魏、晉故事，不辨同異，宋立明堂，唯據自郊徂宮之義，未達祀天旅帝之旨。

translations.literal: Director Wang Jian argued: "Former Han used separate days; Later Han also did not share the occasion; Wei and Jin precedents do not distinguish same and different; Song in establishing the Bright Hall relied only on the meaning of returning from suburb to the hall, and did not grasp the intent of sacrificing to Heaven and presenting the journey to the Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, director of the masters of writing, argued: "Former Han kept separate days; Later Han likewise did not share the occasion; Wei and Jin precedents blur same and different; when Song established the Bright Hall it relied only on returning from suburb to palace, and missed the point of sacrificing to Heaven and presenting the journey to the Lord.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 郊壇旅天，甫自詰朝，還祀明堂，便在日昃，雖致祭有由，而煩黷斯甚，異日之議，於理爲弘。

translations.literal: The suburban altar presents the journey to Heaven—having only just finished at dawn, to return and sacrifice at the Bright Hall lands the rite in the slanting sun; though sacrifice has its reasons, the wearisome doubling is extreme; the proposal of separate days is more ample in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban altar presents the journey to Heaven; scarcely has dawn broken when one returns to sacrifice at the Bright Hall, and the rite falls in the slanting afternoon sun. There may be grounds for offering sacrifice, but the wearisome doubling is extreme; separate days are the broader and sounder course.

sentences.zh: 《春秋感精符》云『王者父天母地』。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Essence and Spirit Talisman, says: "The king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Essence and Spirit Talisman, says: "The king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother."

sentences.zh: 則北郊之祀，應在明堂之先。

translations.literal: Thus the northern suburb sacrifice should come before the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The northern suburb sacrifice should therefore come before the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏北郊，亦皆親奉，晉泰寧有詔，未及遵遂。

translations.literal: Han and Wei northern suburbs were also attended in person; Jin had an edict in Taining but it was not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han and Wei the northern suburb was also attended in person; Jin issued an edict in Taining, but it had not yet been carried out.

sentences.zh: 咸和八年，甫得營繕，太常顧和秉議親奉。

translations.literal: Xianhe 8: the sites were first constructed; Minister of Ceremonials Gu He took charge of the proposal for personal attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe 8 the altars were first built; Gu He, minister of ceremonials, pressed the proposal that the ruler attend in person.

sentences.zh: 康皇之世，已經遵用。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Kang, it was already followed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Kang it was already put into practice.

sentences.zh: 宋氏因循，未遑釐革。

translations.literal: Song followed precedent without reforming.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed old practice and never found occasion to reform.

sentences.zh: 今宜親祠北郊，明年正月上辛祠昊天，次辛瘞后土，後辛祀明堂，御竝親奉。

translations.literal: Now the emperor should personally sacrifice at the northern suburb; next year, first xin of first month sacrifice to August Heaven; next xin bury offerings to Earth; following xin sacrifice at Bright Hall—the ruler attending all in person.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ruler should sacrifice in person at the northern suburb; next year, on the first xin of the first month sacrifice to August Heaven; on the next xin bury offerings to Earth; on the following xin sacrifice at the Bright Hall—the sovereign attending every rite in person.

sentences.zh: 車服之儀，率遵漢制。

translations.literal: Carriage and regalia should follow Han regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage and regalia should follow Han practice throughout.

sentences.zh: 南郊大駕，北郊明堂降爲法駕。

translations.literal: Full imperial progress for southern suburb; northern suburb and Bright Hall reduced to regulated progress.
translations.idiomatic: The full progress for the southern suburb; the northern suburb and Bright Hall reduced to regulated progress.

sentences.zh: 袞冕之服，諸祠咸用。

translations.literal: Dragon robes for all the sacrifices alike.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon robes should be worn for every sacrifice alike.

translations.literal: " Edict: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " Edict: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 建武二年，通直散騎常侍庾曇隆啓：「伏見南郊壇員兆外內，永明中起瓦屋，形製宏壯。

translations.literal: Jianwu 2: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Tanlong memorialized: "I observe that within and without the round altar of the southern suburb, in Yongming a tiled building was raised—its form grand and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 2: Yu Tanlong, regular attendant-in-ordinary, memorialized: "I observe that within and without the round altar of the southern suburb a tiled hall was raised in Yongming—grand and imposing in form.

sentences.zh: 檢案經史，無所准據。

translations.literal: Searching the classics and histories, there is no authority for it.
translations.idiomatic: I have searched the classics and histories and found no authority for it.

sentences.zh: 尋《周禮》，祭天於圜丘，取其因高之義，兆於南郊，就陽位也。

translations.literal: Tracing the Offices of Zhou: sacrifice to Heaven at the round mound takes the meaning of following height; the altar at the southern suburb takes the yang position.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou, traced to their intent, sacrifice to Heaven at the round mound because height is followed; the altar at the southern suburb takes the yang position.

sentences.zh: 故以高敞，貴在上昭天明，旁流氣物。

translations.literal: Therefore (the site) is high and open, prized for being above to display Heaven's brightness and to spread qi and creatures to the sides.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the altar stands high and open: above, to show Heaven's light; around, to let breath and beings flow outward.

sentences.zh: 自秦、漢以來，雖郊祀參差，而壇域中閒，竝無更立宮室。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han, although suburban sacrifices varied, within the altar precincts none ever additionally erected palace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, suburban rites differed in detail, yet within the mound precincts no dynasty added palace halls.

sentences.zh: 其意何也？

translations.literal: What is the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: What did they mean by that restraint?

sentences.zh: 政是質誠尊天，不自崇樹，兼事通曠，必務開遠。

translations.literal: It is simply sincerity and reverence for Heaven, not self-glorifying construction, and also serving openness and breadth, necessarily striving for distant vistas.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to honor Heaven in plain sincerity, not to glorify themselves in timber and tile, and to keep the ground open and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉南郊，至時權作小陳帳以爲退息，泰始薄加脩廣，永明初彌漸高麗，往年工匠遂啓立瓦屋。

translations.literal: At the Yuanjia southern suburb of Song, at the time they temporarily made small pitched tents for resting; Taishi slightly enlarged them; early Yongming they grew increasingly tall and ornate; in recent years craftsmen proposed erecting tile-roofed buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Yuanjia southern suburb, men pitched small tents only for the day; Taishi modestly enlarged them; by early Yongming they had grown tall and fine; last year the builders asked to raise a tiled hall.

sentences.zh: 前代帝皇，豈於上天之祀而昧營構，所不爲者，深有情意。

translations.literal: Could former emperors have been ignorant of construction for sacrifices to Heaven above? What they did not do had deep intention.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier emperors were not blind to building for Heaven's rites; what they refused to build, they refused for deep reasons.

sentences.zh: 記稱『掃地而祭，於其質也，器用陶匏，天地之性也』。

translations.literal: The Record says 「Sweep the ground and sacrifice—in that lies simplicity; vessels of pottery and gourd are Heaven and Earth's nature.」
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 「Sweep the earth and offer—that is the substance of the rite; pottery and gourd vessels match the nature of Heaven and Earth.」

sentences.zh: 故『至敬無文』，『以素爲貴』。

translations.literal: Hence 「utmost reverence has no ornament」 and 「plainness is prized.」
translations.idiomatic: Hence 「the deepest reverence needs no display」 and 「simplicity is the treasure.」

sentences.zh: 竊謂郊事宜擬休偃，不俟高大，以明謙恭肅敬之旨。

translations.literal: I submit that the suburban rite should follow the model of resting quarters, not wait on height and grandeur, to make clear the aim of humble, reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the suburban altar should keep only modest shelters for rest, not lofty halls, so humility and awe remain plain.

sentences.zh: 庶或仰允太靈，俯愜羣望。

translations.literal: Perhaps then above it will please the Supreme Spirit, and below it will satisfy the multitude's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven above may be pleased, and the people below content.

sentences.zh: 」詔「付外詳」。

translations.literal: 」An edict said 「Refer to the outer offices for detailed deliberation.」
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict directed: 「Send the matter to the outer offices for detailed review.」

sentences.zh: 國子助教徐景嵩議：「伏尋《三禮》，天地兩祀，南北二郊，但明祭取犧牲，器用陶匏，不載人君偃處之儀。

translations.literal: National University assistant instructor Xu Jingsong argued: 「Examining the Three Rites, Heaven and Earth have two sacrifices and south and north two suburbs; they only specify victims and pottery-and-gourd vessels, and do not record where the ruler rests.
translations.idiomatic: National University assistant instructor Xu Jingsong argued: 「The Three Rites distinguish Heaven and Earth, southern and northern suburbs, victims and pottery vessels—but nowhere prescribe where the ruler should lodge.

sentences.zh: 今帳瓦之構雖殊，俱非千載成例，宜務因循。

translations.literal: Today's tent and tile structures differ, yet neither is a thousand-year precedent; one should follow established practice.
translations.idiomatic: Tents and tiled halls differ in form, but neither is ancient usage fixed for a millennium; we should stay with what has been done.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士賀瑒議：「《周禮》『王旅上帝，張氈案，設皇邸』。

translations.literal: 」University erudite He Chang argued: 「The Rites of Zhou says, When the king sojourns to sacrifice to the Lord on High, spread felt benches and set up the royal lodging.
translations.idiomatic: 」University erudite He Chang argued: 「The Rites of Zhou says: when the king travels to sacrifice to the Lord on High, he spreads felt benches and sets up the royal lodging.

sentences.zh: 國有故而祭，亦曰旅。

translations.literal: When the state has cause and sacrifices, that too is called a sojourn.
translations.idiomatic: When the state sacrifices on special occasion, that too is called a sojourn.

sentences.zh: 氈案，以氈爲牀於幄中，不聞郊所置宮宇。

translations.literal: Felt benches are beds of felt within curtains; one does not hear of palace buildings set up at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Felt benches are felt beds inside the awning; the classics never mention palace halls at the suburban mound.

sentences.zh: 」兼左丞王摛議，掃地而祭於郊，謂無築室之議。

translations.literal: 」Concurrent left assistant director Wang Chou argued that sweeping the ground to sacrifice at the suburb means there is no proposal to build rooms.
translations.idiomatic: 」Concurrent left assistant director Wang Chou held that sweeping earth for suburban sacrifice means no argument for permanent halls.

sentences.zh: 竝同曇隆。

translations.literal: All agreed with Tanlong.
translations.idiomatic: All sided with Yu Tanlong.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍虞炎議，以爲「誠愨所施，止在一壇，漢之郊祀，饗帝甘泉，天子自竹宮望拜，息殿去壇場旣遠，郊奉禮畢，旋幸於此。

translations.literal: Valiant Cavalry General Yu Yan argued that 「What sincerity offers is shown on a single altar; Han's suburban sacrifice feasted the Lord at Ganquan, and the Son of Heaven looked across and bowed from the Bamboo Palace; the rest hall was already far from the altar field—when the suburban rite was done, he at once went there.
translations.idiomatic: Valiant Cavalry General Yu Yan argued that 「Sincere offering needs only one mound; in Han's suburban rites the Lord was feasted at Ganquan while the emperor bowed from the Bamboo Palace—the rest hall lay far from the altar, and when the suburban rite ended he went straight there.

sentences.zh: 瓦殿之與帷宮，謂無簡格」。

translations.literal: Between a tiled hall and a curtained palace, he said, neither is ritually inferior to the other.」
translations.idiomatic: Between a tiled hall and a curtained lodge, he said, ritual law does not prefer one over the other.」

sentences.zh: 祠部郎李撝議：「《周禮》『凡祭祀張其旅幕，張尸次』。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices Li Huo argued: 「The Rites of Zhou says 「For every sacrifice spread the journeying curtains; spread the personator's place.」
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices Li Huo argued: 「The Rites of Zhou says 「For every sacrifice spread the journeying curtains; spread the personator's station.」

sentences.zh: 尸則有幄。

translations.literal: For the personator there are curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The personator has his canopy.

sentences.zh: 仲師云『尸次，祭祀之尸所居更衣帳也』。

translations.literal: Master Zhong said 「The personator's place is the changing tent where the personator of the sacrifice dwells.」
translations.idiomatic: Master Zhong said 「The personator's station is the tent where the sacrifice's personator robes and rests.」

sentences.zh: 凡祭之文，旣不止於郊祀，立尸之言，理應關於宗廟。

translations.literal: The texts on sacrifice are not limited to suburban rites; language of establishing a personator properly concerns the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial law is not only about the suburbs; talk of setting up a personator belongs chiefly to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 古則張幕，今也房省。

translations.literal: Antiquity spread curtains; today we use roofed chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity used curtains; today we use roofed rooms.

sentences.zh: 宗廟旅幕，可變爲棟宇；

translations.literal: Journeying curtains at the temple may become beam-and-rafter halls;
translations.idiomatic: Temple journeying curtains may become timber halls;

sentences.zh: 郊祀氈案，何爲不轉製檐甍？

translations.literal: why should felt benches at the suburban sacrifice not be turned into eaves and tiles?
translations.idiomatic: why should suburban felt benches not be made into eaves and tiles?

sentences.zh: 」曇隆議不行。

translations.literal: 」Tanlong's proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yu Tanlong's proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 建武二年旱，有司議雩祭依明堂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu there was drought; the relevant offices debated rain sacrifice following the Bright Hall model.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu year 2 brought drought; the relevant offices debated a rain sacrifice modeled on the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議曰：「《周禮司巫》云『若國大旱，則帥巫而舞雩』。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi argued: 「The Rites of Zhou, Office of Shamans, says, If the state suffers great drought, lead the shamans in the rain dance.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi argued: 「The Rites of Zhou, Office of Shamans, says: if the state suffers great drought, lead the shamans in the rain dance.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『雩，旱祭也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said, Yu is the drought sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: Yu is the drought sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 天子於上帝，諸侯以下於上公之神』。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven (sacrifices) to the Lord on High; feudal lords down to the spirits of the upper duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven (sacrifices) to the Lord on High; feudal lords, to the spirits of the upper duke.

sentences.zh: 又《女巫》云『旱暵則舞雩』。

translations.literal: Again, the Office of Female Shamans says, In drought and heat, dance the yu.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Office of Female Shamans says: in drought and scorching heat, dance the yu.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『使女巫舞旱祭，崇陰也』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said, Have female shamans dance the drought sacrifice—honoring yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: have female shamans dance the drought rite—honoring yin.

sentences.zh: 鄭衆云『求雨以女巫』。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong said, Seek rain through female shamans.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong said: seek rain through female shamans.

sentences.zh: 《禮記月令》云『命有司爲民祈祀山川百原，乃大雩帝，用盛樂。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites, Monthly Ordinances, says, Order the officers to pray for the people to the mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs; then perform the great yu to the Lord, using full music.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites, Monthly Ordinances, says: order the officers to pray for the people at mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs; then perform the great yu to the Lord with full music.

sentences.zh: 乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士有益於民者，以祈穀實』。
