translations.literal: Then order the hundred districts to perform yu sacrifice to the hundred lords and ministers who benefit the people, to pray for grain's fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Then order the hundred districts to perform yu to the hundred lords and ministers who benefit the people, praying for full grain.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『陽氣盛而恒旱。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said 「Yang qi is strong and drought is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said 「Yang breath is strong and drought constant.

sentences.zh: 山川百原，能興雲致雨者也。

translations.literal: Mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs are what can raise clouds and bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs are what can raise clouds and send rain.

sentences.zh: 衆水所出爲百原，必先祭其本。

translations.literal: Where the many waters issue is the hundred springs; one must first sacrifice to their source.
translations.idiomatic: Where many waters rise is the hundred springs; one must sacrifice first at their source.

sentences.zh: 雩，吁嗟求雨之祭也。

translations.literal: Yu is the sacrifice of calling and sighing to seek rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is the rite of calling and sighing for rain.

sentences.zh: 雩帝，謂爲壇南郊之旁，祭五精之帝，配以先帝也。

translations.literal: Yu to the Lord means establishing an altar beside the southern suburban altar, sacrificing to the Five Regents, with the former emperor as companion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu to the Lord means an altar beside the southern suburban mound, sacrificing to the Five Regents with the former emperor paired.

sentences.zh: 自鞉鞞至柷敔爲盛樂，他雩用歌舞而已。

translations.literal: From hand-drums to chu and yu is full music; other yu use song and dance only.
translations.idiomatic: From hand-drums to chu and yu counts as full music; lesser yu use song and dance alone.

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，古者上公以下，謂勾龍、后稷之類也。

translations.literal: The hundred lords and ministers—in antiquity those from upper duke down, such as Goulao and Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred lords and ministers—in antiquity, from upper duke downward, such as Goulao and Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰龍見而雩，雩之正當以四月』。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals says, When the dragon appears, perform yu; the proper time for yu is the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals says: when the dragon appears, perform yu; the proper month for yu is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 王肅云『大雩，求雨之祭也。

translations.literal: Wang Su said, The great yu is the sacrifice to seek rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: the great yu is the rite to seek rain.

sentences.zh: 傳曰龍見而雩，謂四月也。

translations.literal: The commentary says, When the dragon appears, perform yu—meaning the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, When the dragon appears, perform yu—meaning the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 若五月六月大旱，亦用雩，《禮》於五月著雩義也』。

translations.literal: If in the fifth or sixth month there is great drought, yu is also used; the Rites sets out the meaning of yu in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: If in the fifth or sixth month drought is severe, yu is used as well; the Rites records the meaning of yu in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 晉永和中，中丞啓，雩制在國之南爲壇，祈上帝百辟，舞童八列六十四人，歌《雲漢》詩，皆以孟夏。

translations.literal: In Jin's Yonghe era the censor memorialized: the yu regulation places an altar south of the state, praying to the Lord on High and the hundred lords; eight ranks of dancers, sixty-four boys; they sing the ode Yun Han—all in the first summer month.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin's Yonghe, the censor reported: yu law set an altar south of the capital, praying to the Lord on High and the hundred lords; eight ranks of dancers, sixty-four boys; they sang the ode Yun Han—all in the first summer month.

sentences.zh: 得雨，報太牢。

translations.literal: When rain came, they reported with the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: When rain came, they reported it with the great offering.

sentences.zh: 于時博士議，舊有壇，漢、魏各自討尋。

translations.literal: At that time the erudites deliberated: there were old altars, and Han and Wei each investigated on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The erudites then debated: altars already existed, and Han and Wei had each traced their own precedents.

sentences.zh: 月令云『命有司祈祀山川百原，乃大雩』。

translations.literal: The Monthly Commands say, 「Let the relevant offices pray and sacrifice to mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs, and then perform the great Yu.」
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Commands say, 「Let the relevant offices pray to mountains, rivers, and the hundred springs, and then hold the great Yu sacrifice.」

sentences.zh: 又云『乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士』。

translations.literal: It also says, 「Then order the hundred districts to perform Yu sacrifice to the hundred lords, ministers, and officers.」
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 「Then order the hundred districts to offer Yu sacrifice to the hundred lords, ministers, and officers.」

sentences.zh: 則大雩所祭，唯應祭五精之帝而已。

translations.literal: Thus what the great Yu sacrifices to should be only the Five Essence Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: On that reading the great Yu rite should worship only the Five Essence Emperors.

sentences.zh: 勾芒等五神，旣是五帝之佐，依鄭玄說，宜配食於庭也。

translations.literal: Gou Mang and the other five spirits are already assistants to the Five Emperors; following Zheng Xuan, they should be paired at the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Mang and the other five spirits are assistants to the Five Emperors; on Zheng Xuan's view they should receive paired offerings in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『雩壇在南郊壇之旁』，而不辨東西。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says, 「The Yu altar is beside the southern suburban altar,」 but does not distinguish east from west.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says the Yu altar stands beside the southern suburban altar but does not say whether east or west.

sentences.zh: 尋地道尊右，雩壇方郊壇爲輕，理應在左。

translations.literal: Tracing the earthly way's honoring of the right, the Yu altar, being lighter than the suburban altar, should in principle stand on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's way honors the right; the Yu altar ranks below the suburban altar and should therefore stand on the left.

sentences.zh: 宜於郊壇之東，營域之外築壇。

translations.literal: It is fitting to build the altar east of the suburban altar, outside the sacred precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The altar should be built east of the suburban altar, outside the sacred enclosure.

sentences.zh: 旣祭五帝，謂壇宜員。

translations.literal: Since one sacrifices to the Five Emperors, the altar should be round.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Five Emperors are worshipped there, the altar should be round.

sentences.zh: 尋雩壇高廣，《禮》、《傳》無明文，案《覲禮》設方明之祀，爲壇高四尺，用珪璋等六玉，禮天地四方之神，王者率諸侯親禮，爲所以教尊尊也。

translations.literal: Searching for the height and breadth of the Yu altar, the Rites and commentaries give no explicit text; examining the Rites of Observation's establishment of the fangming sacrifice, the altar was four chi high and used the gui, zhang, and other six jades to honor the spirits of Heaven, Earth, and the four directions—the king leading the feudal lords in person to teach honoring what is honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites and commentaries say nothing explicit about the Yu altar's height and breadth; the Rites of Observation's fangming rite, however, used a mound four chi high with the six jades—gui, zhang, and the rest—to honor Heaven, Earth, and the spirits of the four quarters, the king leading the feudal lords in person to teach the order of honor.

sentences.zh: 雩祭五帝，粗可依放。

translations.literal: The Yu sacrifice to the Five Emperors may roughly follow that model.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu sacrifice to the Five Emperors may roughly follow that precedent.

sentences.zh: 謂今築壇宜崇四尺，其廣輪仍以四爲度，徑四丈，周員十二丈，而四階也。

translations.literal: I hold that the altar built now should be four chi high; its breadth and circumference should still take four as the measure—a diameter of four zhang, a round circumference of twelve zhang, and four steps.
translations.idiomatic: The new altar should be four chi high; breadth and circumference should still use four as the unit—a diameter of four zhang, a circumference of twelve zhang, and four steps.

sentences.zh: 設五帝之位，各依其方，如在明堂之儀。

translations.literal: Set the places of the Five Emperors, each according to its direction, as in the Bright Hall rite.
translations.idiomatic: Place the Five Emperors each in his proper direction, as at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇齊以世祖配五精於明堂，今亦宜配饗於雩壇矣。

translations.literal: Great Qi pairs the Founder Emperor with the five essences at the Bright Hall; he should now be paired at the Yu altar as well.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi already pairs the Founder Emperor with the five essences at the Bright Hall; he should be paired at the Yu altar too.

sentences.zh: 古者孟春郊祀祈嘉穀，孟夏雩禜祈甘雨，二祭雖殊，而所爲者一。

translations.literal: In antiquity the first-month suburban sacrifice prayed for fine grain; the fourth-month Yu sacrifice prayed for sweet rain—the two rites differ, but their purpose is one.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity prayed for good grain at the spring suburban rite and for sweet rain at the summer Yu rite—different ceremonies, but the same aim.

sentences.zh: 禮唯有冬至報天，初無得雨賽帝。

translations.literal: The rites provide only the winter-solstice report to Heaven; originally there was no thanking the emperors when rain came.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual knows only the winter-solstice report to Heaven; there was originally no separate thanksgiving to the emperors after rain.

sentences.zh: 今雖闕冬至之祭，而南郊兼祈報之禮，理不容別有賽荅之事也。

translations.literal: Though the winter-solstice sacrifice is now omitted, the southern suburb combines prayer and report; in principle there cannot be a separate thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: The winter-solstice rite is now omitted, but the southern suburb already combines prayer and report—so a separate thanksgiving would be out of place.

sentences.zh: 禮祀帝於郊，則所尚省費，周祭靈威仰若后稷，各用一牲，今祀五帝、世祖，亦宜各用一犢，斯外悉如南郊之禮也。

translations.literal: When ritual sacrifices to emperors at the suburb, it values economy; Zhou sacrificed to Lingweiyang and Hou Ji with one victim each—now the Five Emperors and the Founder Emperor should each have one calf; beyond that, all should follow the southern suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban worship of emperors stresses economy: Zhou gave Lingweiyang and Hou Ji one victim each; the Five Emperors and the Founder Emperor should each receive one calf, with everything else following the southern suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 武皇遏密未終，自可不奏盛樂。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor's mourning taboo is not yet ended; grand music naturally need not be performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor's mourning period is not yet over, so grand music need not be played.

sentences.zh: 至於旱祭舞雩，蓋是吁嗟之義，旣非存懽樂，謂此不涉嫌。

translations.literal: As for the drought rite's Yu dance, it is essentially the meaning of calling aloud; since it is not meant to store up pleasure, I hold that this does not run afoul of the taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu dance in a drought rite is a matter of calling aloud, not of stored-up pleasure; I do not think it violates the mourning rule.

sentences.zh: 其餘祝史稱辭，仰祈靈澤而已。

translations.literal: The rest is invocators and clerks speaking the prayers, looking up to beg for spiritual moisture—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, invocators and clerks need only speak the prayers and beg Heaven for rain.

sentences.zh: 禮舞雩乃使無闕，今之女巫竝不習歌舞，方就教試，恐不應速。

translations.literal: The rites say the Yu dance employs those without blemish; today's shamanesses do not all know song and dance and are only now being trained—I fear it should not be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: The rites require unblemished performers for the Yu dance; today's shamanesses are not all trained in song and dance and are only beginning instruction—I doubt they can be ready in time.

sentences.zh: 依晉朝之議，使童子，或時取舍之宜也。

translations.literal: Following the Jin court's deliberation, use boys—that may be what the times call for.
translations.idiomatic: Following Jin practice, boys should be used—that may be the fitting choice for now.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪《禮儀志》云雩祀著皂衣，蓋是崇陰之義。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Treatise on Rites and Ceremonies says Yu sacrifice wears black garments—probably the meaning of honoring yin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Treatise on Rites says Yu worshippers wear black—honoring yin, no doubt.

sentences.zh: 今祭服皆緇，差無所革。

translations.literal: Today's sacrificial robes are already black; there is scarcely anything to change.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress is already black; little needs changing.

sentences.zh: 其所歌之詩，及諸供須，輙勒主者申攝備辦。

translations.literal: As for the hymn to be sung and the various supplies, order the responsible officials at once to oversee preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn and all other requirements should be ordered prepared at once by the officials in charge.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，有司奏，參議明堂，咸以世祖配。

translations.literal: Longchang year 1, the relevant offices memorialized to deliberate jointly on the Bright Hall; all held that the Founder Emperor should be paired.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang 1: the relevant offices memorialized for joint deliberation on the Bright Hall; all agreed the Founder Emperor should be paired.

sentences.zh: 國子助教謝曇濟議：「案《祭法》禘郊祖宗，竝列嚴祀。

translations.literal: National University assistant instructor Xie Tanji argued: 「Examining the Regulations of Sacrifice, di, suburban, ancestral, and forbear rites are all listed as solemn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: National University assistant instructor Xie Tanji argued: 「The Regulations of Sacrifice list di, suburban, ancestral, and forbear rites together as solemn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注義，亦據兼饗。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary meaning also rests on joint sharing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary likewise rests on joint pairing.

sentences.zh: 宜祖宗兩配，文、武雙祀。

translations.literal: It is fitting to pair both ancestral and forbear spirits—Wen and Wu in double sacrifice.」
translations.idiomatic: Both ancestral and forbear spirits should be paired—Wen and Wu worshipped together.」

sentences.zh: 」助教徐景嵩、光祿大夫王逡之謂宜以世宗文皇帝配。

translations.literal: Assistant instructor Xu Jingsong and chamberlain for splendor Wang Xunzhi held that the Shizong Wen Emperor should be paired.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant instructor Xu Jingsong and chamberlain for splendor Wang Xunzhi argued for pairing the Shizong Wen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議：「周之文、武，尚推后稷以配天，謂文皇宜推世祖以配帝。

translations.literal: Director of sacrificial affairs He Tongzhi argued: 「Zhou's Wen and Wu still pushed Hou Ji forward to pair with Heaven—I hold the Wen Emperor should push the Founder Emperor forward to pair with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Director of sacrificial affairs He Tongzhi argued: 「Even Zhou's Wen and Wu set Hou Ji before them to pair with Heaven; the Wen Emperor should set the Founder Emperor before him to pair with the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雖事施於尊祖，亦義章於嚴父焉。

translations.literal: Though the act is directed at honoring an ancestor, it also displays the meaning of revering one's father.」
translations.idiomatic: The rite honors an ancestor, but it also makes clear the reverence due a father.」

sentences.zh: 」左僕射王晏議，以爲「若用鄭玄祖宗通稱，則生有功德，沒垂尊稱，歷代配帝，何止於二邪？

translations.literal: Left vice director Wang Yan argued, holding that 「if one uses Zheng Xuan's general term for ancestral and forbear spirits, then those who had merit in life receive exalted titles after death—how could paired emperors be limited to two?
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Wang Yan argued that 「if Zheng Xuan's general term for ancestral and forbear spirits is followed, every meritorious ruler would receive an exalted posthumous title—why should paired emperors stop at two?

sentences.zh: 今殷薦上帝，允屬世祖，百代不毀，其文廟乎！

translations.literal: Now the offering to the August God surely belongs to the Founder Emperor; undestroyed for a hundred generations—is that not the temple of Wen?」
translations.idiomatic: The August God's offering belongs to the Founder Emperor alone; undestroyed for a hundred generations—is that not Wen's temple?」

translations.literal: Edict: 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: Edict: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 至永元二年，佟之又建議曰：「案《祭法》『有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，祖顓頊而宗堯』。

translations.literal: By Yongyuan year 2, Tongzhi again proposed, saying: 「Examining the Regulations of Sacrifice: 「The Youyu clan performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku; they took Zhuanxu as ancestor and Yao as forbear.」
translations.idiomatic: By Yongyuan 2, Tongzhi proposed again: 「The Regulations of Sacrifice say: 「The Youyu clan performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku, took Zhuanxu as ancestor, and Yao as forbear.」

sentences.zh: 『周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王』。

translations.literal: 「The Zhou performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji; they took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as forbear.」
translations.idiomatic: 「The Zhou performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji, took King Wen as ancestor, and King Wu as forbear.」

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『禘郊祖宗，謂祭祀以配食也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says, 「Di, suburban, ancestral, and forbear mean sacrifice with paired sharing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says, 「Di, suburban, ancestral, and forbear mean sacrifice with paired spirits.

sentences.zh: 此禘謂祀昊天於圜丘也。

translations.literal: This di means sacrificing to August Heaven at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: Di here means worshipping August Heaven at the round mound.

sentences.zh: 祭上帝於南郊曰郊，祭五帝五神於明堂曰祖宗』。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to the Lord on High at the southern suburb is called suburban; sacrificing to the Five Emperors and five spirits at the Bright Hall is called ancestral and forbear.」
translations.idiomatic: Worship at the southern suburb is called suburban; worship of the Five Emperors and five spirits at the Bright Hall is called ancestral and forbear.」

sentences.zh: 『郊祭一帝，而明堂祭五帝，小德配寡，大德配衆』。

translations.literal: 「Suburban sacrifice is to one emperor; the Bright Hall sacrifices to five emperors—small merit pairs with few, great merit with many.」
translations.idiomatic: 「The suburb honours one emperor; the Bright Hall honours five—lesser merit pairs with fewer spirits, greater merit with more.」

sentences.zh: 王肅云『祖宗是廟不毀之名』。

translations.literal: Wang Su says, 「Ancestral and forbear are names for temples that are not destroyed.」
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su says, 「Ancestral and forbear are names for undestroyed temples.」

sentences.zh: 果如肅言，殷有三祖三宗，竝應不毀，何故止稱湯、契？

translations.literal: If it is truly as Su says, Yin had three ancestors and three forbears—all should be undestroyed—so why are only Tang and Qi named?
translations.idiomatic: If Su is right, Yin had three ancestors and three forbears, all of which should stand forever—why are only Tang and Qi named?

sentences.zh: 且王者之後存焉，舜寧立堯、頊之廟，傳世祀之乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, when a king's line survives, would Shun have established temples to Yao and Zhuanxu and passed down sacrifice through the generations?
translations.idiomatic: And when a king's line survives, would Shun have built temples to Yao and Zhuanxu and handed down sacrifice through the generations?

sentences.zh: 漢文以高祖配泰畤，至武帝立明堂，復以高祖配食，一人兩配，有乖聖典。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han paired the High Ancestor at the Grand Unity altar; when Emperor Wu established the Bright Hall, he again paired the High Ancestor—one man paired twice, contrary to the sage canon.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi paired Gaozu at the Grand Unity altar; when Wudi built the Bright Hall he paired Gaozu again—one man twice, against the sage canon.

sentences.zh: 自漢明以來，未能反者。

translations.literal: From Emperor Ming of Han onward, the court could not reverse it.
translations.idiomatic: From Han Mingdi on, no emperor could undo the practice.

sentences.zh: 故明堂無兼配之祀。

translations.literal: Therefore the Bright Hall has no sacrifice with joint pairing.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Bright Hall has no rite with two paired spirits.

sentences.zh: 竊謂先皇宜列二帝於文祖，尊新廟爲高宗，竝世祖而泛配，以申聖主嚴父之義。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that the former emperor should list the two emperors at the Wen ancestor, honor the new temple as Gaozong, and pair broadly with the Founder Emperor—to express the sage ruler's meaning of revering his father.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the former emperor should place both emperors at the Wen ancestor, name the new temple Gaozong, and pair them broadly with the Founder Emperor—thus fulfilling a sage ruler's reverence for his father.

sentences.zh: 先皇於武皇，倫則第爲季，義則經爲臣，設配饗之坐，應在世祖之下，竝列，俱西向。」

translations.literal: As for the Former Emperor relative to Emperor Wu, in order of birth he ranks as the younger, in ritual obligation as a minister-subject; set seats for paired sharing—they should stand below the Founder Emperor, arranged in parallel, all facing west.」
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor before Emperor Wu: by birth he is the younger brother, by ritual the minister; seats for paired offerings should stand below the Founder Emperor, side by side, all facing west.」

sentences.zh: 國子博士王摛議：「《孝經》『周公郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝』。

translations.literal: National University erudite Wang Chi argued: 「In the Classic of Filial Piety, 『Duke of Zhou performed suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to pair with Heaven, ancestral sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to pair with the Lord on High』.
translations.idiomatic: National University erudite Wang Chi argued: 「The Classic of Filial Piety says, 『Duke of Zhou sacrificed at the suburb to Hou Ji to pair with Heaven and performed ancestral sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to pair with the Lord on High』.

sentences.zh: 不云武王。

translations.literal: It does not mention King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: It never names King Wu.

sentences.zh: 又《周頌》『《思文》，后稷配天也』。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Zhou Songs, 『Si Wen—Hou Ji paired with Heaven』.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Zhou Songs: 『Si Wen—Hou Ji paired with Heaven.』

sentences.zh: 『《我將》，祀文王於明堂也』。

translations.literal: 『Wo Jiang—sacrificing to King Wen at the Bright Hall.』
translations.idiomatic: 『Wo Jiang—sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall.』

sentences.zh: 武王之文，唯《執競》云『祀武王』。

translations.literal: Text concerning King Wu appears only in Zhi Jing, which says 『sacrificing to King Wu』.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu appears only in Zhi Jing: 『sacrificing to King Wu.』

sentences.zh: 此自周廟祭武王詩，彌知明堂無矣。」

translations.literal: That is itself a Zhou temple hymn for sacrificing to King Wu—how much more does it show there was none at the Bright Hall.」
translations.idiomatic: That hymn belongs to the Zhou ancestral temple, not the Bright Hall—proof enough that Wu had no place there.」

sentences.zh: 佟之又議：「《孝經》是周公居攝時禮，《祭法》是成王反位後所行。

translations.literal: Tongzhi argued again: 「The Classic of Filial Piety records rites from when the Duke of Zhou served as regent; the Regulations of Sacrifice record what was practiced after King Cheng returned to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi argued again: 「The Classic of Filial Piety belongs to the Duke of Zhou's regency; the Regulations of Sacrifice to King Cheng after he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 故《孝經》以文王爲宗，《祭法》以文王爲祖。

translations.literal: Therefore the Filial Piety classic takes King Wen as forbear, the Regulations take King Wen as ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Filial Piety classic names King Wen forbear, the Regulations ancestor.

sentences.zh: 又孝莫大於嚴父配天，則周公其人也，尋此旨，寧施成王乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, no filial piety is greater than exalting the father and pairing with Heaven—the Duke of Zhou is that man; tracing this intent, how could it apply to King Cheng?
translations.idiomatic: And the greatest filial act is to exalt the father and pair him with Heaven—that was the Duke of Zhou, not King Cheng; read that intent, and Cheng cannot be the subject.

sentences.zh: 若《孝經》所說，審是成王所行，則爲嚴祖，何得云嚴父邪？

translations.literal: If what the Classic of Filial Piety describes was truly King Cheng's practice, it would exalt an ancestor—how could it speak of exalting a father?
translations.idiomatic: If the Filial Piety classic described Cheng's own rites, it would exalt an ancestor, not a father.

sentences.zh: 且《思文》是周公祀后稷配天之樂歌，《我將》是祀文王配明堂之樂歌。

translations.literal: Moreover, Si Wen is the hymn when the Duke of Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji pairing with Heaven; Wo Jiang is the hymn for sacrificing to King Wen paired at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Si Wen is the Duke of Zhou's hymn when he sacrificed to Hou Ji to pair with Heaven; Wo Jiang, when he sacrificed to King Wen at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 若如摛議，則此二篇，皆應在復子明辟之後。

translations.literal: If Wang Chi is right, both pieces should fall after restoring the son and making clear the regency's end.
translations.idiomatic: On Wang Chi's reading, both hymns would postdate the return of the son and the end of the regency.

sentences.zh: 請問周公祀后稷、文王，爲何所歌？

translations.literal: I ask: when the Duke of Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji and King Wen, for what were these hymns sung?
translations.idiomatic: Then for what rites did the Duke of Zhou sing them—to Hou Ji and to King Wen?

sentences.zh: 又《國語》云『周人禘嚳郊稷，祖文王，宗武王』。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Discourses of the States says, 『The Zhou performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji, took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as forbear.』
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of the States also says, 『The Zhou performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji, took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as forbear.』

sentences.zh: 韋昭云『周公時，以文王爲宗，其後更以文王爲祖，武王爲宗』。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao says, 『In the Duke of Zhou's time King Wen was taken as forbear; afterward King Wen was made ancestor and King Wu forbear.』
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao explains: 『Under the Duke of Zhou, Wen was forbear; later Wen became ancestor and Wu forbear.』

sentences.zh: 尋文王以文治而爲祖，武王以武定而爲宗，欲明文亦有大德，武亦有大功，故鄭注《祭法》云『祖宗通言耳』。

translations.literal: Tracing this: King Wen became ancestor through civil order, King Wu forbear through martial settlement—they wished to show Wen also had great virtue and Wu great merit; hence Zheng Xuan's note on the Regulations says, 『ancestor and forbear are general terms.』
translations.idiomatic: Wen earned ancestorhood through civil order, Wu forbearhood through martial settlement—the point was that Wen had great virtue and Wu great merit; hence Zheng Xuan on the Regulations: 『ancestor and forbear are general terms.』

sentences.zh: 是以《詩》云『昊天有成命，二后受之』。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say, 『August Heaven made the fixed mandate; the two queens received it.』
translations.idiomatic: So the Odes: 『August Heaven fixed the mandate; the two queens received it.』

sentences.zh: 注云『二后，文王、武王也』。

translations.literal: The commentary says, 『The two queens are King Wen and King Wu.』
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: 『The two queens are King Wen and King Wu.』

sentences.zh: 且明堂之祀，有單有合。

translations.literal: Moreover, Bright Hall sacrifice has solitary and combined forms.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall worship, moreover, may be single or combined.

sentences.zh: 故鄭云『四時迎氣於郊，祭一帝，還於明堂，因祭一帝，則以文王配』。

translations.literal: Hence Zheng says, 『At the four seasons welcoming qi at the suburb, sacrifice to one emperor; returning to the Bright Hall, with sacrifice to one emperor, pair King Wen.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng says: 『At each season qi is welcomed at the suburb and one emperor is sacrificed to; back at the Bright Hall, with sacrifice to one emperor, King Wen is paired.』

sentences.zh: 明一賔不容兩主也。

translations.literal: This shows one guest cannot hold two hosts.
translations.idiomatic: One guest cannot serve two hosts.

sentences.zh: 『享五帝於明堂，則泛配文、武。

translations.literal: 『When offering to the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall, broadly pair King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: 『When the Five Emperors are offered to at the Bright Hall, King Wen and King Wu are broadly paired.

sentences.zh: 』泛之爲言，無的之辭。

translations.literal: 』 "Broadly" as a word means language without a fixed target.
translations.idiomatic: 』 "Broadly" means an unfixed, general pairing.

sentences.zh: 其禮旣盛，故祖宗竝配。

translations.literal: When the rite is already grand, therefore ancestor and forbear are paired together.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite grows grand, ancestor and forbear are paired together.

sentences.zh: 」參議以佟之爲允。

translations.literal: 」Joint deliberation held Tongzhi acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: 」The joint deliberation found Tongzhi persuasive.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: Edict: 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: Edict: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 太祖爲齊王，依舊立五廟。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor, as Prince of Qi, established the five temples as before.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Qi, the Founder kept the five ancestral temples as before.

sentences.zh: 卽位，立七廟。

translations.literal: Upon taking the throne, he established seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he raised seven temples.

sentences.zh: 廣陵府君、太中府君、淮陰府君、卽丘府君、太常府君、宣皇帝、昭皇后爲七廟。

translations.literal: Lord of Guangling, Lord of Taizhong, Lord of Huaiyin, Lord of Jiuqiu, Lord of Taichang, Emperor Xuan, and Empress Zhao were the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: The seven were: Lords of Guangling, Taizhong, Huaiyin, Jiuqiu, and Taichang; Emperor Xuan; and Empress Zhao.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，太祖親祀太廟六室，如儀，拜伏竟，次至昭后室前，儀注應倚立，上以爲疑，欲使廟僚行事，又欲以諸王代祝令於昭后室前執爵。

translations.literal: Jianyuan 2, the Founder personally sacrificed at the six chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple according to ritual; when bowing was finished, next he came before Empress Zhao's chamber—regulations called for leaning-posture standing; the emperor was doubtful, wishing to have temple officials perform, or wishing princes to replace the invoker at Empress Zhao's chamber to hold the cup.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 2 the Founder sacrificed in person at six chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. When he had finished bowing and came to Empress Zhao's chamber, the regulations required him to stand leaning—he hesitated, considering whether temple staff should act for him or whether a prince should replace the invoker and hold the cup before the empress's seat.

sentences.zh: 以問彭城丞劉瓛。

translations.literal: He questioned Pengcheng assistant Liu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Pengcheng assistant Liu Huan.

sentences.zh: 瓛對謂：「若都不至昭后坐前，竊以爲薄。

translations.literal: Huan replied: 「If he did not come at all before Empress Zhao's seat, I would deem it meager.
translations.idiomatic: Huan answered: 「To stay away from Empress Zhao's seat entirely would, I think, show too little regard.

sentences.zh: 廟僚卽是代上執爵饋奠耳，祝令位卑，恐諸王無容代之。

translations.literal: Temple officials would merely hold the cup and present offerings for the emperor; the invoker's rank is low—I fear princes could not suitably replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Temple officials would only hold the cup and present the offering in the emperor's place; the invoker ranks too low for a prince to stand in for him.

sentences.zh: 舊廟儀諸王得兼三公親事，謂此爲便。

translations.literal: Old temple ritual allowed princes concurrently to handle the Three Dukes' personal duties—this was deemed convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Older temple usage let princes take on the Three Dukes' personal duties—that was the convenient course.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及太子穆妃薨，卒哭，祔于太廟陰室。

translations.literal: When Crown Princess Mu died, after the final mourning wail, she was enshrined in the yin chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Princess Mu died, after the final wail she was enshrined in the temple's yin chamber.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，文惠太子薨，卒哭，祔于太廟陰室。

translations.literal: Yongming 11, Crown Prince Wenhui died; after the final wail, enshrined in the yin chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 11 Crown Prince Wenhui died; after the final wail he too was enshrined in the yin chamber.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，毀廣陵府君。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, Lord Guangling's temple was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Founder's death, Lord Guangling's shrine was removed.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，追尊文帝，又毀太中主，止淮陰府君。

translations.literal: Yulin took the throne, posthumously honored Emperor Wen, again destroyed Lord Taizhong, leaving only Lord Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin acceded he posthumously honored Emperor Wen, removed Lord Taizhong's shrine, and kept only Lord Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，復舊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was enthroned, he restored the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming restored the former order.

sentences.zh: 及崩，祔廟，與世祖爲兄弟，不爲世數。

translations.literal: When he died, enshrined in the temple; paired with the Founder Emperor as brothers, not counted in generations.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was enshrined beside the Founder Emperor as a brother, outside the generational count.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：先儒說宗廟之義，據高祖已下五世親盡，故親廟有四。

translations.literal: The historian says: Former scholars explained ancestral temples by holding that from the High Ancestor down, affection ends at five generations, hence there are four intimate temples.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Earlier scholars explained the ancestral temple by saying that from the High Ancestor down, kinship thins at five generations—hence four intimate temples.

sentences.zh: 周以后稷始祖，文、武二祧，所以云王立七廟也。

translations.literal: Zhou took Hou Ji as founder, Wen and Wu as two elevated lines—hence it is said a king establishes seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou made Hou Ji founder and Wen and Wu two elevated lines—hence the king's seven temples.

sentences.zh: 禹無始祖，湯不先契，夏五殷六，其數如之。

translations.literal: Yu had no founder, Tang did not place Qi first—Xia had five, Yin six; the numbers match.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had no founder; Tang did not place Qi first. Xia kept five, Yin six—the counts follow the same logic.

sentences.zh: 漢立宗廟，違經背古。

translations.literal: Han established ancestral temples in violation of canon and against antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Han's ancestral temples broke the canon and turned from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 匡衡、貢禹、蔡邕之徒，空有遷毀之議，亘年四百，竟無成典。

translations.literal: Kuang Heng, Gong Yu, Cai Yong, and the like had only empty proposals for moving and destroying; four hundred years stretched on, yet no settled statute was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Heng, Gong Yu, Cai Yong, and others debated moving and destroying shrines for four hundred years without ever fixing a lasting rule.

sentences.zh: 魏氏之初，親廟止乎四葉，吳、蜀享祭，失禮已多。

translations.literal: At Wei's beginning, intimate temples stopped at four generations; Wu and Shu in their worship had already lost ritual in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei kept intimate temples to four generations; Wu and Shu had already strayed far from proper sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 晉用王肅之談，以文、景爲共世，上至征西，其實六也。

translations.literal: Jin used Wang Su's doctrine, taking Wen and Jing as one generation; counting up to the western expedition lord, there were actually six.
translations.idiomatic: Jin followed Wang Su, treating Wen and Jing as one generation; counting up to the Lord of the Western Expedition, there were six in fact.

sentences.zh: 尋其此意，非以兄弟爲後，當以立主之義，可相容於七室。

translations.literal: Tracing this intent, it was not that brothers served as successors; by the meaning of establishing the main line, seven chambers could be accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: Read closely, the point was not that brothers succeeded one another, but that the logic of establishing the main line could fit seven chambers.

sentences.zh: 及楊元后崩，征西之廟不毀，則知不以元后爲世數。

translations.literal: When Empress Yang Yuan died, the Western Campaign temple was not destroyed—thus one knows they did not count the empress as a generation in the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yang Yuan died, the Western Campaign shrine was left standing—showing that an empress was not counted as a generation in the line.

sentences.zh: 廟有七室，數盈八主。

translations.literal: The temple had seven chambers, yet the count exceeded eight spirit lords.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine had seven chambers, yet the tablets numbered more than eight.

sentences.zh: 江左賀循立議以後，弟不繼兄，故世必限七，主無定數。

translations.literal: After He Xun established his position in the Jiangzuo court, younger brothers did not succeed elder brothers, so generations were necessarily limited to seven, but the number of spirit lords had no fixed limit.
translations.idiomatic: After He Xun framed the eastern-Jin rule that younger brothers do not succeed elder brothers, generations had to stop at seven, but the number of spirit tablets did not.

sentences.zh: 宋臺初立五廟，以臧后爲世室。

translations.literal: When Song first established its dynasty, it set up five temples, with Empress Zang as the generation hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Song first took the throne, it built five temples and made Empress Zang the generation hall.

sentences.zh: 就禮而求，亦親廟四矣。

translations.literal: Judged by ritual, that already makes four close-ancestor temples.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against ritual, that is already four close-ancestor temples.

sentences.zh: 義反會鄭，非謂從王。

translations.literal: The sense runs counter to Zheng Xuan; it does not mean following Wang Su.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning cuts against Zheng Xuan and does not mean adopting Wang Su's view.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，因仍舊制。

translations.literal: From this time forward, they followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they kept the former practice.

sentences.zh: 夫妻道合，非世葉相承，譬由下祭殤嫡，無關廟數，同之祖曾，義未可了。

translations.literal: Husband and wife are united in the Way, not successive generations in a lineage; it is like inferior sacrifices for untimely-dead legitimate sons—unrelated to temple count; comparing them to ancestors and great-grandfathers—the meaning cannot be fully settled.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife share one bond, not a line of generations; it is like the lesser rites for a legitimate son who died young—nothing to do with how many temples stand. To class wives with ancestors and great-grandfathers leaves the point unresolved.

sentences.zh: 若據伊尹之言，必及七世，則子昭孫穆，不列婦人。

translations.literal: If one follows Yi Yin's words that one must reach seven generations, then sons in zhao and grandsons in mu—women are not listed.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds to Yi Yin's rule of seven generations, then sons in the zhao wing and grandsons in the mu—wives are not entered on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 若依鄭玄之說，廟有親稱，妻者言齊，豈或濫享。

translations.literal: If one follows Zheng Xuan's theory that temples have kinship designations and "wife" means equal standing, how could they enjoy sacrifice indiscriminately?
translations.idiomatic: If one follows Zheng Xuan—that temples name kinship and "wife" means equal rank—how could they share sacrifice at will?

sentences.zh: 且閟宮之德，周七非數，楊元之祀，晉八無傷。

translations.literal: Moreover, the virtue of the secluded palace—Zhou's seven was not a fixed number; sacrifice to Yang Yuan—Jin's eight does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, in the virtue of the inner palace Zhou's seven was never a rigid count, and Jin's eight for Yang Yuan does no injury to the rule.

sentences.zh: 今謂之七廟，而上唯六祀，使受命之君，流光之典不足。

translations.literal: Now it is called seven temples, yet above there are only six sacrifices—making the ruler who received the mandate and the enduring luminous rites insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: They call it seven temples, yet only six receive sacrifice above—so the founding sovereign and the lasting rites fall short.

sentences.zh: 若謂太祖未登，則昭穆之數何繼，斯故禮官所宜詳也。

translations.literal: If one says the Great Ancestor had not yet been enthroned in the temple, then how does the zhao-mu sequence continue—this is what ritual officials ought to examine in detail.
translations.idiomatic: If the Great Ancestor is said not yet to have taken his place, how is the zhao-mu order to be carried on? That is what the ritual officers should settle in full.

sentences.zh: 宋泰豫元年，明帝崩，博士周洽議：「權制：諒闇之內，不親奉四時祠。

translations.literal: Song Taizhi year 1, Mingdi died; erudite Zhou Qia proposed: "Provisional regulation: within mourning seclusion, one does not personally attend the four-season sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Taizhi 1, Mingdi died; erudite Zhou Qia argued: "By expedient rule: during mourning seclusion the ruler does not personally conduct the four seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」建元四年，尚書令王儉採晉中朝《諒闇議》奏曰：「權典旣行，喪禮斯奪，事興漢世，而源由甚遠。

translations.literal: " Jianyuan 4, Director Wang Jian drew on the Jin mid-dynasty Discussions on Mourning Seclusion and memorialized: "Once provisional statutes are in force, mourning rites are set aside; the practice arose in Han but its sources are very remote.
translations.idiomatic: " In Jianyuan 4, director Wang Jian took the Jin court's Discussions on Mourning Seclusion and submitted: "Once expedient law runs, mourning custom is suspended; the usage began in Han, but its roots lie far back.

sentences.zh: 殷宗諒闇，非有服之稱，周王卽吉，唯宴樂爲譏。

translations.literal: Yin Zong's mourning seclusion was not called wearing mourning; Zhou kings' assuming auspicious rites was reproached only for feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zong's seclusion was not styled as wearing mourning; Zhou kings' return to auspicious rites was faulted only for feasts and music.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，嗣君踰年卽位，則預朝會聘享焉。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: when the successor king takes the throne after a full year, he then participates in court audiences, missions, and tributary visits.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals mean that once the heir has reigned a full year he may join court, embassies, and guest rites.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》云『凡君卽位，卿出竝聘，踐修舊好』。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says, "Whenever a lord takes the throne, ministers go on joint missions to renew old friendship."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says, "When any lord succeeds, his ministers go abroad together on missions to renew old ties."

sentences.zh: 又云『諸侯卽位，小國聘焉，以繼好結信，謀事補闕，禮之大者』。

translations.literal: It also says, "When feudal lords take the throne, lesser states send missions—to continue friendship and bind trust, counsel on affairs and supply omissions: these are the greatest of rites."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "When feudal lords succeed, small states call on them to keep friendship, bind good faith, advise on business, and fill gaps—the greatest matters of ritual."

sentences.zh: 至於諒闇之內而圖婚，三年未終而吉禘，齊歸之喪不廢蒐，杞公之卒不徹樂，皆致譏貶，以明鑒戒。

translations.literal: As for plotting marriage within mourning seclusion, auspicious di before three years ended, Qi Gui's mourning without suspending the hunt, Duke Qi's death without withdrawing music—all drew reproach as clear warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage planned in seclusion, an auspicious di before three years were out, Qi Gui's mourning with the hunt still held, Duke Qi's death with music not stopped—all were censured as plain warnings.

sentences.zh: 自斯而談，朝聘蒸嘗之典，卒哭而備行，婚禘蒐樂之事，三載而後舉，通塞興廢，各有由然。

translations.literal: From this perspective, the norms of court audience, missions, and seasonal offerings are fully practiced after the end-of-wailing sacrifice; marriage, di, hunt, and music wait until after three years—whether open or blocked, rising or abolished, each has its reason.
translations.idiomatic: On this view, audiences, missions, and seasonal offerings resume after the end-of-wailing rite, while marriage, di, the hunt, and music wait until the third year—what is allowed or stopped, kept or dropped, each has its ground.

sentences.zh: 又案《大戴禮記》及《孔子家語》竝稱武王崩，成王嗣位，明年六月旣葬，周公冠成王而朝于祖，以見諸侯，命祝雍作頌。

translations.literal: Examining again, the Elder Dai's Record of Rites and the Family Discourse of Confucius both say King Wu died, King Cheng succeeded, the next year in the sixth month after burial the Duke of Zhou capped Cheng and led him to court at the ancestor to receive the feudal lords, ordering Zhu Yong to compose a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder Dai's Record of Rites and the Family Discourse of Confucius both say that when Wu died and Cheng succeeded, in the sixth month of the following year, after burial, the Duke of Zhou capped Cheng and led him to the ancestor's court to receive the lords, and ordered Zhu Yong to compose a hymn of praise.

sentences.zh: 襄十五年十一月『晉侯周卒』，十六年正月『葬晉悼公』。

translations.literal: Xiang year 15, eleventh month, "Marquis Zhou of Jin died"; year 16, first month, "Burial of Duke Dao of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: In Xiang 15, eleventh month, "the marquis of Jin, Zhou, died"; in the first month of the sixteenth year, "Duke Dao of Jin was buried."

sentences.zh: 平公旣卽位，『改服脩官，烝于曲沃』。

translations.literal: Duke Ping having taken the throne, "changed mourning garb and restored offices, performed yin at Quwo."
translations.idiomatic: Once Duke Ping had succeeded, he "changed out of mourning, restored the offices, and offered yin at Quwo."

sentences.zh: 《禮記曾子》問『孔子曰，天子崩，國君薨，則祝取羣廟之主而藏諸祖廟，禮也。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites, Zengzi asked: "Confucius said, when the Son of Heaven dies or a state lord perishes, the invoker takes the spirit tablets of all temples and stores them in the ancestor temple—this is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the Record of Rites, Zengzi asked: "Confucius said that when the Son of Heaven dies or a feudal lord perishes, the invoker takes the tablets of all shrines and keeps them in the ancestor temple—that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 卒哭成事，而後主各反其廟』。

translations.literal: After the end-of-wailing sacrifice completes the affair, then each tablet returns to its temple."
translations.idiomatic: When the end-of-wailing rite is finished, each tablet goes back to its own shrine."

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏傳》『凡君卒哭而祔，祔而後特祀於主，蒸嘗禘於廟』。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: "Whenever a lord, after end-of-wailing, performs fu; after fu, special sacrifice at the spirit lord; seasonal and di offerings at the temple."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: "When a lord has ended wailing he performs fu; after fu he offers specially to the spirit tablet; seasonal and di rites are at the temple."

sentences.zh: 先儒云『特祀於主者，特以喪禮奉新亡者至於寢，不同於古。

translations.literal: Former scholars said: "Special sacrifice at the lord means specially using mourning rites to bring the newly dead to the sleeping chamber—different from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars said: "Sacrifice at the spirit lord means bringing the newly dead to the sleeping chamber by mourning rite alone—not as in old custom.

sentences.zh: 蒸嘗禘於廟者，卒哭成事，羣廟之主，各反其廟。

translations.literal: Seasonal and di at the temple: when end-of-wailing completes, the tablets of all temples each return to their temple.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal and di rites at the temple mean that when wailing is done the tablets of every shrine return each to its place.

sentences.zh: 則四時之祭，皆卽吉也。

translations.literal: Then the four-season sacrifices are all upon assuming auspicious mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Then the four seasonal sacrifices are all held once auspicious mourning has begun.

sentences.zh: 三年喪畢，吉禘於廟，躋羣主以定新主也』。

translations.literal: When three-year mourning ends, auspicious di at the temple, elevating all lords to fix the new lord."
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year mourning is complete, an auspicious di at the temple raises all the tablets to set the new lord in place."

sentences.zh: 凡此諸義，皆著在經誥，昭乎方冊，所以晉、宋因循，同規前典，卒哭公除，親奉蒸嘗，率禮無違，因心允協。

translations.literal: All these meanings are set forth in classics and edicts, clear in written records—hence Jin and Song followed precedent, same norm as former statutes: after end-of-wailing public mourning is removed, personally attending seasonal offerings, observing rites without violation, conforming to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is written in the classics and royal pronouncements, plain in the records; that is why Jin and Song kept the old rule—after the end-of-wailing rite public mourning ends, the ruler attends the seasonal sacrifices in person, keeps the rites without breach, and acts as the heart allows.

sentences.zh: 爰至泰豫元年，禮官立議，不宜親奉，乃引『三年之制自天子達』。

translations.literal: Down to Taizhi year 1, ritual officials proposed one should not personally attend, citing "the three-year rule reaches from the Son of Heaven down."
translations.idiomatic: By Taizhi 1 the ritual officers argued against personal attendance, citing "the three-year rule runs from the Son of Heaven downward."

sentences.zh: 又據《王制》稱『喪三年不祭，唯祭天地社稷，越紼而行事』。

translations.literal: Again citing Royal Regulations: "In mourning three years do not sacrifice, except to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain—cross the mourning cord to conduct affairs."
translations.idiomatic: They also cited Royal Regulations: "For three years of mourning do not sacrifice, except to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain—step over the mourning cord to carry out other business."

sentences.zh: 曾不知自天子達，本在至情，旣葬釋除，事以權奪，委衰襲袞，孝享宜申，越紼之旨，事施未葬，卒哭之後，何紼可越？

translations.literal: They failed to understand that "from the Son of Heaven down" rests on utmost feeling; after burial mourning is released, affairs are set aside by expedient authority—laying aside hemp and donning brocade, filial offering should extend; the intent of crossing the cord applies before burial—after end-of-wailing, what cord could one cross?
translations.idiomatic: They did not see that "from the Son of Heaven down" springs from deepest feeling: after burial mourning is eased and business is suspended by expedient rule—putting off sackcloth and putting on court dress, filial sacrifice should go on; crossing the cord is for what is done before burial—after the end-of-wailing rite, what cord is left to cross?

sentences.zh: 復依范宣之難杜預，譙周之論士祭，竝非明據。

translations.literal: Again relying on Fan Xuan's critique of Du Yu and Qiao Zhou's discussion of scholar sacrifices—none are clear evidence.
translations.idiomatic: They leaned again on Fan Xuan's challenge to Du Yu and Qiao Zhou on the scholar's sacrifice—neither is solid proof.

sentences.zh: 晉武在喪，每欲存寧戚之懷，不全依諒闇之典，至於四時蒸嘗，蓋以哀疾未堪，非便頓改舊式。

translations.literal: Jin Wu in mourning always wished to preserve tranquil grief; he did not fully follow mourning-seclusion statutes—as for four-season offerings, it was because grief and illness made him unable, not convenience in abruptly changing old form.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi in mourning tried to keep a quiet, grieving heart and did not wholly follow seclusion law; as for the four seasonal offerings, he was too worn by grief and sickness to attend—not eager to overturn old custom at once.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，通儒碩學所歷多矣，守而弗革，義豈徒然。

translations.literal: Since Jiangzuo, great Confucians and senior scholars have passed through many reigns, keeping without reform—can the meaning be empty?
translations.idiomatic: Since the eastern court, leading scholars have seen many reigns and left the rule unchanged—the sense cannot be meaningless.

sentences.zh: 又且卽心而言，公卿大夫，則負扆親臨，三元告始，則朝會萬國，雖金石輟響，而簨簴充庭，情深於恒哀，而迹降於凡制，豈曰能安，國家故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, judging by the heart: for grandees he personally presides at the screen; at the three beginnings he holds court for ten thousand states—though bells and stones cease sound, yet reed pipes fill the court; feeling deeper than ordinary grief yet conduct lowered to ordinary regulation—not that he could be at ease, but because of the state.
translations.idiomatic: And as the heart would have it: for ministers and grandees he sits at the screen in person; at the three year-openings he holds court for all the realm—bells and stones may fall silent, yet pipes fill the hall; grief runs deeper than common mourning, yet outward practice sinks to ordinary rule—not that he is at peace, but because the state requires it.

sentences.zh: 宗廟蒸嘗，孝敬所先，寧容吉事備行，斯典獨廢。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple seasonal offerings are what filial reverence puts first—how could auspicious affairs all proceed while this rite alone be abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal sacrifice at the ancestral temple comes first in filial duty—how can every other auspicious act go forward while this alone is dropped?

sentences.zh: 就令必宜廢祭，則應三年永闕，乃復同之他故，有司攝禮，進退二三，彌乖典衷。

translations.literal: Even if sacrifice must be abolished, it should be absent the full three years—yet again they equated it with other reasons, officials acting by proxy, hesitating back and forth, ever more contrary to the ritual core.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice must be stopped, it should be stopped for the full three years—yet they mixed it with other excuses, had officers stand in, and wavered this way and that, straying further from the heart of the rite.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依舊親奉。

translations.literal: We hold one should follow old practice and attend personally.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal is that the old rule stand: the ruler should attend in person.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 永明九年正月，詔太廟四時祭，薦宣帝麪起餅、鴨；

translations.literal: Yongming 9, first month, edict for four-season sacrifice at the Great Temple: offer Emperor Xuan wheat noodles, raised cakes, and duck;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 9, first month, an edict fixed the Great Temple's four seasonal offerings: for Emperor Xuan, wheat noodles, raised cakes, and duck;

sentences.zh: 孝皇后筍、鴨卵、脯醬、炙白肉；

translations.literal: Empress Xiao bamboo shoots, duck eggs, cured sauces, and roasted white meat;
translations.idiomatic: for Empress Xiao, bamboo shoots, duck eggs, cured meats and sauces, and roasted white flesh;

sentences.zh: 高皇帝薦肉膾、葅羹；

translations.literal: High Emperor sliced raw meat and pickled broth;
translations.idiomatic: for the High Emperor, sliced raw meat and pickled broth;

sentences.zh: 昭皇后茗、粣、炙魚：皆所嗜也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao tea, glutinous cakes, and roasted fish—all foods they had loved.
translations.idiomatic: for Empress Zhao, tea, glutinous cakes, and roasted fish—each dish they had favored in life.

sentences.zh: 先是世祖夢太祖曰：「宋氏諸帝嘗在太廟，從我求食。

translations.literal: Earlier the Shizu dreamed the Great Ancestor said: "Song emperors were once in the Great Temple, begging food from me.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shizu dreamed that the Great Ancestor said: "Song's emperors used to be in the Great Temple, asking me for food.

sentences.zh: 可別爲吾祠。

translations.literal: You may set up a separate shrine for me."
translations.idiomatic: Set up a separate shrine for me."

sentences.zh: 」上乃敕豫章王妃庾氏四時還青溪宮舊宅，處內合堂，奉祠二帝二后，牲牢服章，用家人禮。

translations.literal: " The emperor then ordered the Princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu, each season to return to the old residence at Qingxi Palace, dwell in the inner combined hall, and maintain sacrifice to two emperors and two empresses, with victims, regalia, and insignia using family rites.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered the Princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu, to return each season to the old Qingxi Palace residence, keep the inner combined hall, and offer sacrifice to two emperors and two empresses with victims, dress, and insignia by household rite.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢氏之廟，徧在郡國，求祀已瀆，緣情又疏。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Han lineage temples spread through commanderies and kingdoms; seeking sacrifice had already become profane, and following affection was also lax.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Han ancestral temples stood in every commandery and kingdom; eager sacrifice had grown profane, and affectionate observance had grown thin.

sentences.zh: 重檐閟寢，不可兼建，故前儒抗議，謂之遷毀。

translations.literal: Double eaves and sealed inner chambers cannot be built together everywhere; hence former scholars protested and called it relocate-and-destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Double-eaved halls with sealed inner chambers cannot be built everywhere; earlier scholars protested and called the practice "relocate and destroy."

sentences.zh: 光武入纂，南頓君已上四世，別祠舂陵。

translations.literal: When Guangwu took the succession, for the four generations above the Lord of Nandun, separate shrines were set up at Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu took the throne, four generations above the Lord of Nandun received separate worship at Chunling.

sentences.zh: 建武三年幸舂陵園廟是也。

translations.literal: The Jianwu year 3 visit to the Chunling garden temple was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: His Jianwu year 3 visit to the Chunling garden temple was one such case.

sentences.zh: 張衡《南都賦》曰『清廟肅以微微』。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, Rhapsody on the Southern Capital, says 『The clear temple is solemn, subtly humming.』
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Southern Capital says: 『The clear temple is solemn, softly humming.』

sentences.zh: 明帝至于章、和，每幸章陵，輙祠舊宅。

translations.literal: From Mingdi through Zhang and He, each time they visited Zhangling they at once sacrificed at the old residence.
translations.idiomatic: From Mingdi through the Zhang and He emperors, each visit to Zhangling meant sacrifice at the old house.

sentences.zh: 建安末，魏氏立宗廟，皆在鄴都。

translations.literal: At the end of Jian'an, Wei established the lineage temple—all at Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jian'an, Wei set up the lineage temple—all at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏文黃初二年，洛廟未成，親祠武帝於建始殿，用家人禮。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu year 2: the Luoyang temple was not yet complete; he personally sacrificed to Emperor Wu at Jianshi Hall, using family domestic ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu year 2 of Wei Wendi: the Luoyang temple was unfinished, so he sacrificed in person to Emperor Wu in Jianshi Hall with family domestic rite.

sentences.zh: 世祖發漢明之夢，肇祀故宮，孝享旣申，義合前典，亦一時之盛也。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor, taking Han Mingdi's dream as his model, first sacrificed at the former palace; filial feasting was already carried out, the meaning matching former canon—it was also a splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder Emperor, recalling Han Mingdi's dream, first sacrificed at the former palace; filial feasting was fulfilled and matched ancient canon—a splendor of the age.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，太常丞何諲之議：「今祭有生魚一頭，干魚五頭。

translations.literal: Yongming year 6, Chamberlain for Ceremonials aide He Yinzhi argued: 「Today's sacrifice uses one live fish and five dried fish.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming year 6, ceremonial aide He Yinzhi argued: 「Today's offering uses one live fish and five dried fish.

sentences.zh: 《少牢饋食禮》云『司士升魚腊膚魚，用鮒十有五』。

translations.literal: The Lesser Stallion Feeding Rite says 『The steward presents fish, cured meat, and skin fish, using fifteen crucian carp.』
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Stallion Feeding Rite says: 『The steward presents fish, cured meat, and skin-on fish—fifteen crucian carp.』

sentences.zh: 上旣云『腊』，下必是『鮮』。

translations.literal: Since above it says 「cured,」 below must be 「fresh.」
translations.idiomatic: Since the text above says 「cured,」 what follows must be 「fresh.」

sentences.zh: 其數宜同。

translations.literal: The numbers should match.
translations.idiomatic: The counts should match.

sentences.zh: 稱『膚』足知鱗革無毀。

translations.literal: Calling it 「skin」 is enough to know scales and hide are undamaged.
translations.idiomatic: The word 「skin」 alone shows scales and hide were left intact.

sentences.zh: 《記》云『槁魚曰商祭，鮮曰脡祭』。

translations.literal: The Record says 『Dried fish is called shang offering; fresh is called tiao offering.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 『Dried fish is a shang offering; fresh fish is a tiao offering.』

sentences.zh: 鄭注『商，量；

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary: 「Shang means measured;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses: 「Shang means cut to measure;

sentences.zh: 脡，直也』。

translations.literal: tiao means straight.」
translations.idiomatic: tiao means left whole.」

sentences.zh: 尋『商』旨裁截，『脡』義在全。

translations.literal: Examining 「shang,」 the intent is cutting; 「tiao」 means wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: 「Shang」 implies cutting; 「tiao」 implies keeping the fish whole.

sentences.zh: 賀循《祭義》猶用魚十五頭。

translations.literal: He Xun's Meaning of Sacrifice still used fifteen fish.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun's Meaning of Sacrifice still prescribed fifteen fish.

sentences.zh: 今鮮頓刪約，槁皆全用。

translations.literal: Today fresh fish is sharply reduced, while dried fish are all used whole.
translations.idiomatic: Today fresh fish is cut back sharply, while every dried fish is used whole.

sentences.zh: 謂宜鮮、槁各二頭，槁微斷首尾，示存古義。

translations.literal: I hold that fresh and dried should be two each; dried fish should be slightly cut at head and tail, to show preservation of ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold fresh and dried should be two each, with dried fish lightly trimmed at head and tail to preserve the ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 」國子助教桑惠度議：「《記》稱尚玄酒而俎腥魚。

translations.literal: 」National University assistant instructor Sang Huidu argued: 「The Record says they prize dark liquor and set out fish raw on the stand.
translations.idiomatic: 」National University assistant instructor Sang Huidu argued: 「The Record prizes dark liquor and sets raw fish on the stand.

sentences.zh: 玄酒不容多，鮮魚理宜約。

translations.literal: Dark liquor cannot be plentiful; fresh fish should likewise be sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Dark liquor cannot be offered in quantity; fresh fish should likewise be few.

sentences.zh: 干魚五頭者，以其旣加人功，可法於五味，以象酒之五齊也。

translations.literal: The five dried fish—since human labor has already been added—may model the five flavors, symbolizing the five stages of liquor.
translations.idiomatic: Five dried fish—because human labor has been added—may stand for the five flavors and mirror the five stages of brew.

sentences.zh: 今欲鮮、槁各雙，義無所法。

translations.literal: Now wishing fresh and dried each in pairs, there is no model in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: To set fresh and dried at two each now has no precedent in meaning.

sentences.zh: 」諲之議不行。

translations.literal: 」He Yinzhi's proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 」He Yinzhi's proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔故太宰褚淵、故太尉王儉、故司空柳世隆、驃騎大將軍王敬則、鎮東大將軍陳顯達、故鎮東將軍李安民六人，配饗太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: Year 10, an edict ordered the late Grand Tutor Chu Yuan, late Grand Marshal Wang Jian, late Minister of Works Liu Shilong, Valiant Cavalry General Wang Jingze, General Who Pacifies the East Chen Xianda, and late General Who Pacifies the East Li Anmin—six men—to share paired sacrifice in the Taizu temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10: an edict enshrined the late grand tutor Chu Yuan, late grand marshal Wang Jian, late minister of works Liu Shilong, valiant cavalry general Wang Jingze, general who pacifies the east Chen Xianda, and late general who pacifies the east Li Anmin—six men—to share sacrifice at the Taizu temple court.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何諲之議「功臣配饗，累行宋世，檢其遺事，題列坐位，具書贈官爵謚及名，文不稱主，便是設板也。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Yinzhi argued: 「Meritorious ministers' paired sacrifice has accumulated practice since Song; checking surviving affairs, they list seats, fully writing posthumous offices, titles, and names—the text does not say 「lord,」 and that is setting up a board.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Yinzhi argued: 「Paired sacrifice for meritorious ministers was long practice under Song. Surviving records list seats and fully record posthumous offices, titles, and names; because the text never says 「lord,」 it is only a seated board.

sentences.zh: 《白虎通》云『祭之有主，孝子以繫心也』。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Discussion says 『Sacrifice has a spirit-lord; filial sons use it to tether the heart.』
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Discussion says: 『Sacrifice has a spirit-lord; the filial son uses it to bind his heart.』

sentences.zh: 揆斯而言，升配廟廷，不容有主。

translations.literal: Weighing this statement, ascending to share the temple court cannot allow a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing that line, enshrinement in the temple court cannot admit a spirit-lord.

sentences.zh: 宋時板度，旣不復存，今之所制，大小厚薄如尚書召板，爲得其衷。

translations.literal: Song-era board dimensions no longer survive; what is made today—size and thickness like the Masters of Writing summons board—hits the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Song board sizes no longer survive; today's boards, sized and thick like a Masters of Writing summons, strike the right measure.

sentences.zh: 」有司攝太廟舊人亦云見宋功臣配饗坐板，與尚書召板相似，事見儀注。

translations.literal: 」The relevant offices, through acting temple veterans, also said they had seen Song meritorious ministers' paired-sacrifice seat boards, similar to Masters of Writing summons boards; the matter appears in the ritual records.
translations.idiomatic: 」Acting through veteran temple staff, the relevant offices also reported Song paired-sacrifice seat boards for meritorious ministers, similar to Masters of Writing summons boards—the matter is in the ritual records.

sentences.zh: 十一年，右僕射王晏、吏部尚書徐孝嗣、侍中何胤奏：「故太子祔太廟，旣無先准。

translations.literal: Year 11, Right Vice Director Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel Xu Xiaosi, and Attendant Counsellor He Yin memorialized: 「The deceased crown prince's enshrinement in the ancestral temple has no prior precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Year 11: right vice director Wang Yan, minister of personnel Xu Xiaosi, and attendant counsellor He Yin memorialized: 「Enshrining the late crown prince in the ancestral temple has no earlier standard.

sentences.zh: 檢宋元后故事，太尉行禮，太子拜伏與太尉俱。

translations.literal: Checking Song Yuan empresses' precedents, the Grand Marshal performed the rite; the crown prince bowed prostrate together with the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Song precedents for Yuan empresses show the grand marshal performing the rite while the crown prince bowed prostrate beside him.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，依擬前典。

translations.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate, following and modeling former canon.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly propose following former canon.

sentences.zh: 太常主廟位，太尉執禮祔，太孫拜伏，皆與之俱。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain for Ceremonials presides over temple positions; the Grand Marshal carries out the enshrinement rite; the imperial grandson bows prostrate—all together with him.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain for ceremonials should preside over temple stations, the grand marshal perform the enshrinement, and the imperial grandson bow prostrate—all together with him.

sentences.zh: 正禮旣畢，陰室之祭，太孫宜親自進奠。

translations.literal: When the proper rite is finished, for the inner-chamber sacrifice the imperial grandson should personally advance the offering.
translations.idiomatic: When the main rite ends, for the inner-chamber offering the imperial grandson should advance the sacrifice in person.

translations.literal: 」An edict said 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict said: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 建武二年，有司奏景懿后遷登新廟車服之儀。

translations.literal: Jianwu year 2, the relevant offices memorialized on the ritual carriages and dress for Empress Jingyi's transfer to the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu year 2: the relevant offices memorialized on carriages and regalia when Empress Jingyi was moved to the new temple.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議曰：「《周禮》王之六服，大裘爲上，袞冕次之。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi argued: 「The Rites of Zhou: the king's six garments—great fur robe is highest, dragon robe and cap next.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi argued: 「The Rites of Zhou ranks the king's six garments with the great fur robe highest and the dragon robe and cap next.

sentences.zh: 五車，玉輅爲上，金輅次之。

translations.literal: Of five carriages, the jade chariot is highest and the gold chariot next.
translations.idiomatic: Of five carriages, the jade chariot ranks first and the gold chariot second.

sentences.zh: 皇后六服，褘衣爲上，褕翟次之。

translations.literal: The queen's six garments—hui robe highest, yu-di robe next.
translations.idiomatic: The queen's six garments place the hui robe first and the yu-di robe second.

sentences.zh: 首飾有三，副爲上，編次之。

translations.literal: Head ornaments have three grades—full formal headdress highest, braided headdress next.
translations.idiomatic: Head ornaments have three grades: full formal headdress first, braided headdress second.

sentences.zh: 五車，重翟爲上，厭翟次之。

translations.literal: Of five carriages, heavy-di is highest and yan-di next.
translations.idiomatic: Of five carriages, heavy-di ranks first and yan-di second.

sentences.zh: 上公無大裘玉輅，而上公夫人有副及褘衣，是以《祭統》云『夫人副褘立于東房』也。

translations.literal: Upper dukes lack great fur robe and jade chariot, yet an upper duke's consort has full formal headdress and hui robe—hence the Sacrificial Canon says 「the consort in full formal headdress and hui robe stands in the east chamber.」
translations.idiomatic: Upper dukes lack the great fur robe and jade chariot, yet an upper duke's consort wears full formal headdress and hui robe—hence the Sacrificial Canon: 「The consort in full formal headdress and hui robe stands in the east chamber.」

sentences.zh: 又鄭云『皇后六服，唯上公夫人亦有褘衣』。

translations.literal: Again Zheng says 「Of the queen's six garments, only an upper duke's consort also has the hui robe.」
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says: 「Among the queen's six garments, only an upper duke's consort may wear the hui robe.」

sentences.zh: 《詩》云『翟茀以朝』。

translations.literal: The Odes says 「di feather canopy for the morning audience.」
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: 「A di-feather canopy for the morning audience.」

sentences.zh: 鄭以翟茀爲厭翟，侯伯夫人入廟所乘。

translations.literal: Zheng takes the di-feather canopy as yan-di, what marquises' and earls' consorts ride when entering the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan reads the di-feather canopy as yan-di—the carriage marquises' and earls' consorts use when entering the temple.

sentences.zh: 今上公夫人副褘旣同，則重翟或不殊矣。

translations.literal: Now upper-duke consorts' full formal headdress and hui robe are already the same—then heavy-di may not differ either.
translations.idiomatic: If upper-duke consorts already match in full formal headdress and hui robe, heavy-di may not differ either.

sentences.zh: 況景皇懿后禮崇九命。

translations.literal: Moreover Empress Jingyi's ritual honors the nine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: All the more so for Empress Jingyi, whose ritual honors the nine ranks.

sentences.zh: 且晉朝太妃服章之禮，同於太后，宋代皇太妃唯無五牛旗爲異，其外侍官則有侍中、散騎常侍、黃門侍郎、散騎侍郎各二人，分從前後部，同於王者，內職則有女尚書、女長御各二人，棨引同於太后。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Jin the grand consort's regalia matched the empress dowager's; in Song the imperial grand consort differed only in lacking the five-ox banner—in attendants there were two palace attendants, two regular palace attendants, two gentlemen of the yellow gate, and two cavalier attendants each, divided front and rear like a king; inner offices had two ladies chief secretaries and two chief ladies of the long guard, with ceremonial staves like the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin a grand consort's dress and insignia matched an empress dowager's; in Song an imperial grand consort lacked only the five-ox banner—otherwise two palace attendants, two regular palace attendants, two gate gentlemen of the yellow gate, and two cavalier attendants each, split front and rear like a king's train; inside, two ladies chief secretaries and two chief ladies of the long guard, with ceremonial staves as for an empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 又魏朝之晉王，晉之宋王，竝置百官，擬於天朝。

translations.literal: Again, Wei's Prince of Jin and Jin's Prince of Song each established full offices modeled on the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince of Jin and Jin's Prince of Song each set up a full bureaucracy on the model of the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 至於晉文王終猶稱薨，而太上皇稱崩，則是禮加於王矣。

translations.literal: Yet when Prince Wen of Jin died he was still called "demised," while the retired emperor was called "collapsed"—ritual ranked above a prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wen of Jin died he was still styled "demised," but the retired emperor was styled "collapsed"—ritual that set him above a mere king.

sentences.zh: 故前議景皇后悉依近代皇太妃之儀，則侍衞陪乘竝不得異，后乘重翟，亦謂非疑也。

translations.literal: Thus when we earlier proposed that Empress Jing follow the recent imperial grand consort rite, escort and accompanying carriage could not differ; the empress riding the heavy pheasant carriage should likewise be beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When we earlier held that Empress Jing should follow the recent imperial grand consort rite, escort and accompanying carriage could not differ—and her riding the heavy pheasant carriage should be no less beyond question.

sentences.zh: 尋齊初移廟，宣皇神主乘金輅，皇帝親奉，亦乘金輅，先往行禮畢，仍從神主至新廟，今所宜依准也。

translations.literal: Recall at the start of Qi when the temple was moved: the Xuan Emperor's spirit tablet rode in the gold chariot, the emperor personally escorted in a gold chariot too—first going to perform the rite, then following the tablet to the new temple; that is what should be followed now.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qi, when the temple was moved, the Xuan Emperor's tablet rode in the gold chariot and the emperor escorted it in a gold chariot as well—first performing the rite, then following the tablet to the new temple. That is the precedent to follow.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court followed [this view].
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，有司議應廟見不？

translations.literal: Yongtai year 1, the relevant offices debated whether there should be a temple audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 the relevant offices debated whether a new ruler should perform a temple audience.

sentences.zh: 尚書令徐孝嗣議：「嗣君卽位，竝無廟見之文，蕃支纂業，乃有虔謁之禮。

translations.literal: Director Xu Xiaosi argued: 「When a successor takes the throne, none of the records mention temple audience; only when a collateral branch seized the succession was there a reverent visit ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xu Xiaosi argued: 「When an heir succeeds, the records nowhere prescribe a temple audience; only when a collateral line seized the throne was there a reverent visit.

sentences.zh: 」左丞蕭琛議：「竊聞祗見厥祖，義著商書，朝于武宮，事光晉冊。

translations.literal: 」Left vice director Xiao Chen argued: 「I have heard "reverently appear before your ancestor" in the Shang Documents, and "audience at the Martial Palace" shines in Jin annals.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Xiao Chen argued: 「The Shang Documents teach reverent appearance before one's ancestor; Jin annals glorify audience at the Martial Palace.

sentences.zh: 豈有正位居尊，繼業承天，而不虔覲祖宗，格于太室。

translations.literal: How could one rightly occupy the supreme place, inherit the mandate, and not reverently behold the ancestors, attaining the Grand Chamber?
translations.idiomatic: How can one sit in the supreme seat, inherit Heaven's mandate, and not reverently behold the ancestors in the Grand Chamber?

sentences.zh: 《毛詩周頌》篇曰『《烈文》，成王卽政，諸侯助祭也』。

translations.literal: The Mao Odes, Zhou Eulogia, say: 「Lie Wen: when King Cheng took government, the feudal lords assisted at sacrifice.」
translations.idiomatic: The Mao Odes, Zhou Eulogia, say: 「Lie Wen: when King Cheng took the government, the feudal lords assisted at sacrifice.」

sentences.zh: 鄭注云『新王卽政，必以朝享之禮祭於祖考，告嗣位也』。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: 「When a new king takes government, he must use the court-audience sacrifice at the ancestors to announce succession.」
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says: 「A new king must worship his ancestors with the court-audience rite to announce his succession.」

sentences.zh: 又篇曰『《閔予小子》，嗣王朝廟也』。

translations.literal: Again the odes say: 「Min Yu the Lad—succession king's court temple audience.」
translations.idiomatic: Another ode says: 「Min Yu the Lad—the succession king's court temple audience.」

sentences.zh: 鄭注云『嗣王者，謂成王也。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: 「Succession king means King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says: 「Succession king means King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 除武王之喪，將始卽政，朝於廟也』。

translations.literal: Having ended mourning for King Wu, about to take government, he had audience at the temple.」
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for King Wu ended and he was about to take the government, he had audience at the temple.」

sentences.zh: 則隆周令典，煥炳經記，體嫡居正，莫若成王。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou's glorious canonical models shine in the classics; for legitimate succession none surpasses Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's glorious canonical models shine in the classics; for legitimate succession none surpasses King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 又二漢由太子而嗣位者，西京七主，東都四帝，其昭、成、哀、和、從五君，竝皆謁廟，文存漢史，其惠、景、武、元、明、章六君，前史不載謁事，或是偶有闕文，理無異說。

translations.literal: Of Han emperors who succeeded as crown prince—seven in the Western Capital, four in the Eastern—Zhao, Cheng, Ai, He, and Cong all visited the temple, attested in Han histories; Hui, Jing, Wu, Yuan, Ming, and Zhang lack recorded visits in earlier histories—perhaps occasional lacunae, not a differing doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han emperors who succeeded as crown prince—seven in the Western Capital, four in the Eastern—Zhao, Cheng, Ai, He, and Cong all visited the temple, as Han histories record; Hui, Jing, Wu, Yuan, Ming, and Zhang have no visit recorded in earlier histories—perhaps lacunae, not a different rule.

sentences.zh: 議者乃云先在儲宮，已經致敬，卒哭之後，卽親奉時祭，則是廟見，故無別謁之禮。

translations.literal: Some argue that while in the heir apparent's palace they already paid reverence, and after the end of wailing they personally conducted seasonal sacrifice—that was temple audience, so no separate visit was needed.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that in the heir apparent's palace they already paid reverence, and after wailing ended they personally led seasonal sacrifice—that was the temple audience, so no separate visit is required.

sentences.zh: 竊以爲不然。

translations.literal: I hold that is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I do not think so.

sentences.zh: 儲后在宮，亦從郊祀，若謂前虔可兼後敬，開元之始，則無假復有配天之祭矣。

translations.literal: While in the palace the heir apparent also joined suburban sacrifice; if prior piety could cover later reverence, at the opening of rule there would be no need again for Heaven-matching sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace the heir apparent also joined suburban sacrifice; if earlier piety could stand for later reverence, at the start of a reign there would be no need for the Heaven-matching sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 若以親奉時祭，仍爲廟見者，自漢及晉，支庶嗣位，竝皆謁廟，旣同有蒸嘗，何爲獨脩繁禮？

translations.literal: If personally conducting seasonal sacrifice still counts as temple audience, from Han through Jin every collateral succession visited the temple—since they already had steam offerings, why alone pursue an elaborate rite?
translations.idiomatic: If leading seasonal sacrifice still counts as temple audience, then from Han through Jin every collateral successor visited the temple—yet they already had seasonal offerings; why add a separate elaborate rite?

sentences.zh: 且晉成帝咸和元年改號以謁廟，咸康元年加元服，又更謁。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin Chengdi in Xianhe 1 changed the era title and visited the temple; in Xiankang 1 he received the capping and visited again.
