translations.idiomatic: Jin Chengdi in Xianhe 1 changed the era title and visited the temple; in Xiankang 1, after his capping, he visited again.

sentences.zh: 夫時非異主，猶不疑二禮相因，況位隔君臣，而追以一謁兼敬。

translations.literal: When it was not a different lord, two rites in succession was not doubted—how much less when ruler and subject differ in rank should one visit be stretched to serve both ends?
translations.idiomatic: When the same ruler performed two rites in succession, no one doubted it—how much less, when sovereign and subject differ in rank, can one visit do double duty?

sentences.zh: 宜遠纂周、漢之盛範，近黜晉、宋之乖義，展誠一廟，駿奔萬國。

translations.literal: We should follow far off Zhou and Han's great examples and reject near Jin and Song's mistaken practice—unfold sincerity in one temple, gallop to the ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: We should take Zhou and Han's great examples from afar and set aside Jin and Song's recent errors—unfold sincerity in one temple and hasten to the ten thousand states.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: 」The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，兼祠部郎何佟之議：「案《禮記郊特牲》『社祭土而主陰氣也，君南向於北墉下，答陰之義也』。

translations.literal: Yongming 11, Acting Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi argued: 「The Record of Rites, Te Yi, says: "Soil sacrifice honors earth and presides over yin qi; the lord faces south below the north embankment, answering yin's meaning."」
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 11, Acting Director He Tongzhi argued: 「The Record of Rites, Te Yi, says: "Soil sacrifice honors earth and presides over yin qi; the lord faces south below the north embankment, answering yin."」

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『答猶對也』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: 「Answer means respond.」
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 「Answer means to respond.」

sentences.zh: 『北墉，社內北墻也』。

translations.literal: 「North embankment—the north wall within the altar.」
translations.idiomatic: 「North embankment: the north wall inside the altar.」

sentences.zh: 王肅云『陰氣北向，故君南向以答之。

translations.literal: Wang Su says: 「Yin qi faces north, so the lord faces south to answer it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su says: 「Yin qi faces north, so the lord faces south to answer it.

sentences.zh: 答之爲言是相對之稱』。

translations.literal: The word "answer" is a term for facing each other.」
translations.idiomatic: The word answer means facing each other.」

sentences.zh: 知古祭社，北向設位，齋官南向明矣。

translations.literal: Thus in ancient soil sacrifice the seat faced north and the fast-official faced south—clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in ancient soil sacrifice the spirit faced north and the fast-official faced south—that much is clear.

sentences.zh: 近代相承，帝社南向，太社及稷竝東向，而齋官位在帝社壇北，西向，於神背後行禮。

translations.literal: In recent succession the imperial soil altar faces south, Great Soil and Grain both east; the fast-official stands north of the imperial altar facing west, performing rite behind the spirit's back.
translations.idiomatic: In recent practice the imperial soil altar faces south, Great Soil and Grain both east, while the fast-official stands north of the imperial mound facing west—performing rite behind the spirit's back.

sentences.zh: 又名稷爲稷社，甚乖禮意。

translations.literal: Also calling Grain "Grain Soil" greatly violates ritual meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Calling Grain "Grain Soil" badly violates ritual meaning.

sentences.zh: 乃未知失在何時，原此理當未久。

translations.literal: When the error arose is unknown; tracing the principle, it cannot be long ago.
translations.idiomatic: When the mistake began is unknown, but the principle cannot have been wrong for long.

sentences.zh: 竊以皇齊改物，禮樂惟新，中國之神，莫貴於社，若遂仍前謬，懼虧盛典。

translations.literal: I hold that Great Qi has renewed things and ritual and music are made new; among the state's spirits none is nobler than Soil—if we still follow the former error, I fear the great rite will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi has renewed the realm and ritual and music are new; among the state's spirits none outranks Soil—if we keep the old error, the great rite will suffer.

sentences.zh: 謂二社，語其義則殊，論其神則一，位竝宜北向。

translations.literal: I hold that the two soils differ in name but are one spirit—their positions should both face north.
translations.idiomatic: The two soils differ in name but are one spirit—both positions should face north.

sentences.zh: 稷若北向，則成相背。

translations.literal: If Grain faced north it would end up back to back.
translations.idiomatic: If Grain faced north the two would stand back to back.

sentences.zh: 稷是百穀之總神，非陰氣之主，宜依先東向。

translations.literal: Grain is the general spirit of the hundred grains, not master of yin qi—it should as before face east.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is the general spirit of the hundred grains, not lord of yin qi—it should remain east-facing.

sentences.zh: 齋官立社壇東北，南向立，東爲上，諸執事西向立，南爲上。

translations.literal: The fast-official should stand northeast of the altar facing south; east is upper; all officiants stand west-facing, south upper.
translations.idiomatic: The fast-official should stand northeast of the altar facing south—east is the place of honor; officiants stand west-facing, with south as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 稷依禮無兼稱，今若欲尊崇，正可名爲太稷耳，豈得謂爲稷社邪？

translations.literal: By ritual Grain has no compound title; if one wishes to honor it, it may only be called Great Grain—how can it be called Grain Soil?
translations.idiomatic: Ritual gives Grain no compound name; if one wishes to honor it, call it only Great Grain—how can it be called Grain Soil?

sentences.zh: 臘祠太社日近，案奏事御，改定儀注。」

translations.literal: The winter great-soil sacrifice nears; submit to the throne for revising the protocol.」
translations.idiomatic: The winter great-soil sacrifice is near; I submit this for the throne to revise the protocol.」

sentences.zh: 儀曹稱治禮學士議曰：「《郊特牲》又云『君之南向，答陽也，臣之北向，答君也』。

translations.literal: The Rituals Office reported that ritual scholars argued: 「Te Yi also says "the lord's facing south answers yang; ministers' facing north answer the lord."」
translations.idiomatic: The Rituals Office reported that ritual scholars argued: 「Te Yi also says, "The lord faces south to answer yang; ministers face north to answer the lord."」

sentences.zh: 若以陽氣在南，則位應向北，陰氣在北，則宜向南。

translations.literal: If yang qi is in the south, position should face north; if yin qi is in the north, one should face south.
translations.idiomatic: If yang qi lies in the south, seats should face north; if yin qi lies in the north, they should face south.

sentences.zh: 今南北二郊，一限南向，皇帝黑瓚階東西向，故知壇墠無繫於陰陽，設位寧拘於南北。

translations.literal: Today both southern and northern suburbs are limited to south-facing; the emperor at the black libation stair faces east—thus the altar platform is not bound to yin and yang, and placing seats need not be fixed to north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Today both southern and northern suburbs face south, and at the black libation stair the emperor faces east—so the mound is not tied to yin and yang, and seat-direction need not be fixed to north and south.

sentences.zh: 羣神小祠，類皆限南面，薦饗之時，北向行禮，蓋欲申靈祇之尊，表求幽之義。

translations.literal: Minor cults of the host of spirits are mostly limited to south-facing; at offering time ritual is performed north-facing—probably to extend the spirits' honor and show seeking the hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Minor cults of the host of spirits are mostly south-facing; at offering time the rite is performed north-facing—to extend the spirits' honor and show seeking what is hidden.

sentences.zh: 魏世秦靜使社稷別營，稱自漢以來，相承南向。

translations.literal: In Wei Qin Jing had Soil and Grain separately built, saying from Han onward succession faced south.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Qin Jing had Soil and Grain built separately, saying that from Han onward the practice faced south.

sentences.zh: 漢之於周，世代未遠，鄗上頹基，商丘餘樹，猶應尚存，迷方失位，未至於此，通儒達識，不以爲非。

translations.literal: Han from Zhou was not many generations distant; ruined foundations at Hao, remaining trees at Shangqiu ought still to exist—confusion of direction could not reach this; learned men did not deem it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Han was not far from Zhou; ruined foundations at Hao and remaining trees at Shangqiu should still have been there—direction could not have been lost to this degree, and learned men did not treat it as wrong.

sentences.zh: 庾蔚之昔已有此議，後徐爰、周景遠竝不同，仍舊不改。」

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi long ago had this argument; later Xu Ai and Zhou Jingyuan both disagreed and left the old practice unchanged.」
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi argued this long ago; later Xu Ai and Zhou Jingyuan both disagreed, and the old practice was left unchanged.」

sentences.zh: 佟之議：「來難引君南向答陽，臣北向答君。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi argued: 「The objection cites the lord facing south answering yang, ministers north answering the lord.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi argued: 「The objection cites the lord facing south to answer yang and ministers north to answer the lord.

sentences.zh: 敢問答之爲言，爲是相對？

translations.literal: May I ask—in speaking of "answer," does it mean facing each other?
translations.idiomatic: May I ask: when we speak of "answer," does it mean facing each other?

sentences.zh: 爲是相背？

translations.literal: Or does it mean facing away from each other?
translations.idiomatic: Or does it mean turning their backs to one another?

sentences.zh: 相背則社位南向，君亦南向，可如來議。

translations.literal: If they face away, then the Soil position faces south and the lord also faces south—as your objection would allow.
translations.idiomatic: If "answer" means back to back, the Soil seat faces south and the lord faces south too—exactly as your objection would have it.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》云『臣之北向答君』。

translations.literal: The Suburban Sacrifice says 『ministers face north to answer the lord.』
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifice says: 『Ministers face north to answer the lord.』

sentences.zh: 復是君背臣。

translations.literal: That again means the lord has his back to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: But that again puts the lord's back to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 今言君南臣北，向相稱答，則君南不得稱答矣，《記》何得云祭社君南向之答陰邪？

translations.literal: Now you say lord south and ministers north, facing each other in mutual answer—then facing south cannot be called "answer"; how can the Record say that in sacrificing to Soil the lord faces south to answer yin?
translations.idiomatic: You say the lord faces south and ministers north, mutually answering face to face—then the lord's southward stance is not "answering" at all; how can the Record say that at the Soil sacrifice the lord faces south to answer yin?

sentences.zh: 社果同向，則君亦宜西向，何故在社南向？

translations.literal: If Soil truly faced the same direction, the lord should also face west—why does he face south at Soil?
translations.idiomatic: If Soil and the lord truly shared one direction, the lord should face west as well—why does he face south at the Soil altar?

sentences.zh: 在郊西向邪？

translations.literal: Does he face west in the suburbs?
translations.idiomatic: Does he face west at the suburban altar?

sentences.zh: 解則不然，《記》云，君之南向答陽，此明朝會之時，盛陽在南，故君南向對之，猶聖人南面而聽，向明而治之義耳，寧是祈祀天地之日乎？

translations.literal: That reading will not do. The Record says the lord's facing south answers yang—this concerns morning court, when full yang lies in the south, so the lord faces south toward it, as when the sage faces south to listen and governs toward the light—not the day of praying to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: That will not stand. The Record's "lord faces south to answer yang" describes morning court: yang at its height in the south, so the lord turns south toward it—as the sage faces south to listen and rule toward the light—not the day of offering to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 知祭社北向，君答故南向，祀天南向，君答宜北向矣。

translations.literal: Thus we know: at Soil sacrifice Soil faces north, so the lord answers by facing south; at Heaven sacrifice Heaven faces south, so the lord should answer by facing north.
translations.idiomatic: So at the Soil rite the altar faces north and the lord answers by facing south; at the Heaven rite the altar faces south and the lord should answer by facing north.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝黑瓚階東西向者，斯蓋始入之別位，兆接對之時也。

translations.literal: Today the emperor at the black libation stair on the east faces west—that is simply the separate position at first entry, the moment of omen and initial encounter.
translations.idiomatic: Today the emperor west-facing at the black libation stair on the east is only the separate station at first entry—the moment of omen and first encounter.

sentences.zh: 案《記》云『社所以神地之道也』。

translations.literal: Examining the Record, it says 『Soil is how one gives spirit to the way of earth.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 『Soil is how the way of earth is given spirit.』

sentences.zh: 又云『社祭土而主陰氣』。

translations.literal: It also says 『Soil sacrifice honors earth and presides over yin qi.』
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 『The Soil sacrifice honors earth and presides over yin qi.』

sentences.zh: 又云『不用命，戮于社』。

translations.literal: It also says 『Those who do not obey orders are executed at Soil.』
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 『Those who disobey orders are put to death at Soil.』

sentences.zh: 孔安國云『社主陰，陰主殺』。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said 『Soil presides over yin; yin presides over killing.』
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo said: 『Soil is lord of yin, and yin is lord of killing.』

sentences.zh: 傳曰『日蝕，伐鼓于社』。

translations.literal: The Commentary says 『At an eclipse of the sun, beat the drum at Soil.』
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: 『When the sun is eclipsed, beat the drum at Soil.』

sentences.zh: 杜預云『責羣陰也』。

translations.literal: Du Yu said 『This rebukes the host of yin.』
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said: 『This is to rebuke the host of yin.』

sentences.zh: 社主陰氣之盛，故北向設位，以本其義耳。

translations.literal: Soil presides over the fullness of yin qi; therefore its seat is set north-facing, to root the rite in its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Soil is lord of yin qi at its height; that is why its seat faces north—to ground the rite in its own meaning.

sentences.zh: 餘祀雖亦地祇之貴，而不主此義，故位向不同。

translations.literal: Other sacrifices, though they too honor noble earth spirits, do not preside over this meaning, so their seat-directions differ.
translations.idiomatic: Other rites honor earth spirits of rank, but not with this meaning, so their orientations differ.

sentences.zh: 不得見餘陰祀不北向，便謂社應南向也。

translations.literal: One cannot see that other yin sacrifices do not face north and therefore conclude that Soil ought to face south.
translations.idiomatic: Because other yin rites do not all face north, one cannot infer that Soil should face south.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》祭社南向，君求幽，宜北向，而《記》云君南向，答陰之義，求幽之論不乖歟？

translations.literal: Examining the Rites of Zhou, Soil sacrifice faces south and the lord, seeking the hidden, should face north—yet the Record says the lord faces south, answering yin; are the two arguments on "seeking the hidden" not at odds?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou has the Soil altar south-facing and the lord, seeking what is hidden, north-facing—yet the Record has the lord south-facing to answer yin; do these two readings of "seeking the hidden" not conflict?

sentences.zh: 魏權漢社，社稷同營共門，稷壇在社壇北，皆非古制。

translations.literal: Wei Quan's Han Soil: Soil and Grain shared one compound and one gate, the Grain mound north of the Soil mound—all not ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Quan arranged the Han Soil altar, Soil and Grain shared one enclosure and one gate, with Grain north of Soil—none of it ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 後移宮南，自當如禮。

translations.literal: Later, when the palace moved south, it should naturally have followed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace was moved south, practice should have returned to the rites.

sentences.zh: 如靜此言，乃是顯漢社失周法，見漢世舊事。

translations.literal: If Jing's words are accepted, they only show that Han Soil departed from Zhou law and preserve Han-era custom.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes Jing's argument, it merely proves Han Soil broke Zhou law—and preserves a Han-era habit.

sentences.zh: 爾時祭社南向，未審出何史籍。

translations.literal: That Soil sacrifice then faced south—which historical work records it is still unclear.
translations.idiomatic: That the Soil sacrifice then faced south is not yet traced to any historical source.

sentences.zh: 就如議者靜所言是祭社位向仍漢舊法，漢又襲周成規，因而不改者，則社稷三座，竝應南向，今何改帝社南向，泰社及稷竝東向邪？」

translations.literal: Even if what petitioner Jing said were true—that the Soil altar's orientation still followed Han old practice, and Han in turn inherited Zhou's settled rule and left it unchanged—then all three Soil-and-Grain mounds should face south; why change only the emperor's Soil to south, while Great Soil and Grain both face east?」
translations.idiomatic: Even if Jing among the petitioners were right—that Soil's orientation still followed Han usage, and Han merely kept Zhou's rule unchanged—then all three mounds of the Soil-and-Grain cult should face south; why change only the emperor's Soil to the south while Great Soil and Grain both face east?」

sentences.zh: 治禮又難佟之，凡三往反。

translations.literal: The Director of Rituals again challenged Tongzhi; there were three exchanges in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Rituals challenged Tongzhi again, back and forth three times.

sentences.zh: 至建武二年，有司議：「治禮無的然顯據。

translations.literal: In Jianwu year 2 the responsible offices deliberated: 「The Director of Rituals has no clear and evident proof.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 2 the responsible offices reported: 「The Director of Rituals lacks clear, decisive evidence.

sentences.zh: 」佟之議乃行。

translations.literal: 」Tongzhi's proposal was then adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Tongzhi's proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，祠部郎何佟之奏：「案《周禮大宗伯》『以蒼璧禮天，黃琮禮地』。

translations.literal: Jianwu year 2, Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi memorialized: 「Examining the Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward: 『With the azure bi one honors Heaven; with the yellow cong one honors Earth.』
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu year 2, Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices He Tongzhi submitted: 「The Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward, says: 『With the azure bi one honors Heaven; with the yellow cong one honors Earth.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄又云『皆有牲幣，各放其器之色』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said 『Each has victims and silks, each matching the color of its vessel.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also said: 『Each has victims and silks, each matching its vessel's color.』

sentences.zh: 知禮天圓丘用玄犢，禮地方澤用黃牲矣。

translations.literal: Thus we know: honoring Heaven at the round mound uses the dark calf; honoring Earth at the square marsh uses the yellow victim.
translations.idiomatic: So Heaven at the round mound takes the dark calf, and Earth at the square marsh takes the yellow victim.

sentences.zh: 《牧人》云『凡陽祀用騂牲，陰祀用黝牲』。

translations.literal: The Keeper of Herds says 『For yang sacrifices use reddish victims; for yin sacrifices use black victims.』
translations.idiomatic: The Keeper of Herds says: 『Yang sacrifices use reddish victims; yin sacrifices use black victims.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『騂，赤；

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said 『Xing means red;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: 『Xing means red;

sentences.zh: 黝，黑也。

translations.literal: you means black.
translations.idiomatic: you means black.

sentences.zh: 陽祀，祭天南郊及宗廟。

translations.literal: Yang sacrifices: sacrificing to Heaven at the southern suburb and at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yang sacrifices are Heaven at the southern suburb and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 陰祀，祭地北郊及社稷』。

translations.literal: Yin sacrifices: sacrificing to Earth at the northern suburb and at Soil and Grain.』
translations.idiomatic: Yin sacrifices are Earth at the northern suburb and Soil and Grain.』

sentences.zh: 《祭法》云『燔柴於泰壇，祭天也。

translations.literal: The Law of Sacrifices says 『Burn firewood on the great mound—that is sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Law of Sacrifices says: 『Burn firewood on the great mound—that is sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 瘞埋於泰折，祭地也。

translations.literal: Bury offerings in the great fold—that is sacrificing to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Bury offerings in the great fold—that is sacrifice to Earth.

sentences.zh: 用騂犢』。

translations.literal: Use a reddish calf.』
translations.idiomatic: Use a reddish calf.』

sentences.zh: 鄭云『地，陰祀，用黝牲，與天俱用犢，故連言之耳』。

translations.literal: Zheng said 『Earth is a yin sacrifice and uses the black victim; because Heaven and Earth both use calves, the text links them in one phrase.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said: 『Earth is a yin sacrifice and uses the black victim; Heaven and Earth both use calves, so the text names them together.』

sentences.zh: 知此祭天地卽南北郊矣。

translations.literal: Thus we know these sacrifices to Heaven and Earth are indeed the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: So these rites to Heaven and Earth are the southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 今南北兩郊同用玄牲，又明堂、宗廟、社稷俱用赤，有違昔典。

translations.literal: Today both southern and northern suburbs use the dark victim, while Bright Hall, ancestral temple, and Soil and Grain all use red—contrary to former canon.
translations.idiomatic: Today both suburbs use the dark victim, while Bright Hall, ancestral temple, and Soil and Grain all use red—against ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 又鄭玄云『祭五帝於明堂，勾芒等配食』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said 『Sacrifice to the Five Emperors in Bright Hall, with Gou Mang and the rest as paired spirits.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also said: 『Sacrifice to the Five Emperors in Bright Hall, with Gou Mang and the rest as paired spirits.』

sentences.zh: 自晉以來，幷圜丘於南郊，是以郊壇列五帝勾芒等。

translations.literal: Since Jin, the round mound has been merged with the southern suburb, so the suburban altar arrays the Five Emperors, Gou Mang, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin the round mound was folded into the southern suburb, so the suburban altar arrays the Five Emperors, Gou Mang, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 今明堂祀五精，更闕五神之位，北郊祭地祇，而設重黎之坐，二三乖舛，懼虧盛則。」

translations.literal: Today Bright Hall sacrifices to the five essences but lacks seats for the five spirits; the northern suburb sacrifices to earth spirits yet sets out Chongli's seat—two or three contradictions, and I fear the great norm will be impaired.」
translations.idiomatic: Today Bright Hall honors the five essences but omits the five spirits' seats; the northern suburb honors earth spirits yet sets Chongli's place—several contradictions at once, and I fear the great norm will be diminished.」

sentences.zh: 前軍長史劉繪議：「《語》云『犂牛之子騂且角，雖欲勿用，山川其舍諸』。

translations.literal: Former Army Chief of Staff Liu Hui argued: 「The Analects says 『The plow-ox's calf is red and horned; though one wished not to use it, would the mountains and rivers let it go?』
translations.idiomatic: Former Army Chief of Staff Liu Hui argued: 「The Analects says: 『A plow-ox's calf, red and well-horned—even if you wished not to use it, would the mountains and rivers decline it?』

sentences.zh: 未詳山川合爲陰祀不？

translations.literal: It is unclear whether mountains and rivers count as yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear whether mountains and rivers should be classed as yin sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 若在陰祀，則與黝乖矣。」

translations.literal: If they are yin sacrifices, that conflicts with using black victims.」
translations.idiomatic: If they are yin sacrifices, that clashes with the rule for black victims.」

sentences.zh: 佟之又議：「《周禮》以天地爲大祀，四望爲次祀，山川爲小祀。

translations.literal: Tongzhi argued again: 「The Rites of Zhou treats Heaven and Earth as great sacrifices, the four expanses as secondary sacrifices, and mountains and rivers as minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi argued again: 「The Rites of Zhou ranks Heaven and Earth as great sacrifices, the four expanses as secondary, and mountains and rivers as minor.

sentences.zh: 周人尚赤，自四望以上牲色各依其方者，以其祀大，宜從本也。

translations.literal: The Zhou people honored red; from the four expanses upward each victim's color followed its quarter—because the sacrifice was great, it should follow its root.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou honored red; from the four expanses upward, each victim's color followed its direction—great rites should keep to their source.

sentences.zh: 山川以下，牲色不見者，以其祀小，從所尚也。

translations.literal: Below mountains and rivers, where sacrificial animal color is not specified—it is because the cult is minor; follow what is honored.
translations.idiomatic: For cults below the four quarters, where no victim-color is prescribed, the rite is minor and one follows the color the dynasty honors.

sentences.zh: 則《論》、《禮》二說，豈不合符？

translations.literal: Then do the Analects and Rites explanations not agree?
translations.idiomatic: Then do the Analects and the Rites not agree?

sentences.zh: 」參議爲允。

translations.literal: 」The joint deliberation found this acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: 」The joint deliberation approved.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed it.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，步兵校尉何佟之議曰：「蓋聞聖帝明王之治天下也，莫不尊奉天地，崇敬日月，故冬至祀天於圓丘，夏至祭地於方澤，春分朝日，秋分夕月，所以訓民事君之道，化下嚴上之義也。

translations.literal: Yongyuan year 1, Infantry Commandant He Tongzhi argued: 「I have heard that sage emperors and enlightened kings in ordering the realm never failed to honor Heaven and Earth and revere sun and moon; hence winter solstice sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound, summer solstice sacrifice to Earth at the Square Pond, spring equinox audience to the sun, autumn equinox audience to the moon—to teach the people in serving the ruler and to transform those below to revere those above.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 1, Infantry Commandant He Tongzhi argued: 「Sage kings who order the realm always honor Heaven and Earth and revere sun and moon—winter solstice Heaven at the Round Mound, summer solstice Earth at the Square Pond, spring equinox audience to the sun, autumn equinox audience to the moon—to teach subjects how to serve their ruler and to make inferiors revere superiors.

sentences.zh: 故禮云『王者必父天母地，兄日姊月。

translations.literal: Hence the Rites say 『The king must take Heaven as father, Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother, the moon as elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: 『The king must take Heaven as father, Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother, and the moon as elder sister.

sentences.zh: 』《周禮典瑞》云『王搢大圭，執鎮圭，藻藉五采五就以朝日』。

translations.literal: 』The Rites of Zhou, Jade Regalia, says 『The king inserts the great jade tablet, holds the regent jade tablet, with five-colored tassels in five sets to have audience with the sun.』
translations.idiomatic: 』The Rites of Zhou, Jade Regalia, says: 『The king inserts the great jade tablet and holds the regent jade tablet, with five-colored tassels in five sets, to have audience with the sun.』

sentences.zh: 馬融云『天子以春分朝日，秋分夕月』。

translations.literal: Ma Rong says 『The Son of Heaven on the spring equinox has audience with the sun, on the autumn equinox with the moon.』
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong says: 『The Son of Heaven has audience with the sun at the spring equinox and with the moon at the autumn equinox.』

sentences.zh: 《覲禮》『天子出拜日於東門之外』。

translations.literal: The Rites of Observation 『The Son of Heaven goes out to bow to the sun outside the east gate.』
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Observation: 『The Son of Heaven goes out to bow to the sun outside the east gate.』

sentences.zh: 盧植云『朝日以立春之日也』。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says 『Audience with the sun is on the day of Establishment of Spring.』
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi says: 『Audience with the sun is on the day of Establishment of Spring.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『端當爲冕，朝日春分之時也』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says 『"End" should read "cap"; audience with the sun is at the time of the spring equinox.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 『"End" should read "cap"; audience with the sun is at the spring equinox.』

sentences.zh: 《禮記朝事議》云『天子冕而執鎮圭，尺有二寸，率諸侯朝日於東郊，所以教尊尊也』。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, Discourse on Morning Audience, says 『The Son of Heaven in cap holds the regent jade tablet one foot two inches, leads the feudal lords to audience with the sun at the eastern suburb—to teach honoring what is honored.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites, Discourse on Morning Audience, says: 『The Son of Heaven, capped, holds the regent jade tablet one foot two inches long and leads the feudal lords to audience with the sun at the eastern suburb—to teach the order of honor.』

sentences.zh: 故鄭知此端爲冕也。

translations.literal: Hence Zheng knew this "end" meant the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zheng Xuan knew this "end" meant the cap.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》保傅云『三代之禮，天子春朝朝日，秋暮夕月，所以明有敬也』。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, Guardian and Tutor, says 『The rite of the Three Dynasties: the Son of Heaven in spring has morning audience with the sun, in autumn at dusk evening audience with the moon—to make clear that there is reverence.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites, Guardian and Tutor, says: 『In the rites of the Three Dynasties the Son of Heaven in spring had morning audience with the sun and in autumn at dusk evening audience with the moon—to show that reverence was due.』

sentences.zh: 而不明所用之定辰。

translations.literal: But it does not clarify the fixed day to be used.
translations.idiomatic: But it does not fix which day should be used.

sentences.zh: 馬、鄭云用二分之時，盧植云用立春之日。

translations.literal: Ma and Zheng say use the time of the two equinoxes; Lu Zhi says use the day of Establishment of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan say use the two equinoxes; Lu Zhi says use Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 佟之以爲日者太陽之精，月者太陰之精。

translations.literal: Tongzhi holds that the sun is the essence of great yang, the moon the essence of great yin.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi holds that the sun is the essence of great yang and the moon the essence of great yin.

sentences.zh: 春分陽氣方永，秋分陰氣向長。

translations.literal: At spring equinox yang qi is just waxing; at autumn equinox yin qi is growing long.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring equinox yang qi is waxing; at the autumn equinox yin qi is lengthening.

sentences.zh: 天地至尊用其始，故祭以二至，日月禮次天地，故朝以二分，差有理據，則融、玄之言得其義矣。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth, most honored, use their beginnings, hence sacrifice at the two solstices; sun and moon rites rank next to Heaven and Earth, hence audience at the two equinoxes—somewhat reasonable; then Rong and Xuan's words get the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth, supreme in honor, use their beginnings—hence sacrifice at the two solstices; sun and moon rites rank just below Heaven and Earth—hence audience at the two equinoxes. That has some reason; Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan have the right of it.

sentences.zh: 漢世則朝朝日，暮夕月。

translations.literal: Han used morning audience with the sun, evening audience with the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there was morning audience with the sun and evening audience with the moon.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝詔曰『《覲禮》天子拜日東門之外，反禮方明。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi's edict says 『The Rites of Observation: the Son of Heaven bows to the sun outside the east gate—contrary to the fangming rite.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi's edict says: 『The Rites of Observation has the Son of Heaven bow to the sun outside the east gate—contrary to the fangming rite.

sentences.zh: 《朝事議》曰天子冕而執鎮圭，率諸侯朝日於東郊。

translations.literal: Discourse on Morning Audience says the Son of Heaven in cap holds the regent jade tablet and leads the feudal lords to audience with the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourse on Morning Audience says the Son of Heaven, capped, holds the regent jade tablet and leads the feudal lords to audience with the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，蓋諸侯朝，天子祀方明，因率朝日也。

translations.literal: On this reading, probably when the feudal lords had audience the Son of Heaven sacrificed to fangming and thereby led the sun audience.
translations.idiomatic: On that reading, when the feudal lords had audience the Son of Heaven sacrificed to fangming and thereby led the sun audience.

sentences.zh: 漢改周法，羣公無四朝之事，故不復朝於東郊，得禮之變矣。

translations.literal: Han changed Zhou law; the mass of dukes had no four audiences, so they no longer had audience at the eastern suburb—that was a legitimate change in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Han changed Zhou practice; the feudal lords no longer held the four audiences, so audience at the eastern suburb ceased—a legitimate ritual change.

sentences.zh: 然旦夕常於殿下東向拜日，其禮太煩。

translations.literal: Yet morning and evening they constantly bowed to the sun east-facing below the hall—the rite was too burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Yet morning and evening they constantly bowed to the sun, east-facing below the hall—the rite was too burdensome.

sentences.zh: 今採周春分之禮，損漢日拜之儀，又無諸侯之事，無所出東郊，今正殿卽亦朝會行禮之庭也，宜常以春分於正殿之庭拜日。

translations.literal: Now adopt Zhou's spring equinox rite, reduce Han's daily sun-bowing ceremony; with no feudal lords' business there is no going out to the eastern suburb—the main hall is already the court where audience rites are performed; regularly on the spring equinox bow to the sun in the courtyard of the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Now take Zhou's spring-equinox rite and pare back Han's daily sun-bowing; with no feudal lords involved there is no need to go to the eastern suburb—the main hall is already the court for audience rites. On the spring equinox one should bow to the sun in the main hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 其夕月文不分明，其議奏』。

translations.literal: The text on evening audience with the moon is unclear; I submit this memorial for deliberation.』
translations.idiomatic: The wording on evening audience with the moon is unclear; I submit this memorial.』

sentences.zh: 魏祕書監薛循請論云『舊事朝日以春分，夕月以秋分。

translations.literal: Wei Secretary Director Xue Xun's submitted discourse says 『Former practice: sun audience at spring equinox, moon audience at autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Secretary Director Xue Xun submitted a discourse: 『Former practice held sun audience at the spring equinox and moon audience at the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》朝日無常日，鄭玄云用二分，故遂施行。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites of Zhou, sun audience has no fixed day; Zheng Xuan says use the two equinoxes—hence it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou fixes no day for sun audience; Zheng Xuan says use the two equinoxes—hence it was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 秋分之夕，月多東潛，而西向拜之，背實遠矣。

translations.literal: On the evening of the autumn equinox the moon often sinks eastward, yet one bows west-facing—far from the reality.
translations.idiomatic: On the autumn-equinox evening the moon often lies low in the east, yet one bows west-facing—far from the fact.

sentences.zh: 謂朝日宜用仲春之朔，夕月宜用仲秋之朔』。

translations.literal: He holds sun audience should use the new moon of mid-spring, moon audience the new moon of mid-autumn.』
translations.idiomatic: He holds that sun audience should use the new moon of mid-spring and moon audience the new moon of mid-autumn.』

sentences.zh: 淳于睿駮之，引《禮記》云『祭日於東，祭月於西，以端其位』。

translations.literal: Chunyu Rui refuted it, citing the Record of Rites: 『Sacrifice to the sun in the east, to the moon in the west—to set their positions aright.』
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Rui refuted him, citing the Record of Rites: 『Sacrifice to the sun in the east and to the moon in the west—to set their positions aright.』

sentences.zh: 《周禮》秋分夕月，竝行於上世。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou's autumn equinox evening moon—both were practiced in high antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou's autumn-equinox evening moon—both were practiced in high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 西向拜月，雖如背實，亦猶月在天而祭之於坎，不復言背月也。

translations.literal: West-facing bow to the moon, though seemingly turning one's back on reality, is still like the moon being in heaven yet sacrificed to at the north pit—one does not speak of turning one's back on the moon.
translations.idiomatic: A west-facing bow to the moon, though it seems to turn away from the fact, is like sacrificing to the moon in the north pit while it is in the sky—no one calls that turning one's back on the moon.

sentences.zh: 佟之案《禮器》云『爲朝夕必放於日月』。

translations.literal: Tongzhi examined the Record of Ritual Vessels: 『For morning and evening one must set the positions of sun and moon.』
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi examined the Record of Ritual Vessels: 『For morning and evening one must set the positions of sun and moon.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『日出東方，月在西方』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says 『The sun rises in the east, the moon is in the west.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 『The sun rises in the east and the moon is in the west.』

sentences.zh: 又云『大明生於東，月生於西，此陰陽之分，夫婦之位也』。

translations.literal: Again he says 『Great Brightness is born in the east, the moon in the west—this is the division of yin and yang, the positions of husband and wife.』
translations.idiomatic: Again: 『Great Brightness is born in the east and the moon in the west—this is the division of yin and yang and the positions of husband and wife.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『大明，日也』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says 『Great Brightness is the sun.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 『Great Brightness is the sun.』

sentences.zh: 知朝日東向，夕月西向，斯蓋各本其位之所在耳。

translations.literal: Knowing sun audience faces east and moon audience faces west—each follows where its position lies.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that sun audience faces east and moon audience west—each follows where its position lies.

sentences.zh: 猶如天子東西遊幸，朝堂之官及拜官者，猶北向朝拜，寧得以背實爲疑邪？

translations.literal: Just as when the Son of Heaven travels east and west, court officials and those receiving office still bow north-facing in audience—how can one doubt it on the ground of turning one's back on reality?
translations.idiomatic: Just as when the Son of Heaven travels east or west, court officials and appointees still bow north in audience—how can one doubt it as turning away from the fact?

sentences.zh: 佟之謂魏世所行，善得與奪之衷。

translations.literal: Tongzhi said what Wei practiced well hit the mean between holding and discarding.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi said that what Wei practiced struck the right balance between keeping and discarding.

sentences.zh: 晉初弃圓丘方澤，於兩郊二至輟禮，至於二分之朝，致替無義。

translations.literal: Early Jin abandoned Round Mound and Square Pond, halted rites at the two suburbs and two solstices; as for equinox audiences, they lapsed without reason.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin abandoned the Round Mound and Square Pond and dropped the two-suburb and two-solstice rites; the equinox audiences lapsed without reason.

sentences.zh: 江左草創，舊章多闕，宋氏因循，未能反古。

translations.literal: When the Jiangzuo court was first founded, old statutes were largely missing; Song followed inertia and could not return to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern-Jin court was first founded, old statutes were largely missing; Song followed inertia and could not return to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 竊惟皇齊應天御極，典教惟新，謂宜使盛典行之盛代，以春分朝於殿庭之西，東向而拜日，秋分於殿庭之東，西向而拜月，此卽所謂必放日月以端其位之義也。

translations.literal: I venture to think Great Qi, receiving Heaven and holding the summit, has renewed canonical teaching—the grand rites should be performed in this flourishing age: on the spring equinox have audience west of the hall courtyard, east-facing to bow to the sun; on the autumn equinox east of the courtyard, west-facing to bow to the moon—this is the meaning of "must set sun and moon to set their positions aright."
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that Great Qi, receiving Heaven and holding the summit, has renewed canonical teaching—the grand rites should be performed in this flourishing age: on the spring equinox have audience west of the hall courtyard and bow east to the sun; on the autumn equinox east of the courtyard and bow west to the moon—this is what it means to set sun and moon and set their positions aright.

sentences.zh: 使四方觀化者，莫不欣欣而頌美。

translations.literal: So that all who observe the transformation from the four quarters will delight and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Then all who observe the transformation from the four quarters will rejoice and praise.

sentences.zh: 服無旒藻之飾，蓋本天之至質也，朝日不得同昊天至質之禮，故玄冕三旒也。

translations.literal: Garments without tassel-and-emblem ornament mostly reflect Heaven's utmost simplicity; sun audience cannot match the rite of utmost simplicity toward August Heaven, hence black cap with three tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Garments without tassel-and-emblem ornament reflect Heaven's utmost simplicity; sun audience cannot match the rite of utmost simplicity toward August Heaven—hence the black cap with three tassels.

sentences.zh: 近代祀天，著袞十二旒，極文章之美，則是古今禮之變也。

translations.literal: Recent Heaven sacrifice uses dragon robe with twelve tassels, utmost pattern and beauty—that is the change of ritual ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Recent Heaven sacrifice uses the dragon robe with twelve tassels, utmost in pattern and beauty—that is how ritual has changed from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 禮天朝日，旣服宜有異，頃世天子小朝會，著絳紗袍、通天金博山冠，斯卽今朝之服次袞冕者也，竊謂宜依此拜日月，甚得差降之宜也。

translations.literal: Honoring Heaven and sun audience—garments should differ; in recent generations at the Son of Heaven's minor court audience he wears the crimson gauze robe and the heaven-piercing gold Mount Bo crown—that is today's garment ranking below dragon robe and cap; I venture to hold that bowing to sun and moon should follow this—very fitting as graded propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Rites to Heaven and sun audience should differ in dress; in recent generations at the Son of Heaven's minor court audience he wears the crimson gauze robe and the heaven-piercing gold Mount Bo crown—the garment today ranking just below dragon robe and cap. I hold that bowing to sun and moon should follow this—a very fitting gradation.

sentences.zh: 佟之任非禮局，輕奏大典，寔爲侵官，伏追慙震。

translations.literal: Tongzhi's office is not in the Rituals Bureau; lightly memorializing a great statute was truly overstepping— I prostrate myself in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi's office is not in the Rituals Bureau; lightly memorializing a great statute was truly overstepping—I prostrate myself in shame.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」[The court] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court followed it.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，有司奏：「來年正月二十五日丁亥，可祀先農，卽日輿駕親耕。

translations.literal: Yongming year 3, the relevant offices memorialized: 「Next year, the twenty-fifth day of the first month, dinghai, may sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture; on that same day the imperial carriage shall personally plow.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming, the relevant offices memorialized: 「On the twenty-fifth of the first month next year—the day dinghai—we may sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture, and on that same day the imperial carriage shall plow in person.

sentences.zh: 」宋元嘉、大明以來，竝用立春後亥日，尚書令王儉以爲亥日藉田，經記無文，通下詳議。

translations.literal: 」Since Yuanjia and Daming, both used the hai day after Establishment of Spring; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian held that a hai day for the Fertile Field has no textual basis in classics and memorials, and ordered thorough deliberation below.
translations.idiomatic: 」Since the Yuanjia and Daming eras, both had used the hai day after Establishment of Spring. Wang Jian, director of the Masters of Writing, held that plowing the Fertile Field on a hai day had no warrant in the classics and ordered a full debate below.

sentences.zh: 兼太學博士劉蔓議：「《禮》，孟春之月，立春迎春，又於是月以元日祈穀，又擇元辰躬耕帝藉。

translations.literal: Concurrent Grand Academy erudite Liu Man argued: 「The Rites: in the first month of spring, at Establishment of Spring one welcomes spring; in that month on the prime day one prays for grain; again one selects the prime chen and in person plows the emperor's sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Grand Academy erudite Liu Man argued: 「The Rites prescribe that in the first month of spring, at Establishment of Spring one welcomes spring; in that same month on the prime day one prays for grain; and again one chooses the prime chen and plows the emperor's sacred field in person.

sentences.zh: 盧植說禮通辰日，日，甲至癸也，辰，子至亥也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi's exposition of the Rites on 「general chen day」: day means jia through gui; chen means zi through hai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, expounding the Rites on 「general chen day,」 says day means jia through gui, and chen means zi through hai.

sentences.zh: 郊天，陽也，故以日。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven is yang, hence one uses the day.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven is yang—therefore one uses the day [stem].

sentences.zh: 藉田，陰也，故以辰。

translations.literal: The Fertile Field is yin, hence one uses the chen.
translations.idiomatic: The Fertile Field is yin—therefore one uses the chen [branch].

sentences.zh: 陰禮卑後，必居其末，亥者辰之末，故《記》稱元辰，注曰吉亥。

translations.literal: Yin rites are inferior and come last—they must occupy the end; hai is the end of the chen branches, hence the Record calls it 「prime chen,」 and the commentary says 「auspicious hai.」
translations.idiomatic: Yin rites rank lower and come last—they must take the final place; hai is the last of the earthly branches, so the Record speaks of 「prime chen,」 and the commentary glosses 「auspicious hai.」

sentences.zh: 又據五行之說，木生於亥，以亥日祭先農，又其義也。」

translations.literal: Again by the Five Phases doctrine, wood is born at hai—to sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture on a hai day is likewise fitting.」
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Phases as well, wood is born at hai—to sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture on a hai day fits that meaning too.」

sentences.zh: 太常丞何諲之議：「鄭注云『元辰，蓋郊後吉亥也』。

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Ceremonial He Yinzhi argued: 「Zheng's commentary says 『prime chen means roughly the auspicious hai after the suburban sacrifice.』
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Ceremonial He Yinzhi argued: 「Zheng Xuan says, 『Prime chen means, in essence, the auspicious hai after the suburban sacrifice.』

sentences.zh: 亥，水辰也，凡在墾稼，咸存灑潤。

translations.literal: Hai is the water chen; all tilled grain depends on sprinkling and moistening.
translations.idiomatic: Hai is the water branch; everything sown in the fields lives by rain and soak.

sentences.zh: 五行說十二辰爲六合，寅與亥合，建寅月東耕，取月建與日辰合也。」

translations.literal: The Five Phases doctrine treats the twelve chen as six pairs; yin and hai pair; in the month established at yin, plowing east—this takes the month establishment and the day chen in conjunction.」
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases treat the twelve branches as six pairs—yin pairs with hai; in the month established at yin one plows eastward, joining month establishment with the day's branch.」

sentences.zh: 國子助教桑惠度議：「尋鄭玄以亥爲吉辰者，陽生於子，元起於亥，取陽之元以爲生物，亥又爲水，十月所建，百穀賴茲沾潤畢熟也。」

translations.literal: National University assistant instructor Sang Huidu argued: 「Examining Zheng Xuan's treating hai as auspicious chen: yang is born at zi, the origin begins at hai—one takes the origin of yang for bringing forth life; hai is also water, the month established in the tenth month—all grain relies on this soaking to ripen fully.」
translations.idiomatic: National University assistant instructor Sang Huidu argued: 「Zheng Xuan makes hai the auspicious chen because yang is born at zi yet the origin begins at hai—he takes yang's origin as the seed of life; hai is also water, the tenth month's establishment—all grain depends on that soaking to ripen.」

sentences.zh: 助教周山文議：「盧植云『元，善也。

translations.literal: Assistant instructor Zhou Shanwen argued: 「Lu Zhi says 『yuan means good.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant instructor Zhou Shanwen argued: 「Lu Zhi says, 『Yuan means good.

sentences.zh: 郊天，陽也，故以日。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven is yang, hence one uses the day.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven is yang—hence one uses the day.

sentences.zh: 藉田，陰也，故以辰』。

translations.literal: The Fertile Field is yin, hence one uses the chen.』
translations.idiomatic: The Fertile Field is yin—hence one uses the chen.』

sentences.zh: 蔡邕《月令章》句解元辰云『日，幹也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's Monthly Ordinances commentary glosses prime chen: 『Day is the stem.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's commentary on the Monthly Ordinances glosses prime chen: 『Day is the stem.

sentences.zh: 辰，支也。

translations.literal: Chen is the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Chen is the branch.

sentences.zh: 有事於天，用日。

translations.literal: When there is business with Heaven, use the day.
translations.idiomatic: Business with Heaven uses the day.

sentences.zh: 有事於地，用辰』。」

translations.literal: When there is business with Earth, use the chen.』」
translations.idiomatic: Business with Earth uses the chen.』」

sentences.zh: 助教何佟之議：「《少牢饋食禮》云『孝孫某，來日丁亥，用薦歲事于皇祖伯某』。

translations.literal: Assistant instructor He Tongzhi argued: 「The Lesser Stallion Feeding Rite says 『The filial grandson so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the year's offering to the august ancestor Lord So-and-so.』
translations.idiomatic: Assistant instructor He Tongzhi argued: 「The Lesser Stallion Feeding Rite says, 『The filial grandson so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the year's offering to the august ancestor Lord So-and-so.』

sentences.zh: 注云『丁未必亥也，直舉一日以言之耳。

translations.literal: The commentary says 『ding is not necessarily hai—it simply cites one day as an example.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 『Ding need not be hai; the text merely names one day by way of example.

sentences.zh: 禘太廟禮日用丁亥，若不丁亥，則用己亥、辛亥，苟有亥可也』。

translations.literal: The Grand Temple rite uses a dinghai day; if not dinghai, then jihai or xinhai—any hai will do.』
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple rite uses dinghai; if not dinghai, then jihai or xinhai—any day with hai will serve.』

sentences.zh: 鄭又云『必用丁、己者，取其令名，自丁寧自變改，皆爲謹敬』。

translations.literal: Zheng also says 『One must use ding or ji for their auspicious names—dingning and biangai both mean reverent care.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says, 『Ding and ji are chosen for their auspicious names—「settled peace」 and 「reverent change」—both speak of careful respect.』

sentences.zh: 如此，丁亥自是祭祀之日，不專施於先農。

translations.literal: Thus dinghai is naturally a sacrificial day, not exclusively for the Spirit of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: On that reading, dinghai is simply a day fit for sacrifice—not reserved for the Spirit of Agriculture alone.

sentences.zh: 漢文用此日耕藉祠先農，故後王相承用之，非有別義。」

translations.literal: Han Wendi used this day to plow the Fertile Field and sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture, so later kings successively used it—there is no separate meaning.」
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi happened to plow the Fertile Field and sacrifice to the Spirit of Agriculture on that day, and later kings followed him—nothing more was intended.」

sentences.zh: 殿中郎顧暠之議：「鄭玄稱先郊後吉辰，而不說必亥之由。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Gu Haozhi argued: 「Zheng Xuan said after the suburban sacrifice comes the auspicious chen, but did not explain why it must be hai.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Gu Haozhi argued: 「Zheng Xuan said the auspicious chen follows the suburban sacrifice, yet he never explained why it must be hai.

sentences.zh: 盧植明子亥爲辰，亦無常辰之證。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi clarified that zi through hai are chen, but there is also no proof of a fixed chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi showed that zi through hai count as chen, but offered no proof that the chen must always be the same.

sentences.zh: 漢世躬藉，肇發漢文，詔云『農，天下之本，其開藉田』。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty's personal Fertile Field began with Han Wendi; the edict said 『Agriculture is the foundation of the empire—open the Fertile Field.』
translations.idiomatic: Han personal plowing began with Wendi, whose edict read: 『Agriculture is the empire's root—open the Fertile Field.』

sentences.zh: 斯乃草創之令，未覩親載之吉也。

translations.literal: That was a founding ordinance—we have not yet seen which day was auspicious for personal plowing.
translations.idiomatic: That was a founding decree—we have no record yet of which day was deemed lucky for the emperor's own plow.

sentences.zh: 昭帝癸亥耕于鉤盾弄田，明帝癸亥耕下邳，章帝乙亥耕定陶，又辛丑耕懷，魏之烈祖實書辛未，不繫一辰，徵於兩代矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Emperor guihai plowed at the Hook-Shield pleasure fields; Ming Emperor guihai at Xiapi; Zhang Emperor yihai at Dingtao, and again xinchou at Huai—Wei's Liezu in fact recorded xinwei: they are not tied to one chen. Evidence spans two dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Di plowed on guihai at the Hook-Shield pleasure fields; Ming Di on guihai at Xiapi; Zhang Di on yihai at Dingtao, and again on xinchou at Huai—Wei's Liezu actually wrote xinwei. No single branch binds them; two dynasties prove it.

sentences.zh: 推晉之革魏，宋之因晉，政是服膺康成，非有異見者也。

translations.literal: Inferring Jin's overthrow of Wei and Song's succession from Jin—they simply followed Zheng Xuan, not a different view.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin replaced Wei and Song took Jin's place, they were only following Zheng Xuan—not advancing a new theory.

sentences.zh: 班固序亥位云『陰氣應亡射，該藏萬物，而雜陽閡種』。

translations.literal: Ban Gu on the hai position says 『Yin qi responds to wangshe, conceals all things, and with yang blocks the sowing of seed.』
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu, ordering the hai position, writes: 『Yin answers to the season of stored death, enfolds the ten thousand things, and with yang checks the sowing of seed.』

sentences.zh: 且亥旣水辰，含育爲性，播厥取吉，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, hai being the water chen, nurturing is its nature—for sowing to take auspiciousness, is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: Hai is the water branch; to nourish is its nature—if sowing seeks an auspicious day, where else should one look?

sentences.zh: 固序丑位云『陰大旅助黃鍾宣氣而牙物』。

translations.literal: Ban orders the chou position: 『Great yin assists Huangzhong to disseminate qi and sprout things.』
translations.idiomatic: On chou he writes: 『Great yin assists Huangzhong to spread breath and bud the ten thousand kinds.』

sentences.zh: 序未位云『陰氣受任，助蕤賔君主種物，使長大茂盛』。

translations.literal: On the wei position: 『Yin qi receives appointment, assists Ruibin to govern planting, making things grow lush and abundant.』
translations.idiomatic: On wei: 『Yin takes its charge, aids Ruibin to rule over planting, and makes things grow tall and thick.』

sentences.zh: 是漢朝迭選，魏室所遷，酌舊用丑，實兼有據。

translations.literal: Hence Han chose by turns, Wei shifted—weighing the old, they used chou, which indeed has dual support.
translations.idiomatic: Han picked different days in turn; Wei changed again—weighing precedent, they favored chou, and that too had double warrant.

sentences.zh: 」參議奏用丁亥。

translations.literal: 」The joint deliberation memorialized to use dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: 」The joint deliberation recommended dinghai.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 建元四年正月，詔立國學，置學生百五十人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jianyuan, an edict established the National University and set one hundred fifty students.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianyuan 4, an edict founded the National University with one hundred fifty students.

sentences.zh: 其有位樂入者五十人。

translations.literal: Of these, fifty were musicians already holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty were court musicians already in post.

sentences.zh: 生年十五以上，二十以還，取王公已下至三將、著作郎、廷尉正、太子舍人、領護諸府司馬諮議經除敕者、諸州別駕治中等、見居官及罷散者子孫。

translations.literal: Students were to be fifteen or older and not yet twenty, drawn from descendants of kings and dukes down through the three generals, Masters of Writing, director of the Court of Justice, crown prince attendants, marshals and protectors of the various offices who had passed the classics examination by imperial order, provincial vice-prefects and magistrates of the middle rank, and children of men currently in office or dismissed and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Students were to be at least fifteen and not yet twenty, taken from the sons of kings and dukes down through the three generals, Masters of Writing, director of the Court of Justice, crown prince attendants, marshals and protectors of the various offices who had passed the classics examination by edict, provincial vice-prefects and middle-grade magistrates, and the sons of men in office or recently dismissed.

sentences.zh: 悉取家去都二千里爲限。

translations.literal: All were limited to families within two thousand li of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: All were to come from families within two thousand li of the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，乃止。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor died, the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder Emperor died, the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 永明三年正月，詔立學，創立堂宇，召公卿子弟下及員外郎之胤，凡置生二百人。

translations.literal: In the first month of Yongming year 3, an edict established the academy, built halls, and summoned sons of ministers and grandees down to grandsons of supernumerary court gentlemen—in all two hundred students.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongming 3, an edict re-established the academy, raised new halls, and called up sons of the high nobility down to grandsons of supernumerary gentlemen—two hundred students in all.

sentences.zh: 其年秋中悉集。

translations.literal: That autumn they all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they all gathered.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「宋元嘉舊事，學生到，先釋奠先聖先師，禮又有釋菜，未詳今當行何禮？

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: 「Under the Yuanjia precedent of Song, when students arrived they first performed the libation to the Former Sage and Former Teacher; the rites also mention the vegetable offering—it is unclear which rite should be performed now.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: 「Song's Yuanjia precedent had students, on arrival, perform the libation to the Former Sage and Former Teacher; the rites also speak of the vegetable offering. Which ceremony should we perform now?

sentences.zh: 用何樂及禮器？

translations.literal: What music and ritual vessels should be used?
translations.idiomatic: What music and ritual vessels should we use?

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王儉議：「《周禮》『春入學，舍菜合舞』。

translations.literal: 」Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian argued: 「The Rites of Zhou: 『In spring one enters the academy, sets out vegetables, and joins in the dance.』
translations.idiomatic: 」Wang Jian, director of the Masters of Writing, argued: 「The Rites of Zhou says, 『In spring one enters the academy, sets out vegetables, and dances together.』

sentences.zh: 《記》云『始教，皮弁祭菜，示敬道也』。

translations.literal: The Record says 『At the first teaching, in leather cap one sacrifices to the vegetables, showing reverence for the Way.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, 『At the first lesson, in leather cap one sacrifices to the vegetables—to show reverence for the Way.』

sentences.zh: 又云『始入學，必祭先聖先師』。

translations.literal: It also says 『On first entering the academy, one must sacrifice to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.』
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 『On first entering the academy, one must sacrifice to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.』

sentences.zh: 中朝以來，釋菜禮廢，今之所行，釋奠而已。

translations.literal: Since the Central Court, the vegetable-offering rite has fallen into disuse; what is practiced now is only the libation sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Central Court dynasties, the vegetable-offering rite has been abandoned; only the libation sacrifice is performed today.

sentences.zh: 金石俎豆，皆無明文。

translations.literal: Metal and stone [instruments], stands and vessels—all lack explicit text in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Bells, chimes, stands, and vessels—all lack explicit warrant in the classics.

sentences.zh: 方之七廟則輕，比之五禮則重。

translations.literal: Compared to the seven temples it is light; compared to the five great rites it is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the seven temples it is slight; measured against the five great rites it is weighty.

sentences.zh: 陸納、車胤謂宣尼廟宜依亭侯之爵；

translations.literal: Lu Na and Che Yin held that the Temple of Confucius should follow the rank of a district marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na and Che Yin held that Confucius's temple should follow a district marquis's rank;

sentences.zh: 范寧欲依周公之廟，用王者儀，范宣謂當其爲師則不臣之，釋奠日，備帝王禮樂。

translations.literal: Fan Ning wished to follow the Duke of Zhou's temple and use kingly ceremony; Fan Xuan held that when one is his teacher one does not treat him as a subject—on the libation-sacrifice day, employ full imperial ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning wished to model the Duke of Zhou's temple and use royal ceremony; Fan Xuan held that while he is one's teacher one does not treat him as a subject—on the libation day, use the full ritual and music of a king.

sentences.zh: 此則車、陸失於過輕，二范傷於太重。

translations.literal: In this Che and Lu erred toward too light, the two Fans toward too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Here Che and Lu fell short by being too light, the two Fans by being too heavy.

sentences.zh: 喻希云『若至王者自設禮樂，則肆賞於至敬之所；

translations.literal: Yu Xi said, 『If it reaches the point that the king himself sets ritual and music, then the display of gifts is made at the place of utmost reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi said, 『If the king himself sets ritual and music, offerings are displayed where reverence is greatest;

sentences.zh: 若欲嘉美先師，則所況非備』。

translations.literal: If one wishes to honor the Former Master, then what is applied is not complete [imperial ritual].』
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to honor the Former Master, what is used is not the full [royal] ceremony.』

sentences.zh: 尋其此說，守附情理。

translations.literal: Examining this doctrine, it holds to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing this view, it accords with reason.

sentences.zh: 皇朝屈尊弘教，待以師資，引同上公，卽事惟允。

translations.literal: Our dynasty humbles itself to spread the teaching, treats him as teacher and model, ranks him with a supreme duke—the affair is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty lowers itself to exalt the teaching, treats him as teacher and model, and ranks him with a supreme duke—the arrangement is fitting.

sentences.zh: 元嘉立學，裴松之議應儛六佾，以郊樂未具，故權奏登歌。

translations.literal: When Yuanjia established the academy, Pei Songzhi argued there should be six-row dance; because suburban music was not yet complete, they provisionally used ascent hymns only.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjia founded the academy, Pei Songzhi argued for six-row dance; because suburban music was not yet ready, they provisionally performed only the ascent hymns.

sentences.zh: 今金石已備，宜設軒縣之樂，六佾之舞，牲牢器用，悉依上公。

translations.literal: Now metal and stone are complete; there should be suspended hall music, six-row dance, and victims, vessels, and implements—all following a supreme duke.
translations.idiomatic: Now bells and chimes are in place; we should set out hall-suspended music, six-row dance, and victims, vessels, and implements—all on the supreme-duke scale.

sentences.zh: 」其冬，皇太子講《孝經》，親臨釋奠，車駕幸聽。

translations.literal: 」That winter the crown prince lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; he personally attended the libation sacrifice, and the imperial carriage came to listen.
translations.idiomatic: 」That winter the crown prince lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, personally attended the libation sacrifice, and the imperial carriage came to listen.

sentences.zh: 建武四年正月，詔立學。

translations.literal: Jianwu year 4, first month, an edict established the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianwu 4, an edict founded the academy.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，東昏侯卽位，尚書符依永明舊事廢學。

translations.literal: Yongtai year 1, when the Marquis of Eastern Depravity took the throne, a Secretariat order followed the Yongming precedent and abolished the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1, when the Marquis of Eastern Depravity succeeded, the Secretariat followed the Yongming precedent and abolished the academy.

sentences.zh: 領國子助教曹思文上表曰：「古之建國君民者，必教學爲先，將以節其邪情，而禁其流欲，故能化民裁俗，習與性成也。

translations.literal: Associate instructor of the Directorate of Education Cao Siwen memorialized: 「Ancient founders of states who shepherd the people always put teaching first, intending to restrain depraved feelings and forbid excessive desires, and so transform the people and shape custom—habit and nature become one.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Siwen, associate instructor of the Directorate of Education, memorialized: 「States that would rule and nurture the people always put teaching first—to curb wayward feeling and check excess desire, and so transform the folk and shape custom until habit and nature are one.

sentences.zh: 是以忠孝篤焉，信義成焉，禮讓行焉，尊教宗學，其致一也。

translations.literal: Thus loyalty and filial piety are deepened, faith and righteousness established, ritual and deference practiced—honoring teaching and honoring learning achieve the same end.
translations.idiomatic: Then loyalty and filial piety take root, faith and righteousness stand firm, and ritual and yielding prevail—revering teaching and revering learning reach the same end.

sentences.zh: 是以成均煥於古典，虎門炳於前經。

translations.literal: Thus the Completion Equal shines in ancient canon, the Tiger Gate blazes in earlier classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Completion Equal shines in the ancient canon; the Tiger Gate blazes in the earlier classics.

sentences.zh: 陛下體睿淳神，纘承鴻業，今制書旣下，而廢學先聞，將恐觀國之光者，有以擬議也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty embodies pure sagely spirit and carries on great enterprise; now the decree is already issued while abolition of the academy is heard first—I fear those who view the state's brilliance will have grounds for criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty embodies pure sagely spirit and carries forward great enterprise; yet the decree has barely gone forth while word of abolishing the academy comes first—I fear observers of the state's brilliance will find matter for reproach.

sentences.zh: 若以國諱故宜廢，昔漢成立學，爰洎元始，百餘年中，未嘗暫廢，其閒有國諱也。

translations.literal: If because of the imperial taboo it should be abolished—in former Han they established the academy from founding until Yuanshi, more than a hundred years without brief abolition, and in that interval there were imperial taboos.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial taboo requires abolition: Han founded the academy and kept it from founding through Yuanshi—more than a hundred years without a break—and taboo names occurred in that span.

sentences.zh: 且晉武之崩，又其學猶存，斯皆先代不以國諱而廢學之明文也。

translations.literal: Moreover when Jin Wudi died, the academy still remained—all are clear texts of earlier ages that they did not abolish the academy because of imperial taboo.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Wudi died, the academy still stood—these are plain precedents that earlier ages did not abolish teaching because of taboo.

sentences.zh: 永明以無太子故廢，斯非古典也。

translations.literal: Yongming abolished it because there was no crown prince—that is not ancient precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming abolished it for lack of a crown prince—that is not ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 尋國之有學，本以興化致治也，天子於以諮謀焉，於以行禮焉。

translations.literal: Consider that the state has an academy fundamentally to promote transformation and achieve good government; the Son of Heaven thereby consults and deliberates, thereby performs ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The state keeps an academy to foster transformation and good government; the Son of Heaven consults there and performs ritual there.

sentences.zh: 《記》云『天子出征，受命於祖，受成於學。

translations.literal: The Record says, 『When the Son of Heaven campaigns, he receives mandate from the ancestor, receives completion at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, 『When the Son of Heaven goes to war, he receives mandate from the ancestor and completion at the academy.

sentences.zh: 執有罪反，釋奠於學』。

translations.literal: Returning with the captive of guilt, he performs libation sacrifice at the academy.』
translations.idiomatic: Returning with prisoners, he performs the libation sacrifice at the academy.』

sentences.zh: 又云『食三老五更於太學，天子袒而割牲，執爵而酳，以教諸侯悌也』。

translations.literal: It also says, 『He feeds the three elders and five elders at the Grand Academy; the Son of Heaven bares his shoulder and cuts the victim, holds the cup and performs the reciprocal sip, to teach the feudal lords brotherly deference.』
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 『At the Grand Academy he feasts the three elders and five elders; the Son of Heaven bares his shoulder, cuts the victim, holds the cup and sips in turn—to teach the feudal lords brotherly deference.』

sentences.zh: 於斯學，是天子有國之基，教也或以之。

translations.literal: In such an academy lies the foundation of the Son of Heaven's possession of the state; teaching may also rest upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In that academy lies the foundation of the Son of Heaven's holding the state; government may also draw upon it.

sentences.zh: 所言皆太學事也。

translations.literal: What is spoken of are all Grand Academy matters.
translations.idiomatic: All of this concerns the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 今引太學不非證也。

translations.literal: To cite the Grand Academy now is not wrong evidence.
translations.idiomatic: To cite the Grand Academy now is not improper evidence.

sentences.zh: 據臣所見，今之國學，卽古之太學。

translations.literal: By what this subject has seen, today's National University is the ancient Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, today's National University is the ancient Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 晉初太學生三千人，旣多猥雜，惠帝時欲辯其涇渭，故元康三年始立國子學，官品第五以上得入國學。

translations.literal: Early Jin had three thousand Grand Academy students; they were numerous and mixed; under Emperor Hui they wished to distinguish clear from muddy, so in Yuankang 3 they first established the Directorate of Education—officials of fifth rank and above could enter the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin had three thousand Grand Academy students—too many and too mixed; under Emperor Hui they wished to separate pure from base, so in Yuankang 3 they founded the Directorate of Education, and officials of fifth rank and above could enter the National University.

sentences.zh: 天子去太學入國學，以行禮也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven leaves the Grand Academy and enters the National University to perform ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven leaves the Grand Academy and enters the National University to perform ritual.

sentences.zh: 太子去太學入國學，以齒讓也。

translations.literal: The crown prince leaves the Grand Academy and enters the National University for age-order yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince leaves the Grand Academy and enters the National University to yield by age.

sentences.zh: 太學之與國學，斯是晉世殊其士庶，異其貴賤耳。

translations.literal: Grand Academy and National University—in Jin they distinguished commoner from noble, differentiating humble and exalted, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Academy and the National University—in Jin they only separated commoner from noble, humble from exalted.

sentences.zh: 然貴賤士庶，皆須教成，故國學太學兩存之也，非有太子故立也。

translations.literal: Yet noble and humble, commoner and gentry, all need teaching completed; therefore both National University and Grand Academy were kept—it was not because there was a crown prince that they were established.
translations.idiomatic: Yet noble and humble alike must be taught; both the National University and the Grand Academy were kept—not because a crown prince existed.

sentences.zh: 然繫廢興於太子者，此永明之鉅失也。

translations.literal: Yet to tie abolition and revival to the crown prince—this is Yongming's great error.
translations.idiomatic: To tie abolition and revival to the crown prince—that is Yongming's grave mistake.

sentences.zh: 漢崇儒雅，幾致刑厝，而猶道謝三、五者，以其致教之術未篤也。

translations.literal: Han honored Confucian elegance and nearly reached putting away the punishments, yet still fell short of the eras of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—because their method of achieving teaching was not deep.
translations.idiomatic: Han honored Confucian learning and nearly abolished punishment, yet still fell short of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—because its way of teaching was not thorough.

sentences.zh: 古之教者，家有塾，黨有庠，術有序，國有學，以諷誦相摩。

translations.literal: Ancient teachers: the family had a schoolroom, the district had a village academy, the lane had a sequence, the state had an academy—reciting and chanting to polish one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient teaching had a school in every home, a hall in every district, a sequence in every lane, and an academy in the state—students reciting and chanting to sharpen one another.

sentences.zh: 今學非唯不宜廢而已，乃宜更崇尚其道，望古作規，使郡縣有學，鄉閭立教。

translations.literal: The academy today should not only not be abolished; one ought further to honor its Way, look to antiquity as model, and have districts and counties with academies, villages and hamlets with teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The academy should not merely be spared; its Way should be honored further, antiquity taken as model, and every district and county given an academy, every village and hamlet a school.

sentences.zh: 請付尚書及二學詳議。

translations.literal: Request that it be referred to the Secretariat and the two academies for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Secretariat and the two academies deliberate this in detail.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏。

translations.literal: 」The relevant offices memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: 」The relevant offices memorialized.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The throne] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 學竟不立。

translations.literal: The academy in the end was not established.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the academy was not established.

sentences.zh: 永明五年十月，有司奏：「南郡王昭業冠，求儀注未有前准。

translations.literal: Yongming year 5, tenth month, the relevant offices memorialized: 「The Prince of Nan Commandery Zhaoye's capping—we seek protocol for which there is no earlier precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongming 5, the relevant offices memorialized: 「Prince Zhaoye of Nan Commandery is to be capped, but we find no earlier precedent for the protocol.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王儉議：「皇孫冠事，歷代所無，禮雖有嫡子無嫡孫，然而地居正體，下及五世。

translations.literal: 」Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian argued: 「Capping for an imperial grandson—through the ages there is none; ritual though says "no grandson in the direct line when there is a direct son," yet he occupies the principal line in position, extending down through five generations.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wang Jian, director of the Masters of Writing, argued: 「An imperial grandson's capping has no precedent in any age. Ritual says there is no grandson in the direct line when there is a direct son, yet he stands in the principal line and the line runs five generations down.

sentences.zh: 今南郡王體自儲暉，實惟國裔，元服之典，宜異列蕃。

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Nan Commandery embodies the heir's radiance, truly the state's lineage; the ceremony of full adulthood should differ from enfeoffed princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Nan Commandery bears the heir's radiance and is truly of the imperial line; his coming-of-age rite should differ from enfeoffed princes.

sentences.zh: 案《士冠禮》『主人玄冠朝服，賔加其冠，贊者結纓』。

translations.literal: According to the Capping Rite for Commoners: 『The host in dark cap and court dress, the guest adds the cap, the assistant ties the tassel.』
translations.idiomatic: The Capping Rite for Commoners says: 『The host wears a dark cap and court dress; the guest sets on the cap; the assistant ties the tassel.』

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云『主人，冠者之父兄也』。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says, 『The host is the capping man's father or elder brother.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says, 『The host is the capping man's father or elder brother.』

sentences.zh: 尋其言父及兄，則明祖在，父不爲主也。

translations.literal: Examining his words "father and elder brother," thus when grandfather is living, the father does not serve as host.
translations.idiomatic: Reading "father and elder brother," when the grandfather lives, the father does not act as host.

sentences.zh: 《大戴禮記公冠篇》云公冠自爲主，四加玄冕，以卿爲賔。

translations.literal: The Elder Dai Record of Rites, Duke's Capping chapter, says the duke caps himself as host, four additions with dark imperial cap, taking a minister as guest.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder Dai's Record of Rites, Duke's Capping chapter, says the duke caps himself as host, with four additions in dark imperial cap and a minister as guest.

sentences.zh: 此則繼體之君及帝之庶子不得稱子者也。

translations.literal: This is why a succession heir and an emperor's son by a concubine may not be called "son."
translations.idiomatic: That is why a lord who inherits the line and an emperor's son born of a concubine may not be styled "son."

sentences.zh: 《小戴禮記冠義》云『冠於阼，以著代也。

translations.literal: The Small Da Record of Rites, Capping chapter, says, 『Capping at the east steps shows that one takes the place of succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Small Da's Record of Rites, Capping chapter, says, 『One caps at the east steps to mark the handing on of one's place.

sentences.zh: 醮於客位，三加彌尊，加有成也』。

translations.literal: The libation at the guest's place; three additions, each more honored; the additions show completion.』
translations.idiomatic: The libation at the guest's seat; three additions, each more exalted; the additions mark full attainment.』

sentences.zh: 注稱『嫡子冠於阼，庶子冠於房』。

translations.literal: The commentary says, 『The direct son caps at the east steps; the son by a concubine caps in the side chamber.』
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 『The heir caps at the east steps; a younger son by a concubine caps in the side chamber.』

sentences.zh: 《記》又云『古者重冠，故行之於廟，所以自卑而尊先祖也』。

translations.literal: The Record also says, 『In antiquity capping was weighty, hence it was performed in the temple—to humble oneself and honor the ancestors.』
translations.idiomatic: The Record also says, 『Anciently capping was held in high regard, so it was done in the ancestral temple—lowering oneself to exalt the forebears.』

sentences.zh: 據此而言，彌與鄭注《儀禮》相會。

translations.literal: On this basis, [these passages] fully accord with Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, they align fully with Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites.

sentences.zh: 是故中朝以來，太子冠則皇帝臨軒，司徒加冠，光祿贊冠。

translations.literal: Therefore since the Central Court, when the crown prince is capped the emperor attends at the hall, the Minister of Education sets on the cap, and the Director of Imperial Entertainment assists the capping.
translations.idiomatic: Hence since the Central Court dynasties, when the heir apparent is capped the emperor presides at the hall, the Minister of Education places the cap, and the Director of Imperial Entertainment assists.

sentences.zh: 諸王則郎中加冠，中尉贊冠。

translations.literal: For princes, a palace gentleman sets on the cap and the commandant of the guard assists.
translations.idiomatic: For enfeoffed princes, a palace gentleman caps them and the commandant of the guard assists.

sentences.zh: 今同於儲皇則重，依於諸王則輕。

translations.literal: To treat him now like the heir would be too heavy; to follow the princes would be too light.
translations.idiomatic: To rank him with the heir would be excessive; to follow the princes would be slighting.

sentences.zh: 又《春秋》之義，『不以父命辭王父命』。
