translations.literal: Again, the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: 『One does not refuse a grandfather's command on a father's order.』
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Spring and Autumn Annals teach: 『One does not set aside a grandfather's command because of a father's.』

sentences.zh: 《禮》『父在斯爲子，君在斯爲臣』。

translations.literal: The Rites: 『While the father lives one is a son; while the lord lives one is a subject.』
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: 『While the father lives one remains a son; while the sovereign lives one remains a subject.』

sentences.zh: 皇太子居臣子之節，無專用之道。

translations.literal: The crown prince keeps the station of subject and son; he has no way to act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince stands in the role of subject and son; he has no prerogative to act independently.

sentences.zh: 南郡雖處蕃國，非支庶之列，宜稟天朝之命，微申冠阼之禮。

translations.literal: Nan Commandery, though it lies in a feudatory state, is not among collateral younger sons; he should receive the Central Court's command and in modest measure perform the capping rite at the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Commandery, though a feudatory realm, is not a collateral younger line; he should take his mandate from the court and observe the capping at the east steps in due measure.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝詔稱漢、魏遣使冠諸王，非古正典。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin's edict said that Han and Wei sent envoys to cap the princes—this is not the ancient correct canon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin's edict held that Han and Wei sent envoys to cap enfeoffed princes—not the ancient proper canon.

sentences.zh: 此蓋謂庶子封王，合依公冠自主之義，至於國之長孫，遣使惟允。

translations.literal: This surely means that when a son by a concubine is enfeoffed as prince, he should follow the meaning of a duke's capping on his own authority; as for a state's eldest grandson, sending an envoy is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: That surely refers to a younger son by a concubine enfeoffed as prince, who should cap himself as a duke would; for a feudatory state's eldest grandson, an envoy is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 宜使太常持節加冠，大鴻臚爲贊，醮酒之儀，亦歸二卿，祝醮之辭，附准經記，別更撰立，不依蕃國常體。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Ceremonial should bear the staff of office and set on the cap; the Grand Herald should assist; the libation-wine rite too should fall to these two ministers; the blessing and libation texts should follow the classics and records, be newly composed separately, and not follow the feudatory state's usual form.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Director of Grand Ceremonial bear the staff and cap him, the Grand Herald assist, and the libation wine rest with those two ministers as well; the blessing and libation words should track the classics and be drafted anew—not the routine of a feudatory court.

sentences.zh: 國官陪位拜賀，自依舊章。

translations.literal: State officials attending in place to bow and congratulate should follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Feudatory officials attending to bow and offer congratulations should follow established statute.

sentences.zh: 其日內外二品清官以上，詣止車集賀，幷詣東宮南門通牋。

translations.literal: On that day, inner and outer officials of the third rank and above in pure offices should go to where the carriage halts to gather in congratulation, and also go to the Eastern Palace's south gate to submit written felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: That day, pure-office holders of the third rank and above, court and capital alike, should assemble where the carriage stops to offer congratulations, and also present written felicitations at the Eastern Palace's south gate.

sentences.zh: 別日上禮，宮臣亦詣門稱賀，如上臺之儀。

translations.literal: On a separate day present the ceremonial gifts; palace officers too should go to the gate to offer congratulations, as in the upper-terrace ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On another day present the formal gifts; palace staff should likewise come to the gate to congratulate, as at the upper terrace.

sentences.zh: 旣冠之後，尅日謁廟，以弘尊祖之義。

translations.literal: After the capping, set a day to visit the temple, to extend the meaning of honoring ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: After the capping, fix a day to visit the ancestral temple and so fulfill the duty of honoring forebears.

sentences.zh: 此旣大典，宜通關八座丞郎幷下二學詳議。

translations.literal: This being a great ceremony, it should be circulated to the eight chief ministers, their assistants and directors, and the two academies for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: As this is a major rite, it should be sent to the eight chief ministers, their assistants and directors, and the two academies for full debate.

sentences.zh: 」僕射王奐等十四人議竝同，并撰立贊冠醮酒二辭。

translations.literal: 」Vice Director Wang Huan and fourteen others deliberated and all agreed, and together drafted the two texts for assisting the capping and the libation wine.
translations.idiomatic: 」Vice Director Wang Huan and fourteen others debated and were unanimous, and jointly composed the two texts for assisting the capping and for the libation wine.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict: 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 祝辭曰：「皇帝使給事中、太常、武安侯蕭惠基加南郡王冠。

translations.literal: The blessing text says: 「The emperor sends Palace Attendant, Director of Grand Ceremonial, Marquis of Wu'an Xiao Huiji to cap the Prince of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The invocatory text runs: 「The emperor sends Palace Attendant and Director of Grand Ceremonial, Marquis of Wu'an Xiao Huiji, to cap the Prince of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」祝曰：「筮日筮賔，肇加元服。

translations.literal: 」The blessing says: 「On the day divined and the guest divined, begin the first cap.
translations.idiomatic: 」The blessing says: 「Having divined the day and the guest, we begin the first cap.

sentences.zh: 弃爾幼志，從厥成德。

translations.literal: Put aside your youthful aims; follow your completed virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lay down your boyish will; take up your formed virtue.

sentences.zh: 親賢使能，克隆景福。

translations.literal: Draw near the worthy and employ the able; may you greatly receive bright blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Honor the worthy and use the capable; may you receive abundant fortune.

sentences.zh: 」醮酒辭曰：「旨酒旣清，嘉薦旣盈。

translations.literal: 」The libation-wine text says: 「Fine wine is already clear; fine offerings are already full.
translations.idiomatic: 」The libation-wine text says: 「The good wine is clear; the fine offerings are heaped.

sentences.zh: 兄弟具在，淑慎儀形。

translations.literal: Brothers are all present; be good and careful in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Your brothers are all here; be virtuous and careful in your bearing.

sentences.zh: 永屆眉壽，於穆斯寧。」

translations.literal: May you reach eyebrow-length old age; in this may you find peace.」
translations.idiomatic: May you live to hoary age; in this find lasting calm.」

sentences.zh: 永明中，世祖以婚禮奢費，敕諸王納妃，上御及六宮依禮止棗栗腶脩，加以香澤花粉，其餘衣物皆停。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, the Emperor, finding wedding rites extravagant, ordered that when princes took brides, the emperor and empress and the six palaces should by ritual give only dates, chestnuts, minced meat, and dried meat, with scented ointment and face powder added; all other clothing and goods were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, Emperor Wu found wedding rites wasteful and ordered that when princes married, the emperor, empress, and six palaces should send only the ritual gifts of dates, chestnuts, minced meat, and dried strips, plus scented unguent and face powder; all other garments and goods were cut.

sentences.zh: 唯公主降嬪，則止遺舅姑也。

translations.literal: Only when a princess married a consort did they stop at gifts to the parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a princess wed a consort were gifts limited to those for her husband's parents.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，尚書令徐孝嗣議曰：「夫人倫之始，莫重冠婚，所以尊表成德，結歡兩姓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi argued: 「The beginning of human relations lies above all in capping and marriage, whereby one honors and displays completed virtue and joins two clans in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1, Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi argued: 「Human order begins with capping and marriage—the rites that display full virtue and bind two families.

sentences.zh: 年代汙隆，古今殊則，繁簡之儀，因時或異。

translations.literal: Ages rise and fall; ancient and modern differ in rule; the complexity or simplicity of ceremony shifts with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Times wax and wane; ancient and modern norms diverge; ritual may be elaborate or spare according to the age.

sentences.zh: 三加廢於士庶，六禮限於天朝，雖因習未久，事難頓改，而大典之要，深宜損益。

translations.literal: The three additions have been abandoned among commoners and gentry; the six rites are confined to the celestial court—though the custom is not old and sudden change is hard, the essentials of great ceremony should be deeply trimmed or enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: The three additions are gone among commoners; the six rites belong only to the court. Custom is young and wholesale change difficult, yet the heart of great ritual should be revised with care.

sentences.zh: 案《士冠禮》，三加畢，乃醴冠者，醴則唯一而已，故醴辭無二。

translations.literal: Examining the Capping Rite for Commoners: when the three additions are finished, then one offers sweet wine to the capped man—sweet wine is only once, hence there is only one sweet-wine text.
translations.idiomatic: The Capping Rite for Commoners: after three additions one offers sweet wine to the capped man—and sweet wine is offered only once, so there is but one sweet-wine blessing.

sentences.zh: 若不醴，則每加輙醮以酒，故醮辭有三。

translations.literal: If there is no sweet wine, then at each addition one offers libation wine, hence there are three libation texts.
translations.idiomatic: Without sweet wine, each addition is followed by libation wine—hence three libation texts.

sentences.zh: 王肅云『醴本古，其禮重，酒用時味，其禮輕故也』。

translations.literal: Wang Su said, 『Sweet wine is originally ancient; its rite is weighty; wine uses the flavor of the season—its rite is light for that reason.』
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said, 『Sweet wine is archaic and its rite heavy; wine of the season is lighter by nature.』

sentences.zh: 或醴或醮，二三之義，詳記於經文。

translations.literal: Whether sweet wine or libation, the meaning of two or three is set out in detail in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet wine or libation, the logic of two versus three is spelled out in the canon.

sentences.zh: 今皇王冠畢，一酌而已，卽可擬古設醴。

translations.literal: Today when imperial princes finish capping, one pouring suffices—one may model antiquity and use sweet wine.
translations.idiomatic: Today princes of the blood complete capping with a single pouring—we could follow antiquity and use sweet wine.

sentences.zh: 而猶用醮辭，寔爲乖衷。

translations.literal: Yet libation texts are still used—this is truly at odds with the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we still employ libation texts—that is a real departure from the meaning.

sentences.zh: 尋婚禮實篚以四爵，加以合巹，旣崇尚質之理，又象泮合之義。

translations.literal: Considering the marriage rite: the basket of fruits holds four goblets, with the joined gourds added—honoring simplicity in principle and imaging the union at the school pond.
translations.idiomatic: In the marriage rites, the fruit basket bears four goblets and the joined gourds—honoring plain substance and symbolizing union at the pond.

sentences.zh: 故三飯卒食，再酳用巹。

translations.literal: Hence three portions of food and finishing the meal, then a second rinsing with the gourd.
translations.idiomatic: Hence three servings of food, the meal finished, then a second mouth-rinsing with the nuptial cup.

sentences.zh: 先儒以禮成好合，事終於三，然後用巹合。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars held that when the rite is complete and the union made, the matter ends at three—only then use the joined gourds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that the union is sealed when the rite reaches three—only then the joined cups.

sentences.zh: 儀注先酳巹，以再以三，有違旨趣。

translations.literal: The protocol rinses with the gourd first, making the second before the third—this violates the point.
translations.idiomatic: Current protocol rinses with the gourd before the second and third portions—against the true sequence.

sentences.zh: 又《郊特牲》曰『三王作牢用陶匏』。

translations.literal: Again, the Record of Suburban Sacrifice says, 『The Three Kings made the joint pen and used pottery and gourd.』
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Record of Suburban Sacrifice says, 『The Three Kings instituted the joint pen and used earthenware and gourd.』

sentences.zh: 言太古之時，無共牢之禮，三王作之，而用太古之器，重夫婦之始也。

translations.literal: It means that in utmost antiquity there was no rite of the joint pen; the Three Kings instituted it and used utensils of utmost antiquity—to give weight to the beginning of husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: In deepest antiquity there was no shared pen; the Three Kings created the rite and used the oldest vessels—to honor the start of marriage.

sentences.zh: 今雖以方樏示約，而彌乖昔典。

translations.literal: Today, though a square box shows restraint, it departs all the more from the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Today a square box may signal moderation, yet it strays further from ancient statute.

sentences.zh: 又連巹以鏁，蓋出近俗。

translations.literal: Again, chaining the nuptial cups with a lock—this surely comes from recent custom.
translations.idiomatic: Chaining the nuptial cups with a lock is plainly a recent vulgarity.

sentences.zh: 復別有牢燭，雕費采飾，亦虧曩制。

translations.literal: Again there are separate wedding candles, carved at great cost and adorned in colors—this too diminishes former regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Separate wedding candles, carved and gilded at great expense, likewise betray the old rule.

sentences.zh: 方今聖政日隆，聲教惟穆，則古昔以敦風，存餼羊以愛禮，沿襲之規，有切治要，嘉禮實重，宜備舊章。

translations.literal: Now sagely government rises daily and sound teaching is tranquil; then follow antiquity to nurture custom, keep the sacrificial sheep to cherish ritual—rules handed down bear on governance, and auspicious rites are weighty; the old statutes should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Today sagely rule grows daily and teaching spreads in peace; we should follow antiquity to nurture custom, keep the sacrificial sheep to honor ritual—inherited rules touch the heart of government, and auspicious rites are grave; the old statutes ought to be restored.

sentences.zh: 謂自今王侯已下冠畢一酌醴，以遵古之義。

translations.literal: Say that from now, for kings and marquises down, after capping is complete there shall be one libation of ceremonial ale, to follow the ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Let it be that from now on, for kings and marquises downward, after the capping is finished there is a single libation of ceremonial ale, in keeping with ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 醴卽用舊文，於事爲允。

translations.literal: For the ceremonial ale, use the old wording; in practice this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial ale should use the old libation text—that is acceptable in practice.

sentences.zh: 婚亦依古，以巹酌終酳之酒，竝除金銀連鏁，自餘雜器，悉用埏陶。

translations.literal: Weddings too should follow antiquity: use the nuptial gourd-cup for the wine of the final toast, and also abolish gold-and-silver linked locks; all other mixed vessels should be earthenware.
translations.idiomatic: Weddings should follow antiquity as well: the nuptial gourd-cup should pour the wine for the final toast, gold-and-silver linked locks should be removed, and all other mixed vessels should be pottery.

sentences.zh: 堂人執燭，足充焫燎，牢燭華侈，亦宜停省。

translations.literal: Hall attendants holding candles are enough for illumination; lavish stable-candles and ornate display should also be stopped and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Hall attendants with candles suffice for the lights; lavish stable-candles and ornate display should be cut back as well.

sentences.zh: 庶斲雕可期，移俗有漸。

translations.literal: Then carving and ornament may be expected to cease, and changing custom may proceed by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then extravagant carving may be expected to end, and custom may shift by degrees.

sentences.zh: 」參議竝同。

translations.literal: 」The joint deliberation agreed throughout.
translations.idiomatic: 」The joint deliberation unanimously approved.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 漢末，蔡邕立漢《朝會志》，竟不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Cai Yong drafted the Han Court Assembly Chronicle, but in the end it was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Cai Yong began the Han Court Assembly Chronicle, but never finished it.

sentences.zh: 秦人以十月旦爲歲首，漢初習以大饗會，後用夏正，饗會猶未廢十月旦會也。

translations.literal: The people of Qin took the first day of the tenth month as the year's start; early Han was accustomed to a great feast assembly; later they adopted the Xia calendar's first month, yet the feast assembly still did not abolish the first-day-of-the-tenth-month assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Qin took the first day of the tenth month as New Year; early Han kept the great feast on that day; after adopting the Xia calendar's first month, the tenth-month assembly was still not dropped.

sentences.zh: 東京以後，正旦夜漏未盡七刻，鳴鍾受賀，公侯以下執贄來庭，二千石以上升殿稱萬歲，然後作樂宴饗。

translations.literal: After the Eastern Capital, on New Year's dawn, before the night clepsydra had run seven units, bells sounded and congratulations were received; dukes and marquises down bore gifts and came to court; those of two thousand dan and above ascended the hall and hailed ten thousand years; then music was played and a banquet feast held.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Capital, on New Year's dawn, before the night clepsydra had run seven units, bells rang and congratulations were received; dukes and marquises down brought gifts to court; officials of two thousand dan and above ascended the hall and hailed ten thousand years; then music was played and a banquet held.

sentences.zh: 張衡賦云「皇輿夙駕，登天光於扶桑」。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's rhapsody says, 「The imperial carriage sets out early and mounts heaven's light at Fusang.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's rhapsody says, 「The imperial carriage sets out early and mounts heaven's light at Fusang.」

sentences.zh: 然則雖云夙駕，必辨色而行事矣。

translations.literal: Thus though it says "early setting out," affairs must wait until colors can be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus although it speaks of setting out early, business had to wait until dawn could be told.

sentences.zh: 魏武都鄴，正會文昌殿，用漢儀，又設百華燈。

translations.literal: Wei Wu made Ye his capital; the New Year assembly was at Wenchang Hall, using Han protocol, and a hundred flower-lamps were also set out.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao made Ye his capital; the New Year assembly was held in Wenchang Hall by Han rite, with a hundred flower-lamps set out besides.

sentences.zh: 後魏文修洛陽宮室，權都許昌，宮殿狹小，元日於城南立氈殿，青帷以爲門，設樂饗會。

translations.literal: Later Wei Wen repaired the Luoyang palaces but was provisionally at Xuchang; the palaces were cramped, so on New Year's day a felt hall was erected south of the city, with green curtains for a gate, and music and a feast assembly were set.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Pi repaired the Luoyang palaces but was provisionally at Xuchang; the halls were cramped, so on New Year's day a felt pavilion was raised south of the city, green curtains serving as its gate, with music and a feast.

sentences.zh: 後還洛陽，依漢舊事。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Luoyang and followed Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to Luoyang and followed Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝初，更定朝會儀，夜漏未盡十刻，庭燎起火，羣臣集。

translations.literal: At the start of Jin Wudi's reign the court-assembly protocol was revised: before the night clepsydra had run ten units, courtyard torches were lit and the ministers gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Wudi's reign the court-assembly rite was revised: before the night clepsydra had run ten units, courtyard torches were lit and the ministers assembled.

sentences.zh: 傅玄《朝會賦》云「華燈若乎火樹，熾百枝之煌煌』。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's Rhapsody on the Court Assembly says, 「Splendid lamps like a fire-tree, blazing with the glory of a hundred branches.」
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's Rhapsody on the Court Assembly says, 「Splendid lamps like a fire-tree, blazing with the glory of a hundred branches.」

sentences.zh: 此則因魏儀與庭燎竝設也。

translations.literal: This followed Wei protocol, with courtyard torches set out as well.
translations.idiomatic: This followed Wei practice, with courtyard torches set out together.

sentences.zh: 漏未盡七刻，羣臣入白賀，未盡五刻，就本位，至漏盡，皇帝出前殿，百官上賀，如漢儀。

translations.literal: Before the clepsydra had run seven units, the ministers entered to announce congratulations; before five units they took their places; when the clepsydra ran out, the emperor came forth to the front hall and the officials ascended to congratulate, as in Han protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Before seven units on the clepsydra, ministers entered to announce congratulations; before five they took their places; when the clepsydra ran out, the emperor came to the front hall and officials ascended to congratulate, as in Han rite.

sentences.zh: 禮畢罷入，羣臣坐，謂之辰賀。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished they withdrew; the ministers sat—this was called the morning congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended they withdrew and the ministers sat—this was called the morning congratulations.

sentences.zh: 晝漏上三刻更出，百官奉壽酒，大饗作樂，謂之晝會。

translations.literal: At three units on the day clepsydra he came forth again; the officials offered longevity wine, a great feast was held, and music was played—this was called the day assembly.
translations.idiomatic: At three units on the day clepsydra he came forth again; officials offered longevity wine, a great feast was held with music—this was called the day assembly.

sentences.zh: 別置女樂三十人於黃帳外，奏《房中之歌》。

translations.literal: Thirty female musicians were separately placed outside the yellow tent to perform the "Songs from Within the Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty female musicians were set apart outside the yellow tent to perform the "Songs from Within the Chamber."

sentences.zh: 江左多虞，不復晨賀，夜漏未盡十刻，開宣陽門，至平旦始開殿門，晝漏上五刻，皇帝乃出受賀。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi there were many troubles, and the morning congratulations were no longer held; before ten units on the night clepsydra the Xuanyang Gate was opened, and only at dawn were the hall gates opened; at five units on the day clepsydra the emperor then came forth to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the southeast there was much turmoil, and morning congratulations ceased; before ten units on the night clepsydra Xuanyang Gate was opened, hall gates only at dawn; at five units on the day clepsydra the emperor came forth to receive congratulations.

sentences.zh: 宋世至十刻乃受賀。

translations.literal: In the Song era congratulations were received only at ten units.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song, congratulations were not received until ten units.

sentences.zh: 其餘升降拜伏之儀，及置立后妃王公已下祠祀夕牲拜授弔祭，皆有儀注，文多不載。

translations.literal: The rest—protocol for ascending and descending, bowing and prostration, establishing empresses and consorts, sacrifices by kings and dukes down, evening victims, investiture bows, and condolence rites—all had written regulations, but most are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Other protocols—for ascending and descending, bowing and prostration, installing empresses and consorts, sacrifices by kings and dukes down, evening victims, investiture bows, and condolence rites—all had regulations, but most are omitted here for length.

sentences.zh: 三月三日曲水會，古禊祭也。

translations.literal: The third-month third-day winding-water gathering was the ancient purification (xi) sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The third-month third-day winding-water gathering was the ancient spring-purification (xi) rite.

sentences.zh: 漢《禮儀志》云「季春月上巳，官民皆絜濯於東流水上，自洗濯祓除去宿疾爲大絜」。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise on Rites and Protocol says, 「In the last month of spring, on shangsi, officials and people all bathe and cleanse on flowing water to the east, washing and purifying themselves to remove lingering illness—this is the great purification.」
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise on Rites and Protocol says, 「In the last month of spring, on shangsi, officials and people all bathe and cleanse in eastward-flowing water, washing away lingering illness—this is the great purification.」

sentences.zh: 不見東流爲何水也。

translations.literal: It does not say which eastward-flowing water is meant.
translations.idiomatic: It does not identify which eastward-flowing water is meant.

sentences.zh: 晉中朝云，卿已下至於庶民，皆褉洛水之側，事見諸《禊賦》及《夏仲御傳》也。

translations.literal: The Jin central court says that from ministers down to commoners all performed purification beside the Luo River—the matter appears in various Rhapsodies on the Purification and in the Biography of Xia Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin central court records that from ministers down to commoners all purified beside the Luo River—this appears in various Purification rhapsodies and in the Biography of Xia Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，三日，會天淵池誅張林。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, on the third day he assembled at Tianyuan Pool and executed Zhang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, on the third day he met at Tianyuan Pool and executed Zhang Lin.

sentences.zh: 懷帝亦會天淵池賦詩。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai also assembled at Tianyuan Pool to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai also met at Tianyuan Pool for poetry.

sentences.zh: 陸機云「天淵池南石溝，引御溝水，池西積石爲禊堂，跨水，流杯飲酒」。

translations.literal: Lu Ji says, 「South of Tianyuan Pool is a stone channel drawing in water from the imperial canal; west of the pool stones were piled to make a purification hall spanning the water, with floating cups for drinking wine.」
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji says, 「South of Tianyuan Pool is a stone channel fed from the imperial canal; west of the pool stones were piled into a purification hall spanning the water, with floating cups for drinking.」

sentences.zh: 亦不言曲水。

translations.literal: He too does not mention winding water.
translations.idiomatic: He too does not mention winding water.

sentences.zh: 元帝又詔罷三日弄具。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan also issued an edict abolishing the third-day play implements.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan also ordered the third-day play gear abolished.

sentences.zh: 今相承爲百戲之具，雕弄技巧，增損無常。

translations.literal: What is handed down today is the gear of the hundred acts—carved tricks and feats, added to or cut without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: What survives today is the gear of the hundred acts—carved tricks and feats, endlessly added to or trimmed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：案禊與曲水，其義參差。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Examining purification (xi) and winding water, their meanings diverge.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Purification (xi) and winding water, examined closely, do not mean the same thing.

sentences.zh: 舊言陽氣布暢，萬物訖出，姑洗絜之也。

translations.literal: Older accounts say that when yang qi spreads freely and all things have fully emerged, the guxian pitch is used for purification.
translations.idiomatic: Older accounts say that when yang qi spreads freely and all things have fully emerged, the guxian month is the time for purification.

sentences.zh: 巳者祉也，言祈介祉也。

translations.literal: Si means blessing—meaning to pray for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Si means blessing—that is, to pray for blessing.

sentences.zh: 一說，三月三日，清明之節，將脩事於水側，禱祀以祈豐年。

translations.literal: One theory holds that the third month third day is the Clear and Bright festival: rites are to be performed beside the water, with prayer and sacrifice to seek an abundant year.
translations.idiomatic: One theory holds that the third month third day is Clear and Bright: rites are performed beside the water, with prayer and sacrifice for an abundant harvest.

sentences.zh: 應劭云：「禊者，絜也，言自絜濯也。

translations.literal: Ying Shao says, 「Xi means pure—that is, to wash and cleanse oneself.」
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao says, 「Xi means pure—that is, to wash and cleanse oneself.」

sentences.zh: 或云漢世有郭虞者，以三月上辰生二女，上巳又生一女，二日中頻生皆死，時俗以爲大忌，民人每至其日，皆適東流水祈祓自絜濯，浮酌清流，後遂爲曲水。

translations.literal: Or some say that in Han there was a Guo Yu who on the upper chen of the third month bore two daughters, and on shangsi bore another daughter; on both days births came in quick succession and all died, so custom took it as a great taboo—each year when the day came, people would go to eastward-flowing water to pray and purify themselves, float cups on the clear current, and later this became winding water.
translations.idiomatic: Others say that in Han a Guo Yu on the upper chen of the third month bore two daughters, and on shangsi bore another; children born on both days died in quick succession, so the day was held a great taboo—people went each year to eastward-flowing water to pray and purify themselves and float cups on the clear stream, and this later became the winding-water rite.

sentences.zh: 」案高后祓霸上，馬融《梁冀西第賦》云「西北戌亥，玄石承輸。

translations.literal: 」Examining Empress Gao's purification at Bashang, Ma Rong's Rhapsody on Liang Ji's Western Residence says, 「Northwest in the xu and hai quarters, dark stone receives the channel.
translations.idiomatic: 」Empress Gao purified at Bashang; Ma Rong's Rhapsody on Liang Ji's Western Residence says, 「In the northwest, xu and hai quarters, dark stone receives the channel.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟇吐寫，庚辛之域」。

translations.literal: A toad spits and pours forth in the geng and xin domain.」
translations.idiomatic: A toad spits and pours in the geng and xin domain.」

sentences.zh: 卽曲水之象也。

translations.literal: That is the image of winding water.
translations.idiomatic: That is the image of winding water.

sentences.zh: 今據禊爲曲水事，應在永壽之前已有，祓除則不容在高后之後，祈農之說，於事爲當。

translations.literal: Judging the purification as a winding-water affair, it should already have existed before Yongshou; purification cannot have begun only after Empress Gao—the theory of praying for the harvest is the more plausible.
translations.idiomatic: If we treat purification as winding water, it should predate Yongshou; the rite of cleansing cannot have begun only after Empress Gao—the agricultural-prayer explanation fits the facts better.

sentences.zh: 九月九日馬射。

translations.literal: The ninth month ninth day was horse archery.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month ninth day was horse archery.

sentences.zh: 或說云，秋金之節，講武習射，像漢立秋之禮。

translations.literal: Some say that as autumn belongs to metal, troops were drilled and archery practiced, imitating Han protocol for Establishment of Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that as autumn belongs to metal, troops were drilled and archery practiced, on the model of Han Establishment of Autumn.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：案晉中朝元會，設卧騎、倒騎、顛騎，自東華門馳往神虎門，此亦角抵雜戲之流也。

translations.literal: The historian writes: In the Jin central court's New Year assembly there were prone-riding, inverted-riding, and upside-down-riding displays, galloping from Donghua Gate to Shenhu Gate—this too belongs to the strain of wrestling and miscellaneous entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: At the Jin central court's New Year assembly there were prone, inverted, and upside-down riding stunts, galloping from Donghua Gate to Shenhu Gate—another form of wrestling and variety entertainment.

sentences.zh: 宋武爲宋公，在彭城，九日出項羽戲馬臺，至今相承，以爲舊准。

translations.literal: When Song Wu was Duke of Song, at Pengcheng on the ninth day he went out to Xiang Yu's Play-the-Horse Terrace; the practice has been handed down to this day as the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Wu was Duke of Song, at Pengcheng he went on the ninth day to Xiang Yu's Play-the-Horse Terrace—a custom handed down to this day as the old standard.
